The other four form its coset represented by $(2,35,70)$. For this representative, the second equation modulo $3$ forces $U=W=0\bmod3$, and the first then forces $T=V=0\bmod3$, contradicting primitivity. Translation by rational torsion preserves local solubility, excluding that entire coset.
The Kummer map has kernel $2E^*(\mathbb Q)$, so its image has size $2^{2+\operatorname{rank}E^*(\mathbb Q)}$ because the full two-torsion is rational. Its size is at most four; hence the rank is zero. The positive-rank necessity following (32) proves the slope exclusion at every height. This is an explicit specialization of that rank condition, with no analytic-rank assumption.

**A finite arithmetic descent on the reduced slope.** Write $r=m/n$, with $0<m<n$, $\gcd(m,n)=1$, and put $D=n^2-m^2$ and $k_0=\omega(mnD)$. The integers $m,n,D$ are pairwise coprime. Consider

$$
E^-_{m,n}:Y^2=X(X+m^2)(X+n^2).
$$

Define an $\mathbb F_2$-matrix $L(m,n)$ with a sign column $e$, columns $u_q$ for primes $q\mid m$, columns $v_q$ for $q\mid n$, and columns $w_q$ for $q\mid D$. It has $k_0+1$ columns and one row for each odd prime $p\mid mnD$, hence $k_0-1$ rows. With additive Legendre symbols, its equations are

$$
\boxed{\begin{array}{ll}
p\mid m:&
\displaystyle\sum_{q\mid n}[q/p]v_q+
\sum_{q\mid D}[q/p]w_q=0,\\[1mm]
p\mid n:&
\displaystyle[-1/p]e+\sum_{q\mid m}[q/p]u_q+
\sum_{q\mid D}[q/p]w_q=0,\\[1mm]
p\mid D,\ p\equiv1\pmod4:&
\displaystyle\sum_{q\mid m}[q/p]u_q+
\sum_{q\mid n}[q/p]v_q=0,\\[1mm]
p\mid D,\ p\equiv3\pmod4:&
\displaystyle w_p+(v_p(D)\bmod2)
\left(e+\sum_{q\mid m}[q/p]u_q+
\sum_{q\mid n}[q/p]v_q\right)=0 .
\end{array}}
\tag{U-SLOPE-L}
$$

The prime 2 is retained as a column when present and supplies no row. Then

$$
\boxed{\operatorname{rank}E^-_{m,n}(\mathbb Q)
\le\dim\ker L(m,n)-2.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-R}
$$

Thus positive rank requires $\dim\ker L\ge3$, or equivalently $\operatorname{rank}L\le k_0-2$: the rows must have a nontrivial dependence.

Here is a complete local justification. The Kummer map in root order $0,-m^2,-n^2$ injects $E^-_{m,n}(\mathbb Q)/2E^-_{m,n}(\mathbb Q)$ into squareclass triples. The support, product, and real-sign conditions give precisely the form

$$
([a],[b],[c])=([\varepsilon uv],[\varepsilon uw],[vw]),
\quad \varepsilon=(-1)^e,\quad
u\mid\operatorname{rad}m,\ v\mid\operatorname{rad}n,\
w\mid\operatorname{rad}D,
\tag{U-SLOPE-K}
$$

with positive squarefree $u,v,w$. A coordinate's odd valuation must occur at a prime dividing a corresponding root difference; rational abscissa denominators are squares. This proves the support assertion, including its dyadic part.

At an odd $p\mid m$, $X+n^2$ is locally square. For $v_p(X)<0$ all three classes are square; for $v_p(X)>0$ the assertion follows from $X+n^2\equiv n^2$; for $v_p(X)=0$ the ratio $(X+m^2)/X$ is square, so the square product forces the third class to be square. This proves the first row; the second follows in the same way at $p\mid n$.

At $p\mid D$, away from $X=-m^2\bmod p$, the first class is square and the other two valuations are even. Near that collision, $X$ has class $[-1]$. For $p\equiv1\bmod4$ this proves the third row. For $p\equiv3\bmod4$, write $A=X+m^2$, $B=A+D$, and $f=v_p(D)$. The two valuations have equal parity. They cannot both be less than $f$, since then $B/A$ and $AB$ would be squares, contrary to the nonsquare class of $X$. Their common parity is therefore $f\bmod2$. This proves the fourth row. The branch-point Kummer values obey the same rules by their limiting definitions.

At each bad odd prime the valuation-supported ambient local classes have three bits, and the displayed single equation leaves exactly four classes. This is the entire local Kummer image: $E(\mathbb Q_p)/2E(\mathbb Q_p)$ has order four because multiplication by two is an isomorphism on the formal pro-$p$ subgroup, and full rational two-torsion determines the kernel and cokernel on the finite quotient. At good odd primes all four unramified product-one triples occur. Consequently (U-SLOPE-L) is the complete odd-prime part of the descent. In particular, the rational Kummer image lies in $\ker L$ and has size $2^{2+\operatorname{rank}E^-}$, proving (U-SLOPE-R).

**The dyadic condition has an explicit finite stopping depth.** For each vector of $\ker L$, use the signed squarefree representatives $a,b,c$ from (U-SLOPE-K). Let $S_k(m,n)$ retain those vectors for which

$$
aU^2+m^2T^2=bV^2,\qquad
aU^2+n^2T^2=cW^2
\pmod{2^k}
\tag{U-SLOPE-2}
$$

has a solution with at least one of $U,V,W,T$ odd. Then

$$
\boxed{
k_*(m,n)=4v_2(mnD)+5,\qquad
S_{k_*}(m,n)\simeq\operatorname{Sel}_2(E^-_{m,n}/\mathbb Q).}
\tag{U-SLOPE-SEL}
$$

Thus positive rank requires $\#S_{k_*}(m,n)\ge8$. A smaller-depth test $\#S_k\ge8$ is still necessary; only the stated stopping depth is asserted complete.

For the stopping proof put $h=2+2v_2(mnD)$, and let $F_1,F_2$ be the two homogeneous equations with right sides subtracted. At a primitive solution modulo $2^{2h+1}$ their Jacobian columns are

$$
(2aU,2aU),\quad(-2bV,0),\quad
(0,-2cW),\quad(2m^2T,2n^2T).
$$

If $T$ is odd, at least one of $aU^2,bV^2,cW^2$ is odd. Accordingly a minor on $UT,VT,WT$ has valuation respectively $2+v_2(D)$, $2+2v_2(n)$, or $2+2v_2(m)$, at most $h$. If $T$ is even, an odd coordinate among $U,V,W$ cannot have an even coefficient: reduction modulo 4 would force all three squarefree coefficients $a,b,c$ to be even, although their square product permits only zero or two even factors. Hence all three terms are odd and the $UV$ minor has valuation 2. Fixing the other two variables, multivariable Hensel lifting applies because the residual valuation is greater than twice the chosen determinant valuation. The corrections preserve primitivity. This proves exact dyadic solubility at $k_*$; the odd-prime and real conditions already proved then give (U-SLOPE-SEL).

These are finite integer and finite-field equations, not an assumed elliptic-rank computation. Passing is necessary only: Tate–Shafarevich classes can enlarge the Selmer group without supplying rational points.

**All six pair curves impose this descent simultaneously.** The 2-isogeny at $(0,0)$ on $E_{a,b}:Y^2=X(X-a^2)(X-b^2)$ has target

$$
Y^2=X\bigl(X+(a+b)^2\bigr)\bigl(X+(a-b)^2\bigr),
$$

which scales to $E^-_\kappa$ for $\kappa=|a-b|/(a+b)$. Applying this to all pairs in $\{1,r,1+r,1-r\}$ gives

$$
\boxed{\mathcal K(r)=
\left\{\frac{1-r}{1+r},\frac{r}{2+r},\frac{r}{2-r},
\frac1{1+2r},|1-2r|,r\right\}.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-SIX}
$$

For every $\kappa=m_\kappa/n_\kappa$ in lowest terms, the same candidate must satisfy

$$
\boxed{\bigwedge_{\kappa\in\mathcal K(r)}
\#S_{\,4v_2(m_\kappa n_\kappa(n_\kappa^2-m_\kappa^2))+5}
(m_\kappa,n_\kappa)\ge8.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-ALL}
$$

The cheaper projection requires a row dependence in every $L(m_\kappa,n_\kappa)$. Repeated transforms impose the same condition once; $r=1/2$ is already excluded.

For example, $L(1,6)$, with columns $(e,v_2,v_3,w_5,w_7)$, has independent rows $(1,0,0,1,0)$, $(0,1,1,0,0)$, and $(1,0,1,0,1)$. Its nullity two recovers (U-SLOPE6) using only odd-prime symbols. Taking inverse images of this rank-zero negative twist under (U-SLOPE-SIX) yields

$$
\boxed{r\notin
\left\{\frac16,\frac27,\frac25,\frac5{12},
\frac7{12},\frac57\right\}.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-Z}
$$

The fourth transform has no admissible inverse image of $1/6$, while the absolute-value transform has two. The inverse images of $\kappa=1/2$ are exactly the five four-square-progression slopes in (18); $\kappa=0$ occurs only at $r=1/2$. This inverse-image rule requires a certified rank-zero negative twist at its target. It cannot be iterated merely because an original magic-square slope is forbidden.

**The additive and triple factors complete the finite slope system.** For coprime positive integers $a\ne b$, put $c=a+b$ and

$$
E^{\rm add}_{a,b}:\quad y^2=x(x+A)(x+B),\qquad
A=b^3(2a+b),\quad B=a^3(a+2b).
\tag{U-SLOPE-C1}
$$

The cubic $v^2=(1-a^2\tau)(1-b^2\tau)(1-c^2\tau)$ is isomorphic to this model by

$$
x=a^2b^2(1-c^2\tau),\qquad y=a^2b^2c^2v.
\tag{U-SLOPE-C2}
$$

Its point $\tau=0,v=1$ maps to $P_0=(a^2b^2,a^2b^2c^2)$.
The tangent slope at $P_0$ is $a^2+ab+b^2$, and doubling gives $2P_0=-P_0$. Thus $P_0$ has order three. Full rational two-torsion and Mazur's theorem give exactly $E^{\rm add}_{a,b}(\mathbb Q)_{\rm tors}\simeq C_2\times C_6$.

If the three factors $1-a^2\tau,1-b^2\tau,1-c^2\tau$ are nonzero rational squares, then $x,x+A,x+B$ are squares, so the image belongs to $2E^{\rm add}_{a,b}(\mathbb Q)$. The torsion in this doubled subgroup is precisely $\{O,P_0,-P_0\}$. An affine image at $\tau\ne0$ is none of these and is nontorsion.

For a reduced magic-square slope $r=m/n$, both

$$
E^{\rm add}_{n,m},\qquad E^{\rm add}_{n-m,m}
\tag{U-SLOPE-C3}
$$

therefore have positive rational rank. The parameter in (U-SLOPE-C2) is this article's $s^2/n^2>0$.

Since $B-A=(a-b)(a+b)^3$, their combined discriminant support adds no primes to

$$
S_r=\{p:p\mid2mn(n^2-m^2)(4n^2-m^2)(n^2-4m^2)\}.
\tag{U-SLOPE-C4}
$$

### 9.39. Complete finite descent for an integer model

The following applies to any $0<A<B$; swap the two if necessary.
Let $V(A,B)$ be the squareclass space generated by $(-1,-1,1)$ and, for primes dividing $AB(B-A)$,

* $(p,p,1)$ if $p\mid A$;
* $(p,1,p)$ if $p\mid B$;
* $(1,p,p)$ if $p\mid B-A$ but $p\nmid A$.

If a prime divides two differences, it divides all three, and exactly two independent prime generators occur. All listed generators are independent globally.
The Kummer map $\delta(x,y)=([x],[x+A],[x+B])$ has kernel $2E(\mathbb Q)$. At its three nonzero two-torsion points its values are represented by

$$
(AB,A,B),\quad(-A,A(A-B),B-A),\quad(-B,A-B,B(B-A)).
\tag{U-SLOPE-C5}
$$

Every rational Kummer class is in $V(A,B)$: negative valuations of an elliptic abscissa are even, while an odd valuation in one coordinate must be shared by another and hence divide their root difference. Real points give either three positive coordinates or the first two negative and the third positive.

For every $p\mid2AB(B-A)$, let $L_p$ denote the local Kummer image.
Its dimension is two for odd $p$, and three for $p=2$.
The local squareclass coordinates are valuation parity and the Legendre symbol of the unit part for odd $p$, or valuation parity and the unit bits in $\langle-1,5\rangle$ for $p=2$.

The local image $L_p$ is spanned by (U-SLOPE-C5) and the Kummer classes of rational abscissas $x$ for which $x(x+A)(x+B)$ is a nonzero local square. This follows from local constancy of the Kummer map and density of $\mathbb Q$ in $\mathbb Q_p$. A finite collection is a complete spanning set precisely when its rank equals the displayed local-image dimension; a proper subspace gives no equality claim.

Define the finite matrix kernel

$$
\mathcal S(A,B)=\{v\in V(A,B):\operatorname{loc}_p(v)\in L_p
\text{ for every }p\mid2AB(B-A)\}.
\tag{U-SLOPE-C6}
$$

The real condition is built into $V$; at all remaining primes the classes are unramified and the curve has good odd reduction. Consequently

$$
\mathcal S(A,B)\simeq\operatorname{Sel}_2(E/\mathbb Q),\qquad
\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)\le\dim\mathcal S(A,B)-2.
\tag{U-SLOPE-C7}
$$

There is no analytic-rank assumption, point-height cutoff or conjecture on Tate--Shafarevich groups.

The standard local-dimension and certified-local-generation facts are explicit in Michael Stoll, *Descent on elliptic curves*, arXiv:math/0611694, printed p. 20; the Selmer injection and rank bound are in Sections 1.1 and 1.3. Primary source: <https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0611694>.

### 9.40. Unified eight-curve condition

Retain all six conditions (U-SLOPE-ALL), and additionally require

$$
\boxed{\begin{split}
\dim\mathcal S(m^3(2n+m),n^3(n+2m))&\ge3,\\
\dim\mathcal S(m^3(2n-m),(n-m)^3(n+m))&\ge3.
\end{split}}
\tag{U-SLOPE-ADD}
$$

Each pair is reordered increasingly. The excluded degeneracy is $r=1/2$. All eight tests use the support (U-SLOPE-C4).
Passing is necessary only: ranks may be smaller than their Selmer upper bounds, and positive ranks do not supply compatible points.

### 9.41. A rank-zero certificate at $r=9/17$

The plus model is

$$
y^2=x(x+31347)(x+171955),
$$

with $A=3^6\cdot43$, $B=5\cdot7\cdot17^3$, $B-A=2^6\cdot13^3$.
Use ordered bits $(e,t_2,t_3,t_5,t_7,t_{13},t_{17},t_{43})$, corresponding respectively to

$$
(-1,-1,1),(1,2,2),(3,3,1),(5,1,5),(7,1,7),(1,13,13),(17,1,17),(43,43,1).
$$

Six independent necessary local equations are

$$
\begin{array}{c|l}
p&\text{equation}\\ \hline
2&e+t_3+t_7+t_{43}=0\\
2&t_2=0\\
3&t_2+t_5+t_{17}=0\\
7&e+t_3+t_{13}=0\\
13&t_5+t_7=0\\
17&t_3=0.
\end{array}
\tag{U-SLOPE-C9}
$$

They leave exactly two free bits:

$$
t_2=t_3=0,\quad t_7=t_{17}=t_5,\quad e=t_{13},\quad
t_{43}=t_{13}+t_5.
$$

The rational Kummer image has size at most four, and has size $2^{2+\operatorname{rank}E(\mathbb Q)}$. Thus the rank is zero.

Here is a finite local certificate. Encode the first two local squareclasses in an integer, least-significant bit first: for odd $p$, $(v_p(x),\chi_p(x),v_p(x+A),\chi_p(x+A))$; for 2, $(v_2(x),[-1](x),[5](x),v_2(x+A),[-1](x+A),[5](x+A))$. All valuations are modulo two and unit bits use the unit part. Put $T_0=(0,0)$, $T_A=(-A,0)$.

| $p$ | Basis of $L_p$, integer encoding | Witnesses generating the span |
|---|---|---|
| 2 | $48,4,16$ | $T_0,T_A,x=1$ |
| 3 | $10,5$ | $T_A,x=3$ |
| 7 | $1,2$ | $T_0,T_A$ |
| 13 | $4,8$ | $T_A,x=1$ |
| 17 | $1,2$ | $T_0,x=3$ |

The basis entries may be row reductions of the raw signatures.
For $x=1$ the factors are $(1,31348,171956)$, and for $x=3$ they are $(3,31350,171958)$. Their products pass the exact local square criteria at the specified primes. The basis dimensions certify the full local images, and evaluating the eight global generators yields (U-SLOPE-C9). Conditions at 5 and 43 are unnecessary for this upper bound.

Therefore $\boxed{r\ne9/17}$ at every height.

### 9.42. Four additional factor-rank alternatives

The same finite descent evaluates the four $F$-factor alternatives already in this article. For each three-element subset $I$ of the labeled coefficients $(n,m,n+m,n-m)$, sort its values $a<b<c$, and put

$$
q_I=\dim\mathcal S(c^2-b^2,c^2-a^2)-2,\qquad\epsilon_I=\min(1,q_I).
$$

The substitution $x=X-c^2$ gives the required model. Existing torsion alternatives imply

$$
\boxed{\sum_{|I|=3}\epsilon_I\ge2,\qquad
\epsilon_{\{n,m,n+m\}}+\epsilon_{\{n,m,n-m\}}\ge1.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-F}
$$

Thus twelve elliptic factors are evaluated over the same support.

At this slope the six pair-curve transforms are $63/143,20/123,20/83,103/183,23/103,40/103$. Each and both additive models have two-Selmer dimension three by (U-SLOPE-C6), so this exclusion strictly strengthens those eight finite tests. These exact finite calculations assert neither that all eight actual ranks are one nor a density statement.

**The boundary factors supply the common arithmetic support.** Before reducing the six fractions, the triples $(M,N,N^2-M^2)$ are

$$
\begin{gathered}
(n-m,n+m,4mn),\quad(m,2n+m,4n(n+m)),\\
(m,2n-m,4n(n-m)),\quad(n,n+2m,4m(n+m)),\\
(|n-2m|,n,4m(n-m)),\quad(m,n,(n-m)(n+m)).
\end{gathered}
$$

Each reduction cancels at most a factor two. All six descents are therefore supported on

$$
\boxed{
\{p:p\mid2mn(n^2-m^2)(4n^2-m^2)(n^2-4m^2)\}.}
\tag{U-SLOPE-SUP}
$$

The eight linear factors are exactly the slope versions of the coincidence factors $\alpha,\beta,\alpha\pm\beta,2\alpha\pm\beta,\alpha\pm2\beta$. Their support is finite for each slope and varies globally; no bounded global prime support is implied.

The offset squareclasses also occur directly in this descent. With $x=hn,y=hm$, the torsion points $(-m^2,0)$ and $(mn,mn(m+n))$ on $E^-_{m,n}$ have respective Kummer classes

$$
\boxed{
([-1],[-d_3d_4],[d_3d_4]),\qquad
([d_1d_2],[d_2d_3],[d_1d_3]).}
\tag{U-SLOPE-CLASS}
$$

The second class can vanish when the order-four point has a rational half; the cardinality criterion does not assume these two classes form a basis.

For a uniform specialization, let $h_j$ count distinct primes $q\equiv1\bmod4$ dividing $2^{2j}-1$. Then

$$
\boxed{\dim\ker L(1,2^j)=
\begin{cases}2+h_j&j\text{ odd},\\1+h_j&j\text{ even}.
\end{cases}}
\tag{U-SLOPE-POW}
$$

Every $3\bmod4$ row solves its own $w_q$. The other rows involve only $v_2$: for odd $j$, $2^j=\pm1\bmod q$ makes $(2/q)=1$, whereas for even $j$ the prime 5 supplies the equation $v_2=0$. Thus any odd $j$ whose $2^{2j}-1$ has only prime factors $3\bmod4$ excludes $r=2^{-j}$ and its inverse images under (U-SLOPE-SIX). The factorizations $2^6-1=3^2\cdot7$, $2^{10}-1=3\cdot11\cdot31$, and $2^{14}-1=3\cdot43\cdot127$ certify $1/8,1/32,1/128$. Infinitely many qualifying exponents are not established.

The combined system evaluates the six pair ranks, two additive ranks and four triple-factor alternatives over one common prime support. It removes whole slope loci from a candidate envelope without imposing a height bound. It neither improves the established global counting exponent nor decides the full surface.

There is also a conditional exclusion: if $J(\mathcal G_r)(\mathbb Q)$ has rank zero and torsion exponent dividing $8$, (28) has no admissible non-Weierstrass solution. Such a curve point cannot have order $3$ or $4$; its half cannot lie on the theta divisor. A valid half must therefore be treated as a degree-two divisor class, not another individual curve point.

**The genus-two factor supplies a further global slope test.** Put

$$
J_r=J(\mathcal G_r),\qquad
\mathcal G_r:\quad Y^2=X(X-r^2)(X-(1-r)^2)(X-1)(X-(1+r)^2).
$$

For every $0<r<1$, $r\ne1/2$,

$$
\boxed{J_r(\mathbb Q)[2^\infty]=J_r[2]\simeq C_2^4.}
\tag{U-J-2TORS}
$$

This is a statement about the whole Jacobian, including degree-two divisor classes.

Here is a proof. Order the five finite roots as $e_0<\cdots<e_4$, and put $T_i=[(e_i,0)-\infty]$. The split Kummer map has coordinates

$$
\delta(T_i)_j=
\begin{cases}[e_i-e_j],&j\ne i,\\[1mm]
[f_r'(e_i)],&j=i.
\end{cases}
$$

The two sign vectors for $i=0,1$ are $(+,-,-,-,-)$, those for $i=2,3$ are $(+,+,+,-,-)$, and $i=4$ has all signs positive. Since every nonzero element of $J_r[2]$ is one $T_i$ or one $T_i+T_j$, only

$$
T_4,\qquad T_0+T_1,\qquad T_2+T_3
$$

can be divisible by two over $\mathbb R$.

The fixed elliptic curves $E_k^-:v^2=u(u+1)(u+k^2)$, $k=2,3,4$, have rank zero. Their odd-prime descent matrices have respective columns and independent equations

$$
\begin{array}{c|c|c}
k&\text{columns}&\text{equations}\\ \hline
2&(e,v_2,w_3)&e+v_2+w_3=0\\
3&(e,v_3,w_2)&e+w_2=0\\
4&(e,v_2,w_3,w_5)&e+v_2+w_3=0,\quad v_2=0.
\end{array}
$$

Each nullity is two. Their rational points have precisely the affine abscissas $0,-1,-k^2,\pm k$: eight visible points exhaust the torsion, as reductions at $5,7$ have orders $8,8$ for $k=2,3$, and reductions at $7,11$ have orders $8,16$ for $k=4$. The curve $E^\circ:v^2=u(u-1)(u-4)$ is two-isogenous to $E_3^-$, has rank zero and only two-torsion; none of its three nonzero two-torsion points can be halved, by the root-difference square test, and its odd torsion injects into that of $E_3^-$.

The three possible Jacobian halves are excluded by the following explicit consequences of their Kummer coordinates.

| Class and range | Squares forced by halving | Contradiction |
|---|---|---|
| $T_4$, all $r$ | $r,r+2,1+2r$ | An $E_2^-$-point with $u=2r\in(0,2)$. |
| $T_0+T_1$, $r<1/2$ | $1-2r,1-r^2,1+2r$ | An $E^\circ$-point with $u=r^{-2}>4$. |
| $T_2+T_3$, $r<1/2$ | $r+2,r(1-r^2)(r+2)$ | $r(1-r^2)=v^2$ gives a rational right triangle of area one. |
| $T_0+T_1$, $r>1/2$ | $r,2r-1,r(2-r)$ | $2r-1,r,1,2-r$ are four distinct rational squares in arithmetic progression. |
| $T_2+T_3$, $r>1/2$ | $4r^2-1,4-r^2$ | An $E_4^-$-point with $u=-4r^2\in(-4,-1)$. |

The three elliptic ordinates in this table are respectively

$$
2\sqrt r\sqrt{r+2}\sqrt{1+2r},\qquad
\frac{\sqrt{1-r^2}\sqrt{1-2r}\sqrt{1+2r}}{r^3},\qquad
4r\sqrt{4r^2-1}\sqrt{4-r^2}.
$$

In the area-one case the sides are $(1-r^2)/v,2r/v,(1+r^2)/v$. The two remaining contradictions are Fermat's area-one and four-square-progression theorems. Thus $J_r[2]\cap2J_r(\mathbb Q)=0$, proving (U-J-2TORS).

For a reduced slope $r=m/n$, use the integral root set

$$
\mathcal E_r=\{0,m^2,(n-m)^2,n^2,(n+m)^2\},
\quad
\Sigma_r=\left\{p:p\mid2\prod_{e<e',\ e,e'\in\mathcal E_r}(e-e')\right\}.
$$

This is the same boundary-prime support already used by the twelve elliptic factors. Let $\mathbb Q(\Sigma_r,2)$ be generated by $-1$ and the primes in $\Sigma_r$, and let

$$
V_r=
\left\{(d_0,\ldots,d_4)\in\mathbb Q(\Sigma_r,2)^5:
\prod_i d_i=1\right\}.
$$

For each $v\in \Sigma_r\cup\{\infty\}$, let $W_{r,v}$ be the local Kummer image of $J_r(\mathbb Q_v)/2J_r(\mathbb Q_v)$. Then

$$
\boxed{\mathcal S_J(r)=
\{d\in V_r:\operatorname{loc}_v(d)\in W_{r,v}
\text{ for every }v\in \Sigma_r\cup\{\infty\}\}
\simeq\operatorname{Sel}_2(J_r/\mathbb Q).}
\tag{U-J-SEL}
$$

The local dimensions are $4$ at odd primes, $6$ at $2$, and $2$ over $\mathbb R$. Outside $\Sigma_r$, good odd reduction makes the supported classes unramified. A local span obtained from certified curve points, branch points or degree-two divisor classes is complete once it reaches the stated dimension; incomplete sampling cannot certify an upper bound. As $J_r[2]$ has dimension four,

$$
\operatorname{rank}J_r(\mathbb Q)\le\dim\mathcal S_J(r)-4.
$$

There is a uniform domain where the entire rational torsion is determined by one good reduction. For an abelian variety over $\mathbb Q_p$, reduction is injective on all torsion when $p>2$: the general sufficient hypothesis is ramification degree $e<p-1$, and here $e=1$. This is Lemma 4.3.4(b) of Laga--Schembri--Shnidman--Voight, *Rational torsion points on abelian surfaces with quaternionic multiplication*, [arXiv:2308.15193v1](https://arxiv.org/html/2308.15193v1). The lemma applies to every abelian variety and requires no quaternionic multiplication. Good reduction makes the target the finite group $J_r(\mathbb F_p)$.

Require either of the following conditions:

$$
\boxed{\begin{aligned}
&11\nmid n,\quad mn^{-1}\bmod11\in\{3,4,7,8\},\\
&\hspace{25mm}\text{or}\\
&13\nmid n,\quad mn^{-1}\bmod13\in\{5,8\}.
\end{aligned}}
\tag{U-J-GOOD}
$$

All listed residues are nonsingular. The exact Jacobian orders are $128$ for the four listed residues at $11$ and $256$ for the two listed residues at $13$. Either condition excludes all odd rational torsion, including residue-characteristic torsion. Together with (U-J-2TORS),

$$
\boxed{\text{(U-J-GOOD)}\Longrightarrow J_r(\mathbb Q)_{\rm tors}=J_r[2]\simeq C_2^4.}
\tag{U-J-TORS}
$$

The two-prime subdomain requiring a listed residue at $11$ and any nonsingular residue $3,4,5,8,9,10$ at $13$ is contained in this domain. At $13$, the other four nonsingular residues have order $160$ and are not sufficient alone for this power-of-two argument.

A magic square gives a non-Weierstrass point $P$ with $[P-\infty]\in2J_r(\mathbb Q)$. If $J_r$ had rank zero on this domain, its doubled rational group would be zero. The Abel--Jacobi map is injective on curve points, so the required $P\ne\infty$ could not exist. The further global necessary condition is therefore

$$
\boxed{\text{(U-J-GOOD)}\ \Longrightarrow\
\operatorname{rank}J_r(\mathbb Q)\ge1\
\Longrightarrow\ \dim\mathcal S_J(r)\ge5.}
\tag{U-J-RANK}
$$

It acts on infinitely many arithmetic slope classes and involves the full genus-two factor. A failed test excludes the entire slope, without any bound on center height. Passing remains necessary only. In particular, a surviving genus-two Selmer class need not give a rational point or the final compatible lift.

**Quotient heights constrain the same point.** On $\mathcal D_r$, use $j(P)=[32P-K_{\mathcal D_r}]$ and the canonical height for $2\Theta$. $$
\boxed{h\le\frac{17}{2}h_G+\frac5{24}B_r,\qquad
h\le17h_F+\frac9{16}B_r\quad\text{for each }F.}
\tag{32a}
$$

Here $M(\mathcal D_r)$ is the Arakelov constant in the cited gap inequality, not a sum of character dimensions. The averaging has an explicit rational certificate. Encode deck elements by five-bit masks $b$, whose low four bits change the signs of $u_a$ and whose last bit changes the sign of $s$. Put $\chi_a(b)=(-1)^{\operatorname{popcount}(a\mathbin{\&}b)}$. The positive-genus character masks are
$7,11,13,14,15,19,21,22,25,26,28,23,27,29,30,31$.
The genus-two target is $31$. Uniform averaging over
$7,11,13,14,19,21,22,25,26,28$
has eigenvalue $1/5$ on every other positive-genus character and $-1$ on $31$.
For an $F$ target $30$, give masks
$3,5,9,14,15,17,22,23,26,27,28,29,30$
respective integer weights
$1,1,1,2,1,1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2$, divided by $18$.
The eigenvalues are $1/9$ off the target and $-7/9$ on it; permuting the low four bits covers the other $F$ targets. Averaging
$34\langle v,bv\rangle-2h\le B_r$
therefore gives $(24h-204h_G)/5\le B_r$ and
$(16h-272h_F)/9\le B_r$, exactly (32a).
A rank-zero genus-two factor bounds $h\le5B_r/24$, independently of all other ranks; a rank-zero $F$ bounds $h\le9B_r/16$. More generally

$$
h>9B_r/16\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{rank}J(\mathcal D_r)(\mathbb Q)\ge16,
\tag{32b}
$$

because all four $F$ projections and the genus-two projection are then nontorsion. The unconditional lower bound at arbitrary height remains $13$. The constant varies with $r$; this is not a global height bound on magic squares.

The same argument applies on the **full** genus-321 fiber, so it retains every original square condition. Its 219 positive-genus character quotients are

$$
C_I:\quad w^2=\prod_{j\in I}(1+b_js),\quad
b_j\in\{\pm1,\pm r,\pm(1+r),\pm(1-r)\},\quad |I|\ge3.
$$

There are 126 genus-one, 84 genus-two and 9 genus-three factors. For $j_H(P)=[640P-K_H]$, write $h_H=\widehat h(j_H(P))$, and $h_I$ for its orthogonal character component. If $B_H\ge M(\mathcal H_r)$ is a certified nonnegative bound, then

$$
\boxed{h_H\le\frac{321}{g_I}h_I+c_{g_I}B_H,\qquad
(c_1,c_2,c_3)=\left(\frac{209}{224},\frac{59}{96},\frac{51}{112}\right).}
\tag{32c}
$$

Every coefficient is obtained by exact rational averaging over the $2$-group characters. In particular,

$$
h_H>\frac{209}{224}B_H
\Longrightarrow \operatorname{rank}J(\mathcal H_r)(\mathbb Q)\ge219.
\tag{32d}
$$

A single rank-zero character factor, or a total rank bound at most 218, therefore gives an effective fixed-slope height bound. This remains conditional on the rank/height alternative; it is not an unconditional rank-219 restriction.

**Uniform relative heights.** Let $h_0$ be the logarithmic rational height, and choose a rational branch point $W_I$ on each character curve $C_I$. Norm/pullback adjunction gives the exact normalization

$$
h_I=3200\,\widehat h_{2\Theta_I}([P_I-W_I]).
$$

For the fixed families, there are constants $C_I$ independent of both $r$ and the candidate such that

$$
\boxed{|h_I-3200g_Ih_0(s)|\le C_I(h_0(r)+1).}
\tag{32g}
$$

The proof combines $A_I^*\mathcal O(2\Theta_I)^{\otimes2} \simeq x^*\mathcal O(2g_I)$ on the generic hyperelliptic fiber, a vertical-divisor height comparison, and Call–Silverman's uniform family theorem. It concerns all points in the fibers, rather than specialization of one fixed section.

Taking the maximum of the finitely many constants yields absolute constants $B,B_D$ for this fixed family, with

$$
\boxed{\operatorname{rank}J(\mathcal H_r)(\mathbb Q)\ge219
\quad\text{or}\quad h_0(s)\le B(h_0(r)+1),}
\qquad
\boxed{\operatorname{rank}J(\mathcal D_r)(\mathbb Q)\ge16
\quad\text{or}\quad h_0(s)\le B_D(h_0(r)+1).}
\tag{32h}
$$

The low-height alternative holds if one character projection is torsion, whatever the rank of its factor. The constants are specified existentially. The conclusion is a uniform relative bound, not an absolute cutoff.

It is tied to the primitive center without height estimates: if $r=a/b$ is reduced, then

$$
\boxed{A_1^2\mid b,\quad A_2^2\mid a,\quad
A_3^2\mid(a+b),\quad A_4^2\mid(b-a),\quad
h_0(s)=2\log H_1\le2\log c\le h_0(s)+h_0(r).}
\tag{32i}
$$

Indeed $\gcd(c,\gcd(x,y))=1$, so none of these deficit squares cancels from its indicated offset. On the low-height side of (32h),

$$
\boxed{c\le e^{B/2}b^{(B+1)/2}.}
\tag{32j}
$$

The same denominator in (29g), the primitive normalization, and the relative-height bound is therefore constrained by one chain of exact identities. The slope denominator $b$ remains unbounded.

For completeness, $h_H=1{,}027{,}200h_0(s)+O(h_0(r)+1)$ and
$h_D=2176h_0(s)+O(h_0(r)+1)$; the $J(\mathcal D_r)$ component of $h_H$ is exactly $25h_D$. For the genus-five quotient the corresponding height is $80h_0(s)+O(h_0(r)+1)$. When scale dominates slope, $h_I/h_H\to g_I/321$, so the deck-averaging trace bound is saturated on the large-relative-height branch.

**A fixed K3 model with exact residual tests.** Write the root array as $(A,B,C;D,M,E;F,G,H)$ and consider the fixed surface in $\mathbb P^5$

$$
X:\quad A^2+M^2-F^2-G^2=0,\quad
B^2-2M^2+G^2=0,\quad C^2-2M^2+F^2=0.
\tag{32e}
$$

Its K3 resolution has Picard rank 19. On $M\ne0$, set $\alpha=A^2/M^2-1$, $\beta=C^2/M^2-1$. The remaining three roots exist exactly when

$$
\boxed{[1-\alpha]=[1-\alpha+\beta]=[1+\alpha-\beta]=1.}
\tag{32f}
$$

Together with the canonical sector and distinctness, this is equivalent to (U). It transfers the problem to one fixed geometric model, retaining an explicit degree-eight lifting condition. Suitable pairs of six-root projections also recover the full surface as the main component of their fiber product over the three common root coordinates; the common squared coordinates must span the magic-square linear space. Solving either projection alone loses the residual tests.

### 9.45. A certified positive-rank first-lift exclusion

Let

$$
C:\quad Y^2=\prod_{e\in E}(X-e),\qquad
E=(0,93025,509796,1038361,3003289),
$$

and let $J=\operatorname{Jac}(C)$, based at the unique point infinity. Then

$$

\{Q\in C(\mathbb Q):[Q-\infty]\in2J(\mathbb Q)\}
=\{\infty\}.}
\tag{U-J-RANKONE}
$$

Consequently the slope $r=714/1019$ is excluded at every center height. It passes all twelve evaluated elliptic rank-upper-bound tests and the positive-genus-two-rank test. This is an exclusion using actual positive Jacobian rank; it does not assert that every elliptic factor has positive actual rank.

### 9.46. Exact arithmetic inputs

The roots are the ordered numbers $0,(n-m)^2,m^2,n^2,(n+m)^2$, where $(m,n)=(714,1019)$. The supported primes for split two-descent are

$$
2,3,5,7,17,43,61,331,409,1019,1733,2447.
$$

There are $4(12+1)=52$ global squareclass columns. The complete local Kummer images have dimensions 6 at 2, 4 at every listed odd prime, and 2 over $\mathbb R$. Their inverse-image constraints have binary rank 47. Thus the two-Selmer dimension is 5, and full rational two-torsion gives

$$
\operatorname{rank}J(\mathbb Q)\le 5-4=1.
$$

These are finite dimension-certified local calculations with exact rational witnesses. The twelve elliptic upper bounds, in the established order of six pair factors, two additive factors, and four triple factors, are

$$
(1,3,2,3,2,1;\ 2,1;\ 2,1,1,2).
$$

Complete local bases and witness conventions are given in Section 14.

The exact point

$$
P=(528565,73832128430760)\in C(\mathbb Q)
$$

supplies a rational Jacobian class. Put

$$
D=8[P-\infty],\qquad
T=[(0,0)+(93025,0)-2\infty].
$$

Here $2T=0$. Exact Cantor arithmetic gives an 11-integral reduced Mumford pair $(u,v)$ for $D+T$ satisfying

$$
u\equiv X^2+24X,\qquad v\equiv11X+99\pmod{121}.
\tag{U-J714-MUMFORD}
$$

The chain $P,2P,4P,8P,T,D+T$ is determined by exact Cantor addition; the displayed congruences follow by reducing rational coefficients with denominator prime to $11$. Reduction also verifies that $[P-\infty]$ has order 8 over $\mathbb F_{11}$, hence $D$ belongs to the kernel of reduction.

### 9.47. Logarithm and the only possible residue disk

The five roots are distinct modulo 11, reducing in the displayed order to $(0,9,1,5,3)$. This is good reduction. Write

$$
\omega_0=dX/Y,\qquad \omega_1=X\,dX/Y,\qquad
\lambda_j=\log_{\omega_j}(D).
$$

The roots of $u$ Hensel-lift to two 11-adic points near the branch points at $e=0,93025$. In the branch parameter $z=Y$,

$$
X=e+z^2/f'(e)+O(z^4),\qquad
\omega_j=(2e^j/f'(e)+O(z^2))\,dz.
$$

All power-series coefficients are 11-integral. The ordinates belong to $11\mathbb Z_{11}$, and the integrated remainder has valuation at least 3: an error term of degree $k\ge3$ has valuation at least $k-v_{11}(k)\ge3$. Consequently (U-J714-MUMFORD) gives

$$
\lambda_j\equiv
2\sum_{e\in\{0,93025\}}\frac{e^jv(e)}{f'(e)}\pmod{121},
\qquad (\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\equiv(99,55)\pmod{121}.
\tag{U-J714-LOG}
$$

In this calculation $f'(0)\equiv47$, $f'(93025)\equiv111$, and $v(93025)\equiv77\pmod{121}$. The nonzero logarithm shows that $D$ is nontorsion, so the upper bound proves rank exactly one.

The exact 11-adic differential

$$
\eta=(\lambda_1/11)\omega_0-(\lambda_0/11)\omega_1
$$

annihilates $J(\mathbb Q)$ and reduces to $(5-9X)dX/Y$. It is the exact logarithm coefficients, rather than their displayed residues alone, that define the annihilator. No Mordell--Weil generator or saturation computation is needed: rank one and nontorsion of $D$ make every rational class an integral relation with $D$, up to torsion, and the logarithm kills torsion.

At infinity put $z=1/X$ and $w=Y/X^3$. The equation is

$$
w^2=z\prod_{e\in E}(1-ez),\qquad z=w^2+O(w^4).
$$

Thus $w$ is an integral uniformizer,
$\omega_0=(-2w^2+O(w^4))dw$, and
$\omega_1=(-2+O(w^2))dw$. The constant coefficient of $\eta$ is a unit. For any nonzero $w\in11\mathbb Z_{11}$, its integral has a linear term of valuation $v_{11}(w)$, while every later degree $k\ge2$ term has valuation at least
$k v_{11}(w)-v_{11}(k)>v_{11}(w)$.
It cannot vanish. Since the integral vanishes at every rational point, infinity is the only rational point in its residue disk.

It remains to determine the disk of a possible first lift. The complete affine $\mathbb F_{11}$-point list has abscissas

$$
0,1,3,4,5,6,9,10,
$$

with respectively $1,1,1,2,1,2,1,2$ ordinates. At each such point its five-coordinate split Kummer tuple has a nonsquare coordinate. The tuple is $(X-e)_{e\in E}$ at a nonbranch point; at a branch point replace the zero entry by $f'(e)$. Therefore

$$
i(C(\mathbb F_{11}))\cap 2J(\mathbb F_{11})=\{0\},
\qquad i(Q)=[Q-\infty].
$$

Reduction commutes with doubling, so every rational $Q$ with $i(Q)\in2J(\mathbb Q)$ lies in the infinity disk. The preceding zero argument proves (U-J-RANKONE).

**Transfer and scope.**

The rational isomorphism from the normalized genus-two slope model to $C$ is

$$
(X_0,Y_0)\longmapsto(n^2X_0,n^5Y_0),\qquad n=1019.
$$

It carries infinity to infinity and preserves the doubled-subgroup condition. A point of the original first cover has $X_0=s^{-2}$, where $0<s<1/(1+r)$; hence it is an affine nonbranch point and its integral-model abscissa satisfies $X>(n+m)^2$. Each of $X$ and $X-e$ is a nonzero rational square. Thus its Abel--Jacobi class lies in $2J(\mathbb Q)$, contrary to (U-J-RANKONE). This excludes the first lift itself, before the remaining common-squareclass and final branched-cover conditions.

This argument determines the rational doubled-class locus needed by the first lift. The next argument determines all rational points, including the points in other residue disks. It also does not derive empty local solubility at 11: the local infinity branch survives. The obstruction combines that finite-field disk constraint with the global rank-one logarithm direction. There is no all-slope, density, or finite-confinement conclusion.

### 9.48. Complete rational-point determination at slope $714/1019$

Let

$$
E=(0,93025,509796,1038361,3003289),\qquad
C:\ Y^2=\prod_{e\in E}(X-e),\qquad J=\operatorname{Jac}(C),
$$

and

$$
P=(528565,73832128430760),\qquad W_e=(e,0).
$$

Then the complete set of rational points is

$$
\boxed{C(\mathbb Q)=\{\infty\}\cup\{W_e:e\in E\}
\cup\{P,\iota(P)\},\qquad \iota(X,Y)=(X,-Y).}
\tag{U-J-POINTS714}
$$

In particular none is in the admissible real interval $X>3003289$, and no affine point has doubled Abel--Jacobi class. This strengthens the first-lift exclusion to an actual rational-point determination for its genus-two base, whose Jacobian has rank one.

**1. The rational reduction image has order 64.**

The preceding certificate proves $\operatorname{rank}J(\mathbb Q)=1$, with $[P-\infty]$ nontorsion. Let

$$
H=\langle[P-\infty],J[2](\mathbb Q)\rangle\subset J(\mathbb Q).
$$

The finite quotient $J(\mathbb Q)/H$ has odd order. This follows from exact rational Kummer linear algebra: the five branch classes span a four-dimensional subspace in $J(\mathbb Q)/2J(\mathbb Q)$, and the class of $P$ is independent of it. Since

$$
\dim_{\mathbb F_2}J(\mathbb Q)/2J(\mathbb Q)
=\operatorname{rank}J(\mathbb Q)+\dim_{\mathbb F_2}J(\mathbb Q)[2]=5,
$$

the image of $H$ is the entire quotient. Thus multiplication by two is surjective on the finite group $J(\mathbb Q)/H$, which makes its order odd. This argument needs no generator of the free Mordell--Weil group and no rational torsion classification.

Here the Kummer tuple for $P$ is

$$
(528565,435540,18769,-509796,-2474724).
$$

At $W_e$, its tuple has entries $e-e_j$, replacing the zero entry by $f'(e)$. The supported primes are the same twelve primes as in the rank certificate; $18769=137^2$ contributes no squareclass. Encoding the first four tuple entries proves that the 16 torsion images are distinct and the $P$ image is outside their span. The fifth entry is determined by square product.

The good reduction at 11 has

$$
\#J(\mathbb F_{11})=128,\qquad\#\overline H=64.
$$

These numbers are certified by enumerating every reduced Mumford pair $(u,v)$ with monic $u$, $\deg u\le2$, $\deg v<\deg u$, and $u\mid f-v^2$, and by generating $\overline H$ from the order-eight reduction of $P$ and the 16 rational two-torsion classes. The quotient of the rational reduction image by $\overline H$ has odd order, as it is a quotient of $J(\mathbb Q)/H$; it is also a quotient of subgroups of the 2-group $J(\mathbb F_{11})$. Hence it is trivial:

$$
\operatorname{red}_{11}J(\mathbb Q)=\overline H.
\tag{U-J714-REDUCTION}
$$

The complete affine point list modulo 11 is

$$
(0,0),(1,0),(3,0),(4,4),(4,7),(5,0),
(6,4),(6,7),(9,0),(10,2),(10,9).
$$

Exactly the four points with abscissas 6 or 10 have Abel--Jacobi classes outside $\overline H$. Equation (U-J714-REDUCTION) excludes their residue disks for every rational curve point. The remaining eight disks contain the eight displayed known rational points.

**2. Seven of these disks each contain one rational point.**

For $D=8[P-\infty]$, put

$$
\lambda_j=\log_{\omega_j}(D),\qquad
\omega_0=dX/Y,\quad\omega_1=X\,dX/Y.
$$

The rank-one certificate gives

$$
(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\equiv(99,55)\pmod{121}.
$$

The exact annihilator

$$
\eta=(\lambda_1/11)\omega_0-(\lambda_0/11)\omega_1
$$

has reduction $(5-9X)dX/Y$. Its only zero on the reduced curve is the branch point with abscissa 3, namely the reduction of $W_e$ for $e=3003289$. It is nonzero at the other seven remaining residue points, including infinity. Formal integration about the known rational point in each such disk has a unit linear term, and all later terms have larger valuation. It therefore has exactly one zero in that disk. Since the annihilator integral is zero at every rational point, each disk contains only its known point.

**3. The exceptional branch disk also contains one point.**

The certified reduced Mumford pair for
$D+[(0,0)+(93025,0)-2\infty]$ satisfies the stronger congruence

$$
u\equiv X^2+266X+121,
\qquad v\equiv858X+220\pmod{1331}.
\tag{U-J714-MUMFORD3}
$$

Both coefficients of $v$ are divisible by 11. If $\alpha$ is its Hensel-lifted abscissa near either $e=0$ or $93025$, then
$\alpha-e\in11^2\mathbb Z_{11}$, so
$v(\alpha)-v(e)\in11^3\mathbb Z_{11}$.
The local branch-coordinate integral has first omitted term of valuation at least three. Thus the same linear branch formula remains valid modulo $11^3$:

$$
\lambda_j\equiv
2\sum_{e\in\{0,93025\}}\frac{e^jv(e)}{f'(e)}\pmod{1331}.
$$

Evaluation of (U-J714-MUMFORD3) gives

$$
(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)\equiv(946,176)\pmod{1331},\qquad
\lambda_1-3003289\lambda_0\equiv121\pmod{1331}.
\tag{U-J714-LOG3}
$$

Therefore

$$
v_{11}\!\left(\frac{\lambda_1-e\lambda_0}{\lambda_0}\right)=1,
\qquad e=3003289.
\tag{U-J714-ODD}
$$

Suppose there were a rational nonbranch point $Q$ in the residue disk of $W_e$. Use $z=Y\in11\mathbb Z_{11}\setminus\{0\}$ as its local coordinate and put $a=f'(e)\in\mathbb Z_{11}^{\times}$. The integral implicit function theorem and formal integration give

$$
X-e=z^2/a+O(z^4),
$$

$$
\int_{W_e}^{Q}\omega_0=\frac{2z}{a}(1+11\mathbb Z_{11}),\qquad
\int_{W_e}^{Q}(\omega_1-e\omega_0)
=\frac{2z^3}{3a^2}(1+11\mathbb Z_{11}).
$$

The factors displayed as units are evaluated at the chosen nonzero $z$. Integration denominators do not affect the leading valuations: every subsequent term has strictly larger valuation at 11. Consequently their quotient has valuation

$$
2v_{11}(z)\ge2.
\tag{U-J714-EVEN}
$$

On the other hand $[Q-W_e]\in J(\mathbb Q)$, so its logarithm is on the rank-one line spanned by $(\lambda_0,\lambda_1)$. The first integral is nonzero, making the quotient in (U-J714-EVEN) equal to the quotient in (U-J714-ODD). Their different valuations are a contradiction. The disk therefore contains only $W_e$.

Together the eight single-point disks and the four excluded disks prove (U-J-POINTS714).

The finite computations use the explicitly specified equations, local squareclass encodings, and complete residue or coefficient domains. Arithmetic certificates are interpreted according to Section 14.

This is an all-height determination at one positive-rank slope, obtained with exact integer and rational arithmetic. It does not rely on searching for points up to a bound, on knowing a Mordell--Weil generator, or on a conjectural analytic rank. It supplies no uniform finite set of admissible slopes as the slope varies.

### 9.49. A rank-one logarithmic direction must satisfy a local square condition
Let

$$
C:Y^2=f(X)=\prod_{i=0}^4(X-e_i),\qquad e_i\in\mathbb Q,
$$

have good reduction in this monic integral model at an odd prime
$p\ge5$: all $e_i$ lie in $\mathbb Z_p$ and are pairwise distinct
modulo $p$. Let $J=\operatorname{Jac}(C)$, based at infinity, and suppose
$\operatorname{rank}J(\mathbb Q)=1$. Choose a rational nontorsion class
with nonzero logarithm, and scale its logarithmic coordinates for
$\omega_0=dX/Y$, $\omega_1=X\,dX/Y$ to a primitive vector
$(L_0,L_1)\in\mathbb Z_p^2$. No assumption that this class generates
the free group is needed.

If a rational point other than infinity lies in infinity's residue disk,
then

$$
 \boxed{L_1\in\mathbb Z_p^\times,\qquad
       \frac{3L_0}{L_1}\in\{t^2:0\ne t\in p\mathbb Z_p\}.}
 \tag{U-J-DIRECTION-INF}
$$

In particular the valuation of
$L_0$ must be a positive even integer, at least two, and its leading
unit after multiplication by $3/L_1$ must be a square. If $L_0=0$, no
such nonboundary rational point exists.

For a finite branch point $W_e=(e,0)$, a different rational point in
its residue disk similarly requires

$$
 \boxed{L_0\in\mathbb Z_p^\times,\qquad
       3f'(e)\left(\frac{L_1}{L_0}-e\right)
         \in\{t^2:0\ne t\in p\mathbb Z_p\}.}
 \tag{U-J-DIRECTION-BRANCH}
$$

If the displayed difference is zero, this disk contains only its branch
point among rational points. These are necessary conditions on the
actual rank-one Mordell--Weil direction, not on a freely selected
Selmer representative.

**Proof.** Abelian integration is additive, annihilates torsion, and
agrees with local formal integration. Since the rational group has rank
one, every rational divisor-class logarithm is proportional to
$(L_0,L_1)$. This statement holds for any nonzero rational multiple of a
generator and requires no saturation computation.

At infinity put $z=1/X$ and $w=Y/X^3$, so
$w^2=z h(z)$ with $h(z)=\prod_i(1-e_i z)$ and $h(0)=1$.
The analytic uniformizer $t=w/\sqrt{h(z)}$ is well-defined throughout
this disk by the square root congruent to one. It satisfies $z=t^2$,
and $t\in p\mathbb Z_p$. This is a local analytic parameter; no
globally rational square-root function is assumed. Put

$$
 g(t)=h(t^2)^{-1/2}=\sum_{j\ge0}a_jt^{2j},
 \qquad a_j\in\mathbb Z_p,\quad a_0=1.
$$

Then

$$
 \omega_0=-2t^2g(t)\,dt,\qquad \omega_1=-2g(t)\,dt,
$$

and for $0\ne t\in p\mathbb Z_p$ their integrals from infinity are

$$
 I_0=-\frac23t^3 V(t),\qquad I_1=-2t U(t),
 \qquad U(t),V(t)\in1+p\mathbb Z_p.
$$

Indeed

$$
 U=1+\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{a_jt^{2j}}{2j+1},\qquad
 V=1+\sum_{j\ge1}\frac{3a_jt^{2j}}{2j+3}.
$$

Writing $k=v_p(t)\ge1$, every summand after the constant has positive
valuation, since $2jk-v_p(2j+1)\ge1$ and
$2jk-v_p(2j+3)\ge1$ for $p\ge5$. This includes the denominator five
when $p=5$. The valuations tend to infinity, establishing convergence.
Consequently $I_0/I_1=(t^2/3)(V/U)$ is nonzero, has valuation $2k$,
and $V/U$ is a square unit. Proportionality to the global logarithmic
line gives (U-J-DIRECTION-INF), including primitivity of $L_1$.

At a finite branch point use $t=Y$. The integral implicit-function
expansion gives

$$
 X=e+\frac{t^2}{f'(e)}+t^4\mathbb Z_p[[t^2]],
$$

and hence

$$
 I_0=\frac{2t}{f'(e)}U_e(t),\qquad
 I_1-eI_0=\frac{2t^3}{3f'(e)^2}V_e(t),
 \qquad U_e,V_e\in1+p\mathbb Z_p.
$$

The same denominator estimates justify these unit factors. The branch
class $[W_e-\infty]$ is two-torsion, so its logarithm is zero. Thus
$I_1/I_0=L_1/L_0$ for a rational point in this disk, and

$$
 3f'(e)(L_1/L_0-e)=t^2V_e/U_e.
$$

This is exactly (U-J-DIRECTION-BRANCH). $\square$

**Use for a slope first lift.** If finite-field enumeration shows that
$i(C(\mathbb F_p))\cap2J(\mathbb F_p)=\{0\}$, all rational first-lift
points must lie in infinity's disk. Failure of (U-J-DIRECTION-INF)
therefore excludes the entire first lift. A finite precision computation
can certify failure by exhibiting a nonzero leading logarithmic term
with odd valuation, valuation below two, or a nonsquare normalized unit.
Passing the test proves neither a rational point nor a later lift. It is
a refinement of the usual nonvanishing-annihilator test: valuation one
or a higher odd valuation also excludes the nonboundary disk.

The integration input is Michael Stoll, *Arithmetic of Hyperelliptic
Curves* (2014), Theorem 6.4 and Corollary 6.5. The local square
conditions and their denominator estimates are proved above.

For the normalized slope quintic, the following are complete residue
lists for which the good-reduction curve has
$i(C(\mathbb F_p))\cap2J(\mathbb F_p)=\{0\}$:

| $p$ | Slope residues $r\pmod p$ |
|---|---|
| 11 | $3,4,7,8$ |
| 19 | $7,8,11,12$ |
| 23 | $3,8,15,20$ |
| 31 | $3,7,9,10,11,12,13,14,17,18,19,20,21,22,24,28$ |

Each row is an exhaustive finite-field calculation using the five
root-difference Kummer coordinates, including the derivative coordinate
at every branch point. Independent programs check the complete lists.
They supply disks for the conditional rank-one direction test; no
uniform rank-one assumption or slope exclusion from the residue alone
is asserted. At $714/1019$, $r\equiv7\pmod{11}$, and the actual
logarithmic direction fails (U-J-DIRECTION-INF).

The external analytic input for these arguments is the additive abelian
integration pairing, compatible with formal integration and Abel--Jacobi:
Michael Stoll, *Arithmetic of Hyperelliptic Curves* (2014), Theorem 6.4
and Corollary 6.5 [19]. The required local zero estimates and square
conditions are proved here; no black-box determination of rational
points is assumed.

### 9.50. A unique rational descent branch for a six-square family

Consider the six-square family of Bremner–Elsholtz–Ulas,
[Section 4.2](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.05459). If its independent parameter
is $t$, its three missing entries are $f_j(t)=a_0+2a_3+j a_1$,
$j=0,1,2$, in that source's degree-ten data. The following polynomial
identity fixes the correspondence without a choice of square-root signs:

$$
f_j(t)=(1-t)^{10}B_j\!\left(\frac{(1+t)^2}{(1-t)^2}\right),
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
B_0(s)&=8s^5-65s^4+104s^3-28s^2+34s-4,\\
B_1(s)&=8s^5-41s^4+68s^3-64s^2+58s-4,\\
B_2(s)&=8s^5-17s^4+32s^3-100s^2+82s-4.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-BEU-DATA}
$$

For $t\ne1$, set $z=(1+t)/(1-t)$, $s=z^2$, and
$w_j=v_j/(1-t)^5$. The missing-square equations $v_j^2=f_j(t)$ become
$w_j^2=B_j(s)$. The chart $t=1$ is excluded because all three
$f_j(1)=8192$ are nonsquares. The parameter $t=\infty$ is represented by
$z=-1$. It and $t=0$, represented by $z=1$, have repeated entries
and are inadmissible.

Write

$$
B_j(s)=(s-2)H_j(s),\qquad K(s)=s^3-6s^2-2,
$$
$$
\begin{aligned}
H_0(s)&=8s^4-49s^3+6s^2-16s+2=(8s-1)K(s),\\
H_1(s)&=8s^4-25s^3+18s^2-28s+2,\\
H_2(s)&=8s^4-s^3+30s^2-40s+2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-BEU-FACTORS}
$$

**Theorem (unique rational descent branch).** The simultaneous equations
$s=z^2$, $w_j^2=B_j(s)$, $j=0,1,2$, have a rational solution if and
only if, at the same $s$, there are rational numbers $z,r,h,V,y_1,y_2$
satisfying

$$
\boxed{z^2+r^2=2,\qquad8z^2-7h^2=1,}
\tag{U-BEU-UNIQUE-CONICS}
$$
$$
\boxed{V^2=-7K(s),\qquad y_1^2=-H_1(s),\qquad y_2^2=-H_2(s).}
\tag{U-BEU-RESIDUAL}
$$

The reconstruction is

$$
\boxed{w_0=rhV,\qquad w_1=ry_1,\qquad w_2=ry_2.}
\tag{U-BEU-RECONSTRUCT}
$$

The signs of the reconstructed roots may be chosen independently. In
particular every finite rational completion parameter obeys

$$
\boxed{t^2-6t+1\in\mathbb Q^{\times2},\qquad
(7t^2+18t+7)/7\in\mathbb Q^{\times2}.}
\tag{U-BEU-PARAMETER-SQUARES}
$$

**Proof.** Write $z=a/b$ in lowest terms, with $b>0$, and set

$$
D=a^2-2b^2,\quad E=8a^2-b^2,\quad
K_h=a^6-6a^4b^2-2b^6,\quad H_{j,h}=b^8H_j(a^2/b^2).
$$

Then $H_{0,h}=EK_h$, and $DH_{j,h}=(b^5w_j)^2$ is an integer
square. Neither $D$ nor $E$ vanishes, because 2 and 1/8 are not rational
squares. Also $K$ has no rational root: its only rational-root candidates
$\pm1,\pm2$ all fail. Thus $H_{0,h}\ne0$.

If an odd prime $p\mid D$, then $p\nmid b$, and
$H_{j,h}\equiv b^8H_j(2)\pmod p$. The three specialization values are

$$
H_0(2)=-270,\qquad H_1(2)=-54,\qquad H_2(2)=162.
$$

For $p\ne3$, at least one of these is nonzero modulo $p$, so the
corresponding square $DH_{j,h}$ forces $v_p(D)$ to be even. On the other
hand $D\equiv a^2+b^2\pmod3$ cannot vanish for a primitive pair.
Consequently the signed squarefree part of $D$ lies in
$\{1,-1,2,-2\}$.

For all three indices,
$H_{j,h}\equiv2(a^2+b^2)^4\equiv2\pmod3$. The square $DH_{j,h}$ is
nonzero modulo 3, hence $D\equiv2\pmod3$. It follows that $3\nmid ab$
and

$$
D=dR^2,\qquad d\in\{-1,2\},\quad R\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}.
\tag{U-BEU-TWO-CLASSES}
$$

Moreover $b$ is odd: if $b$ were even, $a$ would be odd and
$D\equiv1\pmod8$, incompatible both with $-R^2$ and with the even
number $2R^2$.

The integer $E$ is therefore odd. If an odd prime $p\mid E$, then
$p\nmid b$, and evaluation at $a^2/b^2=1/8$ yields

$$
512K_h\equiv-1071b^6\pmod p,\qquad1071=3^2\cdot7\cdot17.
$$

Since $DEK_h$ is a square and $D$ has class $-1$ or 2, every prime
outside $\{3,7,17\}$ has even valuation in $E$. Also
$E\equiv1\pmod3$. Hence
$E=eT^2$ with
$e\in\{\pm1,\pm7,\pm17,\pm119\}$.
The congruences $E\equiv7\pmod8$ and $E\equiv1\pmod3$ leave precisely
$e=7$ or $e=-17$.

In fact $E>0$. If $d=2$, then $s>2$, so $8s-1>0$. If $d=-1$,
then $0\le s<2$ and $K(s)=s^2(s-6)-2<0$. The nonzero square
$B_0(s)=(s-2)(8s-1)K(s)$ again forces $8s-1>0$. Therefore
$E=7T^2$.

The case $d=2$ is now impossible modulo 7. Indeed $E=7T^2$ gives
$a^2\equiv b^2\pmod7$, where both sides are nonzero by primitivity.
Then $2R^2=D\equiv-b^2\pmod7$, requiring the nonsquare 3 to equal
$(R/b)^2\pmod7$. Thus

$$
\boxed{a^2-2b^2=-R^2,\qquad8a^2-b^2=7T^2.}
\tag{U-BEU-UNIQUE-CLASS}
$$

Taking $r=R/b$, $h=T/b$ proves (U-BEU-UNIQUE-CONICS). Dividing
$w_j^2$ by $r^2=2-s$ shows that every $-H_j(s)$ is a square.
Finally $H_0=7h^2K$, so $V=w_0/(rh)$ satisfies $V^2=-7K$.
All divisions use nonzero quantities. This proves necessity. Substitution
in (U-BEU-RECONSTRUCT) proves the converse. The parameter-square conditions
follow by substituting $z=(1+t)/(1-t)$. $\square$

**Elliptic targets and the exact lifting coset.** Every completion maps to
the two fixed elliptic curves

$$
\mathcal E_1:\quad Y^2=X(X+7)(X+112),\qquad
(X,Y)=(-56s,392zrh),
\tag{U-BEU-E1}
$$
$$
\mathcal E_2:\quad Y^2=X^3+42X^2+686,\qquad
(X,Y)=(-7s,7V).
\tag{U-BEU-E2}
$$

Put $P=(-56,392)\in\mathcal E_1(\mathbb Q)$. The full-two-torsion
Kummer map, with root order $0,-7,-112$, is
$\delta(Q)=([X],[X+7],[X+112])$, with kernel
$2\mathcal E_1(\mathbb Q)$. The three individual square conditions
$s=z^2$, $2-s=r^2$, and $(8s-1)/7=h^2$ are equivalent to

$$
\delta(Q)=([-14],[-1],[14])=\delta(P),
$$

because $X=-14(2z)^2$, $X+7=-49h^2$, and $X+112=14(2r)^2$.
Consequently the exact rational-lifting condition to the two conics is

$$
\boxed{Q\in P+2\mathcal E_1(\mathbb Q).}
\tag{U-BEU-COSET}
$$

The special abscissae are excluded: $s=0$ would make
$(8s-1)/7<0$, while $s=1/8,2$ are not rational squares. The projective
two-quadric lift has no rational point at infinity, since its equations
there include $z^2+r^2=0$ and $8z^2-7h^2=0$. Thus no additional rational
boundary lift is lost by the affine coset description.

For completion, a point of this coset must still have a point on
$\mathcal E_2$ with $X_1=8X_2$, and the two residual numbers
$-H_1(s),-H_2(s)$ must both be squares. These conditions, together with
the explicit reconstruction, are sufficient for the three missing entries;
the canonical positivity and distinctness tests on all nine entries remain
necessary for an admissible magic square.

Both elliptic curves have positive rational rank. Their displayed integral
models have discriminants

$$
\Delta_1=2^{12}3^25^27^6,\qquad
\Delta_2=-2^63^37^6\cdot17,
$$

and good reduction at 11 and 13. Complete residue counts give

| Curve | $\#\mathcal E(\mathbb F_{11})$ | $\#\mathcal E(\mathbb F_{13})$ |
|---|---:|---:|
| $\mathcal E_1$ | 8 | 12 |
| $\mathcal E_2$ | 15 | 19 |

The good-reduction injections on prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion
show that $\mathcal E_1(\mathbb Q)_{\mathrm{tors}}=(\mathbb Z/2)^2$ and
$\mathcal E_2(\mathbb Q)_{\mathrm{tors}}=0$. The points $(-56,392)$ and
$(-7,49)$ are therefore non-torsion. No upper rank, Mordell–Weil basis,
or complete compatible point list is asserted by this descent.

**The two residual elliptic targets.**

Set $u=s-1$. The residual equations are

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal Q_1:\ y^2&=-8u^4-7u^3+9u^2+35u+25,\\
\mathcal Q_2:\ y^2&=-8u^4-31u^3-75u^2-49u+1.
\end{aligned}
$$

For a general quartic $y^2=au^4+bu^3+cu^2+du+q^2$, $q\ne0$, put

$$
X=\frac{2q(y+q)+du}{u^2},\qquad
Y=\frac{(X^2-4aq^2)u-dX-2q^2b}{2q}.
\tag{U-BEU-QUARTIC-MAP}
$$

Direct expansion gives

$$
Y^2=X^3+cX^2+(bd-4aq^2)X+(ad^2+b^2q^2-4acq^2).
\tag{U-BEU-QUARTIC-MODEL}
$$

The inverse, off its displayed exceptional divisor, is

$$
u=\frac{2qY+dX+2q^2b}{X^2-4aq^2},\qquad
y=\frac{Xu^2-du}{2q}-q.
\tag{U-BEU-QUARTIC-INVERSE}
$$

These are birational maps; the smooth projective models are isomorphic.
The point $(u,y)=(0,q)$ maps to the elliptic origin. Expanding at the
other point $(0,-q)$ gives

$$
X=\frac{d^2}{4q^2}-c,\qquad
Y=-\frac d{2q}X-qb.
$$

Thus the two quartics have the exact models and non-origin rational points

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal E_3:\quad Y^2&=X^3+9X^2+555X-1375,
&P_3&=(13/4,189/8),\\
\mathcal E_4:\quad Y^2&=X^3-75X^2+1551X-20647,
&P_4&=(2701/4,132597/8).
\end{aligned}
$$

Their discriminants are

$$
\Delta_3=-2^6 3^7 5^2\cdot3793,\qquad
\Delta_4=-2^6 3^{12}\cdot11\cdot193.
$$

The following complete residue counts occur at good-reduction primes:

| Curve | First count | Second count |
|---|---:|---:|
| $\mathcal E_3$ | $\#\mathcal E_3(\mathbf F_7)=6$ | $\#\mathcal E_3(\mathbf F_{23})=31$ |
| $\mathcal E_4$ | $\#\mathcal E_4(\mathbf F_5)=4$ | $\#\mathcal E_4(\mathbf F_{13})=9$ |

Prime-to-residue-characteristic torsion injectivity shows that both rational
torsion groups are trivial. For each pair the two group orders are coprime,
and neither residue characteristic divides the other group order. Therefore
$P_3,P_4$ are non-torsion and both curves have rank at least one.

Together with $\mathcal E_1,\mathcal E_2$, this gives **four** fixed
positive-rank elliptic targets. The points must still determine the same
$s$ under the specified maps. No four unrelated rational points produce
a lift. Section 9.51 determines the rank of $\mathcal E_2$ and an additional elliptic quotient, but does not certify complete generators for all four targets.

**Geometric scope.** The full simultaneous system retains all six square
roots of $s,2-s,(8s-1)/7,-7K,-H_1,-H_2$. Their classes are independent:
each has a finite zero not shared by the other five. Their finite branch
product has degree fourteen and is squarefree (its reduction modulo 13 is
coprime to its derivative), and infinity is also branched. The resulting
degree-64 cover of the $s$-line therefore has genus
$1+64(-1+15/4)=177$. It is a degree-four étale cover of the original
genus-45 completion curve: the original radicals
$z,w_0,w_1,w_2$ have exponent vectors
$100000,011100,010010,010001$, of rank four, and every inertia vector
has a nonzero image. Thus this theorem provides a rationally exhaustive
descent with fixed elliptic projections, not a reduction of the genus of
the entire common-lift curve.

### 9.51. A common cubic-field elliptic target and its rank bound

Let
\[
K(s)=s^3-6s^2-2,
\qquad C:\ V^2=-7(z^6-6z^4-2).
\]
Every completion in the preceding six-square family determines a rational
point of \(C\), through \(s=z^2\) and \(V^2=-7K(s)\). The additional
conditions \(r^2=2-s\), \(h^2=(8s-1)/7\), and
\(y_j^2=-H_j(s)\), \(j=1,2\), remain necessary.

**Theorem.** Put
\[
L=\mathbb Q(\theta),\qquad \theta^3-6\theta^2-2=0,\qquad
\beta=\frac{(\theta+1)^2}{3},\qquad
\eta=1-3\theta+\beta.
\]
Then \(\eta^2=2/\theta=\theta^2-6\theta\). Rational points of \(C\)
are in exact correspondence, up to the simultaneous sign choices, with
\(z\in\mathbb Q\) and \(\kappa,w\in L\) satisfying
\[
\kappa^2=(\theta-1)(\theta-z^2),
\tag{CE1}
\]
\[
\mathcal E_L:\quad
w^2=7(\theta-1)
       \bigl(z^4+(\theta-6)z^2+\theta^2-6\theta\bigr).
\tag{CE2}
\]
The reconstruction is \(V=w\kappa/(\theta-1)\). The curve
\(\mathcal E_L\) is an elliptic curve over \(L\), with origin chosen at
\((z,w)=(1,7)\), and
\[
1\le\operatorname{rank}\mathcal E_L(L)\le2<3=[L:\mathbb Q].
\tag{CE3}
\]
Section 9.53 sharpens (CE3) to exact rank two and supplies an explicit
subgroup of finite odd index. These rank statements alone do not give
a complete rational-coordinate point list.

**Proof.** First consider the two elliptic quotients
\[
E_2:Y^2=X^3+42X^2+686,
\qquad E_5:Y^2=X^3+588X-1372,
\]
with maps
\[
(z,V)\longmapsto(-7z^2,7V),\qquad
(z,V)\longmapsto(14/z^2,14V/z^3).
\tag{CE4}
\]
Their pulled-back invariant differentials are \(-z\,dz/V\) and
\(-dz/V\), so \(\operatorname{Jac}(C)\) is isogenous over
\(\mathbb Q\) to \(E_2\times E_5\).

We apply the cubic-algebra two-descent of
[Cremona–Fisher–O’Neil–Simon–Stoll, *Explicit n-descent on elliptic curves, III. Algorithms*](https://mathe2.uni-bayreuth.de/stoll/papers/Explicit-Descent-III.pdf), Section 3, equation (10) and its homogeneous
two-quadric construction. Here the two cubic roots used in the descent
are \(-7\theta\) and \(14/\theta\), respectively. The general descent
map is \((X,Y)\mapsto[X-\alpha]\), with kernel \(2E(\mathbb Q)\).

The maximal order of \(L\) has basis \(1,\theta,\beta\), discriminant
\(-204\), and class number one. To verify maximality, \(\beta\) has
polynomial \(T^3-17T^2+7T-3\); only 2 could divide the index of the
resulting order. The polynomial of \(\theta\) is Eisenstein at 2,
giving a tame totally ramified cubic extension with discriminant exponent
two, already the exponent in \(-204\). The Minkowski bound is
\((8/(9\pi))\sqrt{204}<5\). The prime above 2 is generated by
\(\theta\), of norm 2, and the two distinct primes above 3 by
\(\beta\) and \(\gamma=\beta-2\theta\), both of norm 3. These generate
all ideal classes within the Minkowski bound.

The unit \(\epsilon=\beta-\theta\) has norm 1 and polynomial
\(T^3-11T^2+5T-1\). It is not a square: a square root would have an
integral unit polynomial \(T^3+aT^2+bT+c\), \(c=\pm1\), requiring
\(2b-a^2=-11\) and \(b^2-2ac=5\). The first makes \(a\) odd; direct
substitution excludes \(|a|=1,3\), while
\(((a^2-11)/2)^2-5>2|a|\) excludes \(|a|\ge5\).
Thus \(-1,\epsilon\) generate the units modulo squares; a fundamental
unit assertion is unnecessary.

Above 7 and 17 choose
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mu&=\theta-1,& N(\mu)&=7,\\
\nu&=\theta^2-5\theta-5=7/\mu,&N(\nu)&=49,\\
\pi_u&=-1-3\theta+2\beta,&N(\pi_u)&=17,\\
\pi_r&=-2-3\theta+\beta,&N(\pi_r)&=-17.
\end{aligned}
\]
They generate, respectively, the degree-one and degree-two primes over 7,
and the unramified and ramified primes over 17. The squareclasses
supported above \(2,3,7,17\) are therefore generated independently by
\[
-1,\epsilon,\theta,\beta,\gamma,\mu,\nu,\pi_u,\pi_r.
\tag{CE5}
\]
For either rational elliptic curve, the norm-square condition leaves
exactly the sixteen classes
\[
\delta_m=\epsilon^{m_0}(\beta\gamma)^{m_1}
               \nu^{m_2}(-\pi_u\pi_r)^{m_3},
\quad m=m_0+2m_1+4m_2+8m_3.
\]

Write \(\delta_m(u+v\theta+w\beta)^2=A+B\theta+D\beta\).
The projective covering equations are
\(B=7t^2,D=0\) for \(E_2\), and
\(B=56t^2,D=-21t^2\) for \(E_5\). Complete primitive projective
enumeration gives the following exclusions:

| Curve | Excluded masks | Exclusion modulus |
|---|---|---:|
| \(E_2\) | \(1,2,5,6,8,11,12,15\) | 4 |
| \(E_2\) | \(9,10,13,14\) | 9 |
| \(E_5\) | \(1,2,5,6,8,11,12,15\) | 8 |
| \(E_5\) | \(3,7,9,13\) | 9 |
| \(E_5\) | \(10,14\) | 289 |

Each enumeration normalizes the first unit coordinate to one and retains
all lifts of the other three coordinates. The surviving Kummer classes
are \(\{0,3,4,7\}\) for \(E_2\), and \(\{0,4\}\) for \(E_5\).
They are realized by
\[
P=(-7,49),\quad Q=(1,27)\quad\text{on }E_2,
\qquad P_5=(14,98)\quad\text{on }E_5,
\]
using the identities
\[
7(\theta-1)=(\theta-1)^2\nu,
\quad (1+7\theta)\epsilon\beta\gamma=(1+5\theta^2)^2,
\quad \eta^2=2/\theta.
\]
The rational torsion groups are trivial, as follows from the respective
coprime good-prime counts \((15,19)\) at \((11,13)\), and \((5,9)\)
at \((5,11)\). Consequently
\[
\operatorname{rank}E_2(\mathbb Q)=2,
\qquad\operatorname{rank}E_5(\mathbb Q)=1,
\qquad\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Jac}(C)(\mathbb Q)=3.
\tag{CE6}
\]

For a point of \(C(\mathbb Q)\), put \(s=z^2\). The two Kummer
classes from (CE4) have ratio
\[
\frac{14/s-14/\theta}{-7s+7\theta}
=\frac2{s\theta}=(\eta/z)^2,
\]
so their common class is either 0 or 4. The square \(-7K(s)\) excludes
both positive and negative \(7\)-adic valuations of \(s\); hence
\(s\equiv1\pmod7\). At the degree-two prime above 7, \(\theta-s\)
is a unit and \(7(\theta-s)\) has odd valuation. The common class is
therefore 4. In particular the images lie in the single cosets
\[
P+2E_2(\mathbb Q),\qquad P_5+2E_5(\mathbb Q).
\tag{CE7}
\]
This class identity is precisely (CE1), because \(\nu=7/(\theta-1)\).
Factoring \(K(z^2)\) over \(L\) gives (CE2) and the displayed
reconstruction. Conversely, that reconstruction has square
\(-7K(z^2)\in\mathbb Q\). An element of a cubic field whose square
is rational is rational, proving exactness. There is no omitted rational
point at \(z=0\), which would require \(V^2=14\), or at infinity,
whose leading coefficient is \(-7\). Also \(\kappa\ne0\), since
\(\theta\notin\mathbb Q\).

It remains to prove (CE3). With \(A=7(\theta-1)\), \(B=\theta-6\),
the elliptic curve (CE2) is isomorphic over \(L\) to
\[
\mathscr E:\quad Y^2=X(X-e_+)(X-e_-),
\quad e_\pm=A(B\pm2\eta),
\]
where
\[
e_+=35+7\theta-7\beta,
\qquad e_-=35-133\theta+49\beta.
\]
Here is an explicit birational isomorphism, including the rational
function needed for elliptic Chabauty. Put
\[
u=z-1,\quad a=A,\ b=4A,\ c=A(6+B),\ d=A(4+2B),\ q=7,
\quad \sigma=A(B+2).
\]
The shifted quartic is \(w^2=au^4+bu^3+cu^2+du+q^2\). Set
\[
X_0=\frac{2q(w+q)+du}{u^2},\qquad
Y=\frac{(X_0^2-4aq^2)u-dX_0-2q^2b}{2q},\qquad
X=X_0+\sigma.
\tag{CE8}
\]
Direct substitution gives the displayed equation of \(\mathscr E\).
Conversely, with \(X_0=X-\sigma\),
\[
u=\frac{2qY+dX_0+2q^2b}{X_0^2-4aq^2},\qquad
z=1+u,\qquad w=\frac{X_0u^2-du}{2q}-q.
\tag{CE9}
\]
These maps are mutual inverses on dense open sets, hence extend to an
isomorphism of the smooth projective curves. The point \((z,w)=(1,7)\)
maps to the identity, while \((1,-7)\) maps to
\[
R=(9\theta^2-66\theta+36,\ 3\theta^2-36\theta+222)
\]
on \(\mathscr E(L)\). Thus this target is the quartic itself with the
specified origin. The different map \((z,w)\mapsto(Az^2,Azw)\) has
degree two and lands on the other, two-isogenous cubic; it is not used
as the identification (CE8). The three reductions above 29, at
\(\theta=3,14,18\), have orders \(24,28,32\), and the degree-one
reduction above 31 at \(\theta=25\) has order 32. These good-reduction
counts prove \(\mathscr E(L)_{\rm tors}\cong(\mathbb Z/2)^2\).
The ordinate of \(R\) is nonzero, so the rank is positive.

For the upper bound, the norms
\[
N(e_+)=-2\cdot3^2\cdot7^4,\quad
N(e_-)=2\cdot3\cdot7^4\cdot17,\quad
N(e_+-e_-)=-2^7\cdot7^4
\]
show that the full-two-torsion Kummer map is supported on (CE5). Its
first two coordinates lie in an 18-dimensional binary space; the third
is their product. No norm condition to \(\mathbb Q\) is imposed here.

The local Kummer dimensions used below are the standard number-field dimensions in Stoll, *Descent on elliptic curves*, Sections 1.1 and 1.3 (the local formula on printed page 20). The local square tests use valuation parity and residue characters at
odd primes. At the dyadic prime, a unit is a square exactly when it is
a square modulo \(\theta^7\), by \(v(2)=3\) and Hensel's strict
inequality \(7>6\). There are 128 residues, 64 units, four unit-square
residues, and sixteen unit squareclasses. This gives the full
five-dimensional local squareclass space after adjoining valuation
parity.

The integral multiplication table is
\[
\theta^2=-1-2\theta+3\beta,\quad
\theta\beta=-2-5\theta+8\beta,\quad
\beta^2=-5-14\theta+22\beta.
\]
Using it, exact local Kummer image spans have dimensions five at 2 and
two at each odd bad place. These are the complete dimensions of
\(\mathscr E(L_v)/2\mathscr E(L_v)\), so a spanning set of actual
local points certifies the entire image. At 2 such a set is supplied by
the three two-torsion abscissae, \(X=1\), and
\[
-3+\theta/2,\quad -6-23\theta/2+18\beta,
\quad35/4-7\theta/2+3\beta/4.
\]
At the two places above 3, use the two-torsion points and \(X=2\).
At the degree-one places \(17u,17r\), use them with \(X=5,6\),
respectively. The two places above 7 require only the two-torsion points.
Local square tests on the displayed products certify each point's
existence; this is not an inference from a truncated point search.

Pulling the annihilators of these local images back to the 18 global
coordinates gives accumulated ranks
\[
\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrr}
v&2&3u&3r&7u&7v&17u&17r\\\hline
\text{rank}&5&7&9&11&12&14&14.
\end{array}
\]
Thus the two-Selmer dimension is at most four. Subtracting the two
dimensions of rational two-torsion gives rank at most two, completing
the proof. \(\square\)

The rational-coordinate condition in (CE2), the residual conic (CE1),
and the other four rational square conditions are essential. The rank
inequality makes elliptic Chabauty over the cubic field applicable at
the level of its rank hypothesis; it supplies neither a complete
Mordell--Weil basis nor the required local analytic zero certificate.


### 9.52. The exact cubic-field two-Selmer group

Retain the field and elliptic curve $\mathscr E/L$ of Section 9.51.
The finite-place calculation there determines the complete group:
\[
\dim_{\mathbf F_2}\operatorname{Sel}^{(2)}(\mathscr E/L)=4.
\tag{CE10}
\]
In particular, put
\[
\delta=(\beta-\theta)(-1-3\theta+2\beta)
       =-3-8\theta+12\beta.
\]
The smooth projective two-cover represented by
\[
\delta u^2-v^2=e_+t^2,\qquad
\delta(u^2-w^2)=e_-t^2
\tag{CE11}
\]
has a point over every completion of $L$. This assertion does not give an
$L$-rational point or a compatible magic-square completion.

**Proof.** The nine generators in (CE5), ordered as
\[
-1,\epsilon,\theta,\beta,\gamma,\mu,\nu,\pi_u,\pi_r,
\]
give two independent nine-bit squareclass coordinates $a,b$; the third
coordinate is their product. Represent their combined vector by $a+512b$.
The complete local Kummer conditions at the seven specified finite places
have the following seventeen binary annihilator rows, written in decimal:
\[
\begin{split}
(&2243,223147,431,219,73,76296,4096,8192,16,16384,\\
 &32,91200,178,159744,65536,131072,256).
\end{split}
\]
Their rank is fourteen, as follows either by binary row reduction or by
the cumulative ranks and dimension-certified local images in Section 9.51.
Thus their common kernel has sixteen elements.

The unique real embedding satisfies $6<\theta<61/10$. Substitution into
the displayed generator formulas shows that only $-1$ and $\pi_r$ are
negative. Also $e_+<0<e_-$. The real Kummer image has sign triples
$(+,+,+)$ and $(-,+,-)$, so its sole condition on the two coordinates is
$b_0+b_8=0$. Its binary row is $131584$, the exclusive-or sum of rows
$1,4,6,7,9,10,14,15$ of the list above. Hence it imposes no additional
condition. The complex place imposes none.

At every remaining finite place the residue characteristic is odd and
$\mathscr E$ has good reduction, since
$\Delta=16e_+^2e_-^2(e_+-e_-)^2$ is supported above $2,3,7,17$.
All candidate squareclasses have even valuations there. They are therefore
unramified and lie in the local Kummer image, which equals the unramified
subgroup by [Stoll, *Selmer groups and descent*, Proposition 2.4(2)--(3)](https://people.maths.bris.ac.uk/~matyd/Trieste2017/Stoll.pdf).
This also explains why imposing additional good-prime tests cannot shrink
this kernel. All places have now been accounted for, proving (CE10).

The class $(\delta,1,\delta)$ has coordinates $(a,b)=(130,0)$.
Its binary inner product with every listed row is zero, so it belongs to
the Selmer group. The full-two-torsion descent identifies its two-cover
with (CE11). Membership in every local Kummer image is precisely local
solubility of the smooth projective cover, proving the assertion. $\square$

The exact sequence
\[
0\longrightarrow\mathscr E(L)/2\mathscr E(L)
\longrightarrow\operatorname{Sel}^{(2)}(\mathscr E/L)
\longrightarrow\Sha(\mathscr E/L)[2]\longrightarrow0
\]
therefore gives
\[
\dim_{\mathbf F_2}\Sha(\mathscr E/L)[2]
=2-\operatorname{rank}\mathscr E(L).
\tag{CE12}
\]
Together with (CE3), this leaves rank two with trivial $\Sha[2]$, or rank
one with one-dimensional $\Sha[2]$. Local solubility alone does not select an alternative. The explicit
global point in Section 9.53 selects rank two. No finiteness of all
of $\Sha$ is assumed.


### 9.53. The missing global class, exact rank two, and odd index

Use the field, basis, elliptic model, and known point $R$ of Section 9.51:
\[
L=\mathbb Q(\theta),\quad \theta^3-6\theta^2-2=0,
\quad\beta=(\theta+1)^2/3,
\]
\[
\mathscr E:\ Y^2=X(X-e_+)(X-e_-),\quad
e_+=35+7\theta-7\beta,\quad e_-=35-133\theta+49\beta.
\]
Put $\delta=-3-8\theta+12\beta$ and
\[
R_2=\left(-\frac{401}{4}-\frac{695}{2}\theta+\frac{809}{2}\beta,
5759+\frac{61237}{4}\theta-\frac{193277}{8}\beta\right).
\tag{CE-SECOND-POINT}
\]

**Theorem.** The displayed point belongs to $\mathscr E(L)$ and has
Kummer class $(\delta,1,\delta)$, the class represented by $(130,0)$
in Section 9.52. Moreover
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{rank}\mathscr E(L)=2,\qquad
\Sha(\mathscr E/L)[2^\infty]=0.}
\tag{CE-EXACT-RANK}
\]
The subgroup
\[
H=\langle(0,0),(e_+,0),R,R_2\rangle
\]
has finite odd index in $\mathscr E(L)$. In particular its closure has
the full image modulo every power of two. No index-one assertion or
saturation at an odd prime is made.

**Exact point certificate.** With $X_2=X(R_2)$, direct reduction by
$\theta^3=6\theta^2+2$ gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
X_2&=\delta\left(-12-14\theta+\frac{11}{2}\beta\right)^2,\\
X_2-e_+&=\left(-3+13\theta-\frac12\beta\right)^2,\\
X_2-e_-&=\delta\left(-12+7\theta-\frac32\beta\right)^2.
\end{aligned}
\tag{CE-SECOND-FACTORS}
\]
Multiplying these three square roots and $\delta$ gives the displayed
ordinate. These identities certify both the point and its Kummer class.

**Independent squareclass certificate.** Let $T_0=(0,0)$ and
$T_+=(e_+,0)$. Their first two Kummer coordinates are
$(e_+e_-,-e_+)$ and $(e_+,e_+(e_+-e_-))$, respectively. At the two
degree-one primes above 29 given by $\theta=3,14$, the corresponding
values of $\beta$ are $15,17$. The first two coordinates specialize as
follows; every listed element is nonzero.

| Point | $\theta=3$ | $\theta=14$ |
|---|---|---|
| $T_0$ | $(4,20)$ | $(4,15)$ |
| $T_+$ | $(9,19)$ | $(14,18)$ |
| $R$ | $(6,26)$ | $(6,21)$ |
| $R_2$ | $(8,1)$ | $(2,1)$ |

Writing a nonsquare character as 1 and a square character as 0 gives,
with these points as columns, the matrix
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
0&0&0&1\\
0&1&1&0\\
0&1&0&1\\
1&1&1&0
\end{pmatrix},
\]
of rank four over $\mathbb F_2$. Any global square has trivial characters
at these places, so the four global Kummer classes are independent.
Section 9.52 proves that the containing two-Selmer group has dimension
four. Thus they span $\mathscr E(L)/2\mathscr E(L)$, the rank is two,
and $\Sha[2]=0$. A nonzero two-primary torsion element has a nonzero
multiple of order two, proving $\Sha[2^\infty]=0$ without assuming
finiteness of all of $\Sha$.

For completeness, the good-reduction orders at the three primes above
29 are $24,28,32$, and the order at $\theta=25$ above 31 is $32$.
These bounds, together with the displayed full two-torsion, give
$\mathscr E(L)_{\rm tors}\simeq(\mathbb Z/2)^2$. Consequently $R,R_2$
are independent nontorsion points and $H$ has finite index. The finite
quotient $\mathscr E(L)/H$ equals twice itself, because
$H+2\mathscr E(L)=\mathscr E(L)$; hence its order is odd. $\square$

**Two-primary descent is now entirely realized by points.** For every
$n\ge1$ the Selmer exact sequence gives
\[
\operatorname{Sel}^{(2^n)}(\mathscr E/L)
\simeq\mathscr E(L)/2^n\mathscr E(L)
\simeq(\mathbb Z/2^n)^2\oplus(\mathbb Z/2)^2.
\tag{CE-REALIZED-TOWER}
\]
Every transition is surjective and every induced Cassels--Tate pairing
is zero. The previously missing class cannot be excluded by additional
local conditions or by any finite two-power descent, since it has the
explicit global representative (CE-SECOND-POINT).

**Rational-coordinate scope.** The exact inverse map (CE9) sends $R_2$ to
\[
z=\frac{10057}{33009}-\frac{32480}{33009}\theta
  +\frac{4292}{11003}\beta\notin\mathbb Q.
\]
Thus $R_2$ itself is not a rational-coordinate quartic point or a
completion of the six-square family. The group certificate supplies
the full rank and the index condition at 2. Section 9.54 uses the
actual logarithmic span and all residual conditions to complete the
family exclusion.

### 9.54. Complete rational-coordinate determination and family exclusion

Retain the exact family correspondence of Section 9.50 and the cubic
descent of Section 9.51. Put $A=7(\theta-1)$, $B=\theta-6$, and
$\eta=1-3\theta+\beta$. Thus the elliptic quartic is
\[
\mathcal E_L:\quad w^2=f(z)=A(z^4+Bz^2+\eta^2).
\]

**Theorem.** The complete rational-coordinate locus is
\[
\boxed{\{(z,w)\in\mathcal E_L(L):
z\in\mathbb Q\}
=\{(1,7),(1,-7),(-1,7),(-1,-7)\}.}
\tag{CE-RATIONAL-COORDINATES}
\]
The genus-two curve $C:V^2=-7(z^6-6z^4-2)$ consequently has exactly
the four rational points $(z,V)=(\pm1,\pm7)$. Every simultaneous
completion in Section 9.50 has $z$ in this locus.
Consequently its only rational completion parameters are $t=0,\infty$,
both repeated-entry cases. The Bremner--Elsholtz--Ulas six-square
family of Section 9.50 has no admissible completion to nine distinct
positive squares.
\[
\boxed{\text{There is no admissible completion in this specified family.}}
\tag{U-BEU-COMPLETE-EXCLUSION}
\]

**All nonunit rational coordinates are locally excluded.** In
$K=L\otimes\mathbb Q_2$, normalize $\nu(\theta)=1$; then
$\nu(2)=3$, $\nu(B)=1$, $\nu(\eta^2)=2$, and $\nu(A)=0$.
Both $A$ and $f(2)/\eta^2=-21-49\theta+126\beta$ are nonsquares
in $K$. Here is a complete finite certificate. Encode a residue
$\sum_{j=0}^6\epsilon_j\theta^j$ modulo $\theta^7$ by
$\sum_{j=0}^6\epsilon_j2^j$, with $\epsilon_j\in\{0,1\}$.
Enumerating the squares of all 64 unit residues gives exactly
$\{1,37,49,85\}$. The residues of $A$ and $f(2)/\eta^2$ are
respectively $83$ and $51$, outside that set. This computation uses
only $\theta^3=6\theta^2+2$ and the integral basis already established.

For rational $z\ne0$, write $n=v_2(z)$. If $n<0$,
\[
\frac{f(z)}{z^4}=A\left(1+\frac B{z^2}+\frac{\eta^2}{z^4}\right),
\]
and the correction to one has $\nu\ge7$. If $n\ge2$,
\[
\frac{f(z)}{\eta^2}
=A\left(1+\frac B{\eta^2}z^2+\frac{z^4}{\eta^2}\right),
\]
and the correction has $\nu\ge11$. Every $1+\epsilon$ with
$\nu(\epsilon)>2\nu(2)=6$ is a square by Hensel's lemma, so
both cases have nonsquare class $A$. The case $z=0$ has that class
as well. If $n=1$, put $z=2u$ with $u\in\mathbb Z_2^\times$.
Since $u^2-1$ is divisible by eight, the difference
$(f(z)-f(2))/\eta^2$ has $\nu\ge14$. Hence $f(z)/f(2)$ is a
square, and $f(z)$ has the nonsquare class of $f(2)/\eta^2$.
Thus a rational coordinate of a $K$-point must lie in
$\mathbb Z_2^\times$. The quartic's points at infinity require
$\sqrt A\in K$ and are also absent.

**A global logarithmic annihilator.** The field
$K=L\otimes\mathbb Q_2$ is a field, since the polynomial of $\theta$
is Eisenstein at 2. Its integers have the integral basis
$(1,\theta,\beta)$ used above. On the integral elliptic model
\[
Y^2=X^3+a_2X^2+a_4X,\qquad
a_2=-(e_++e_-),\quad a_4=e_+e_-,
\]
use the parameter $T=-X/Y$ at the origin. Its invariant differential is
\[
\omega=\frac{dX}{2Y}
=\frac{dT}{\sqrt{1-2a_2T^2+(a_2^2-4a_4)T^4}}.
\]
The coefficient of $T^{2n}$ in the inverse square root is the integral
polynomial
\[
c_n=\sum_{j=0}^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}
\binom n{2j}\binom{2j}j a_2^{n-2j}a_4^j.
\]
Thus the formal logarithm
$\log_E(T)=\sum_{n\ge0}c_nT^{2n+1}/(2n+1)$ has integral
coefficients at 2, converges on $2\mathcal O_K$, and differs from
$T$ by an element of $T^3\mathcal O_K$ there. This is the formal
logarithm associated with the invariant differential, as in Silverman
[35], Proposition IV.5.2 and Theorem IV.6.4(a). Good reduction at 2 is not required.

Two exact doublings of the points $R,R_2$ in Section 9.53 give:

| Point | Coordinates of $T$ modulo $16\mathcal O_K$ | Coordinatewise valuations at 2 |
|---|---|---|
| $4R$ | $(4,12,0)$ | $(2,2,7)$ |
| $4R_2$ | $(0,0,8)$ | $(6,4,3)$ |

It follows that the integral coordinate vectors
\[
\ell_1=\log_E(4R)/4,\qquad \ell_2=\log_E(4R_2)/8
\]
reduce respectively to $(1,1,0)$ and $(0,0,1)$ modulo 2.
Their cross product therefore defines a $\mathbb Q_2$-linear
functional $\lambda:K\to\mathbb Q_2$ with integral coefficients,
annihilating both logarithms, and satisfying
\[
\lambda(1)\equiv1\pmod2.
\tag{CE-UNIT-ANNIHILATOR}
\]
These residues also independently prove the two logarithms linearly
independent. Since $R,R_2$ have full rank, $\lambda$ annihilates
the logarithm of every global point of $E(L)$.

Here the logarithm on all of $E(K)$ is obtained by multiplying a point
into a sufficiently small formal subgroup, taking the formal logarithm,
and dividing by that integer. Such a subgroup is open in the compact
group $E(K)$ and has finite index; the formal homomorphism identity
makes the definition independent of the chosen multiple. Thus the
preceding annihilation uses full rank, without a saturation hypothesis
or a good-reduction integration theorem.
