For \(S\in E(N)\), the anti-invariant point \(S-\sigma S\) consequently
has order at most two, so \(2S\in E(F)\). The no-halving result in §1
implies \(2S=2R\) for \(R\in E(F)\). Since all two-torsion is already
defined over \(F\), \(S-R\in E[2](F)\), proving (QUADCOVER-1).
This excludes both new saturation and new torsion; it is stronger than
a rank comparison alone.

#### 3. Transfer to the entire full-root curve

Assume (QUADCOVER-1). A point of the full-root curve over \(N=\mathbb C(t)\)
away from the exceptional charts of
[genus 49_generic_points.md](genus 49_generic_points.md)
gives an offset elliptic point of the old group and a square center.
Every nonboundary old image has a positive-genus center cover, so it
cannot acquire a square center under any rational substitution.
Thus only the same four \(n\)-coordinates and 128 signs can occur.

The exceptional charts cannot create extra points in a quadratic
extension, even though some individual radicands could become squares:

* At \(n=\pm1\), the required classes include
  \(1+m^2,\ 3-m^2,\ 3m^2-1\), whose disjoint simple roots give rank three.
* At \(n=0\) or infinity, the required classes include
  \(1+m^2,\ 1+m^2-4m,\ 1+m^2+4m\), again of rank three.
* At \(n=\pm i\), the required classes include \(m,\ 1-m^2\),
  of rank two.

A quadratic field kills at most one independent squareclass. These
charts therefore supply no point over \(N\). The argument handles
the entire smooth projective full-root curve, not merely its dense
affine chart.

#### Certificate and limitation

[verify_quadratic_halving_extensions.py](verify_quadratic_halving_extensions.py)
enumerates the complete fifteen nonzero Kummer classes, records all
eight halving fields and their genera, checks every pulled-back root
and pairwise gcd, and verifies the exceptional-chart independence.

This result leaves the positive-rank quadratic twists unresolved.
It gives a precise prerequisite for a new rational quadratic family;
it does not prove that such families are absent.


### 12.42. Exact groups on four families of quadratic conic covers

Write $F=\mathbb Q(m)$, $p=2m/(1-m^2)$ and retain the alternate elliptic curve
\[
E_p:y^2=x(x+\beta^2)(x+\alpha\gamma),\qquad
\alpha=p^2-3,\quad\beta=p^2+1,\quad\gamma=1-3p^2.
\]
Let $C/F$ denote the full-root genus-forty-nine curve. The constant in a quadratic cover cannot be discarded: different rational constants can have different arithmetic ranks even though their geometric ranks agree.

**Theorem (four conic-cover families).** For every $c\in\mathbb Q^*$, each of
\[
F\bigl(\sqrt{c(1+m^2)}\bigr),\qquad
F\bigl(\sqrt{cm}\bigr),\qquad
F\bigl(\sqrt{c(m^2-1)}\bigr)
\tag{U-CONIC-THREE}
\]
has exactly the old elliptic group and exactly the old 128 full-root points. The same conclusion holds for
\[
N_c=F\bigl(\sqrt{c(m^2-2m-1)}\bigr)
\tag{U-CONIC-MIXED}
\]
whenever its defining conic has a rational point. Reflection $m\mapsto-m$ gives the corresponding statement with $m^2+2m-1$. These are function-field theorems; they do not classify all rational points of specialized fibers.

The proof has three distinct rank calculations. The first and third establish arithmetic rank zero for the required constant twists. The second establishes geometric rank zero. The distinction is necessary.

**The branch pair $m=\pm i$.** Put $w=m^2$. Clearing denominators by
$x_w=(1-m^2)^4x_p$, $y_w=(1-m^2)^6y_p$ gives
\[
E_w:y^2=x(x+A)(x+B),\qquad
A=(w+1)^4,\quad B=(-3w^2+10w-3)(w^2-14w+1).
\tag{U-CONIC-DESCENT-MODEL}
\]
The anti-invariant rank for adjoining $\sqrt{c(1+m^2)}$ is the sum of the ranks of $E_w^{c(w+1)}$ and $E_w^{cw(w+1)}$ over $\mathbb Q(w)$. The reciprocal identities $w^4A(1/w)=A(w)$ and $w^4B(1/w)=B(w)$, with $x\mapsto w^6x$, $y\mapsto w^9y$ on the twisted models, identify these two ranks without changing $c$.

Consider the fixed twist
\[
\mathcal T:y^2=x\bigl(x+(w+1)A\bigr)\bigl(x+(w+1)B\bigr).
\]
Its fibers are $I_8^*$ at $-1$, two $I_4$ at $w^2-6w+1=0$, four $I_2$ at $3,1/3$ and $w^2-14w+1=0$, and $I_0^*$ at infinity. Thus $\chi(\mathcal O)=3$, $b_2=34$, and the trivial lattice has rank $28$. The residual cohomology has dimension six. Full rational two-torsion fixes the outer components of the $D_{12}$ and $D_4$ diagrams; the diagrams are split. At an $I_4$ position its root trace is $2+\chi_q(-(w+1))$.

These are good resolved models at 5. At $w=-1$, the root contacts are $u^5$ and $uB(u-1)$ with $u=w+1$ and $B(-1)=-256$. At infinity the two nonzero minimal roots are
\[
t(1+t)^5,\qquad t(1+t)(-3+10t-3t^2)(1-14t+t^2),
\]
whose distinct initial slopes are $1,-3$. The bad-position discriminants and pairwise resultants have prime support contained in $\{2,3\}$. The indicated blowup resolutions therefore have unit leading coefficients at 5.

Exact counts give the following data. A root component adds $q$ times its trace to the Weierstrass count.

| $q$ | Weierstrass count | Root trace | Residual trace |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| $5$ | $36$ | $18$ | $0$ |
| $25$ | $662$ | $22$ | $-14$ |
| $125$ | $15876$ | $18$ | $0$ |
| $625$ | $391274$ | $26$ | $-602$ |

Newton identities and orthogonal reciprocity give
\[
F_5(T)=T^6+7T^4+175T^2+15625
=(T^2+25)(T^4-18T^2+625),\qquad F_5(\pm5)=40000.
\tag{U-CONIC-I-FROBENIUS}
\]
The fourth coefficient fixes the reciprocity sign. A nontorsion point on a constant $c$-twist supplies a quadratic-character line in the residual divisor representation: the Shioda projection subtracting the zero section, fiber and component corrections is Galois equivariant and has positive height. If this character is ramified at 5, it contradicts good reduction. If unramified, its Frobenius eigenvalue must be $5$ or $-5$, both absent. Hence every constant twist of $\mathcal T$ has arithmetic rank zero. No Tate conjecture is used. The eigenvalues $\pm5i$ are retained; this argument does not prove geometric rank zero.

**The branch pairs $\{0,\infty\}$ and $\{-1,1\}$.** The fixed surface now is
\[
\mathcal U:y^2=x\bigl(x+(w-1)A\bigr)\bigl(x+(w-1)B\bigr).
\]
Its fibers are $I_8$ at $-1$, the same two $I_4$ and four $I_2$, and $I_0^*$ at $1$ and infinity. The trivial lattice has rank $27$, so the residual dimension is seven. The $I_8$ tangent class is $2$; the $I_4$ tangent class is $-(w-1)$. Both $D_4$ diagrams are split. The root trace is
\[
14+3\chi_q(2)+\#\{w^2-14w+1=0\}
+2\#\{w^2-6w+1=0\}
+\sum_{w^2-6w+1=0}\chi_q(-(w-1)).
\]
At 5 and 7 all these components are defined over the quadratic finite-field extension. Good resolved reduction follows from the same bad-position resultants, and from the distinct $I_0^*$ slopes $0,16,-48$ at $1$ and $0,1,-3$ at infinity.

| Prime | Extension degrees | Weierstrass counts | Residual traces |
|---:|---|---|---|
| $5$ | $1,2,3,4$ | $39,655,15663,390747$ | $3,-21,-213,-1129$ |
| $7$ | $1,2,3,4$ | $61,2459,118765,5766955$ | $-3,-41,429,-2649$ |

In each row the residual trace is $N_W-1-q^2-2q$: the resolved component contribution cancels the component part of the trivial representation. The complete polynomials are
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_5(T)&=(T+5)(T^2-8T+25)(T^4+30T^2+625),\\
F_7(T)&=(T-7)(T^6+10T^5+95T^4+588T^3
+4655T^2+24010T+117649).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-CONIC-REAL-FROBENIUS}
\]
Exact cyclotomic factor tests on $F_\ell(\ell T)$ show that the displayed linear factor is the only root-of-unity eigenvalue in each residual representation. Thus the geometric characteristic-zero Picard rank is either $27$ or $28$.

For completeness the discriminant argument does not assume an unproved Tate conjecture for these surfaces with $\chi=3$. Suppose that rank $28$ occurs in characteristic zero. Its specialized divisor space fills every possible algebraic eigenvalue at both reductions. Over $\mathbb F_{\ell^2}$ these $28$ classes have eigenvalue $\ell^2$ and fill the whole generalized eigenspace, so the Tate conjecture holds under this supposition. Milne's surface theorem [47] then supplies finiteness of the Brauer group and the Artin–Tate formula. The finite Brauer order is a square by [48], including the corrected corollary.

Set $G_5=F_5/(T+5)$, $G_7=F_7/(T-7)$. The Artin–Tate exponent is $\chi(\mathcal O)-1=2$, and the field size $\ell^2$ makes its contribution a square. The two discriminant squareclasses are
\[
-G_5(5)G_5(-5)=-3600000000\sim-1,
\quad
-G_7(7)G_7(-7)=-188900999168\sim-2.
\tag{U-CONIC-REAL-DISCRIMINANTS}
\]
Equal-rank specialization changes a lattice discriminant by a square, so these different classes contradict the hypothetical rank $28$. Therefore the geometric Picard rank is $27$ and $\mathcal U$ has geometric Mordell–Weil rank zero.

Here is the correspondence with the required covers, retaining constants. For the $cm$ twist put $u=m+1/m$, $X=x/m^5$, $Y=y/[m^7(m+1)]$ in the model with $c=1$. The equation becomes
\[
(u+2)Y^2=X(X+u^4)(X+(16-3u^2)(u^2-16)).
\]
The two characters over $u$ give twists by $c(u+2)$ and $c(u-2)$. The change $u=2(w+1)/(w-1)$ rescales the roots by the square $16/(w-1)^4$ and gives twists $cw(w-1)$ and $c(w-1)$. Reciprocity identifies the former with the $-c(w-1)$ twist. Their geometric ranks vanish by the preceding result. Finally $M=(m-1)/(m+1)$ gives $p(M)=-1/p(m)$; scaling the original model by fourth and sixth powers of $p$ preserves it and turns the class $cM$ into $c(m^2-1)$. This proves geometric anti-rank zero for both real branch-pair families.

**The branch pair $1\pm\sqrt2$.** Let $h=m^2-2m-1$ and work temporarily over $K=\mathbb Q(i)(p)$. Write $\delta_\pm=(p+1)(p\pm i)$. The exact identities
\[
\frac{h(m)(m\pm i)^2}{m^2\delta_\pm(p(m))}
=\mp i\left(\frac{1-m^2}{m}\right)^2
\tag{U-CONIC-MIXED-CONSTANTS}
\]
show that $\mathbb Q(i)(m,\sqrt{ch})/K$ is biquadratic with characters $\beta,-ic\delta_+,ic\delta_-$. The two new eigenspaces are conjugate. It suffices to exclude rational sections on every required constant $-ic$ twist of
\[
\mathcal V:y^2=x(x+\delta_+\beta^2)(x+\delta_+\alpha\gamma).
\]
This surface has two $I_4^*$ at $p=-1,-i$, two $I_4$ at $1,i$, four $I_2$ at $\alpha\gamma=0$, and smooth infinity fiber $y^2=x(x+1)(x-3)$. Its trivial rank is $28$ and residual dimension six.

The resolved surface has good reduction at every Gaussian prime away from $2,3$. All discriminants and pairwise resultants of $p\pm1,p\pm i,\alpha,\gamma$ have this support, as do all initial coefficients in the root contacts. The orders of $(\delta\beta^2,\delta\alpha\gamma,\delta(\beta^2-\alpha\gamma))$ at $-1,-i,1,i$ are respectively
\[
(1,1,3),\quad(3,1,1),\quad(0,0,2),\quad(2,0,0).
\]
Their unit leading coefficients give the same successive resolutions away from $2,3$; the infinity root differences are $1,3,4$. Consequently any constant-character line supplied by a nontorsion section is unramified at every Gaussian prime outside $2,3$. For rational $c$ this requires
\[
c\in\{\pm1,\pm2,\pm3,\pm6\}\pmod{\mathbb Q^{*2}}.
\tag{U-CONIC-MIXED-SUPPORT}
\]
This conclusion is conditional on a nontorsion section, not an assertion that arbitrary conic constants have finite support.

At the Gaussian prime $(17,i-4)$, exact Weierstrass counts over degrees $1,2,3$ are $322,84554,24142978$. Including the smooth infinity fiber and removing the trivial representation gives traces $-2,454,-4418$. Newton identities and the nonzero middle coefficient fix
\[
F_{17}(T)=(T+17)^2(T^4-32T^3+574T^2-9248T+83521),
\quad F_{17}(17)=21381376\ne0.
\tag{U-CONIC-MIXED-FROBENIUS}
\]
For $c=\pm1,\pm2$, the constants $\pm ic$ are squares modulo this prime: $i=4$ and $-1,2$ are squares in $\mathbb F_{17}$. A section would therefore require the absent eigenvalue $+17$. The possible $-17$ eigenvalues are retained, so this is an arithmetic exclusion.

The remaining constants in (U-CONIC-MIXED-SUPPORT) do not give rational conics. For all finite $m\in\mathbb Q_3$, the valuation of $(m-1)^2-2$ is even: it is zero for integral $m-1$, and twice its valuation otherwise. Thus odd $v_3(c)$ makes $z^2=c((m-1)^2-2)$ insoluble. At infinity the conic would require $c$ to be a local square, again impossible. Both new eigenspaces consequently have arithmetic rank zero whenever the conic is rationally parameterizable. This last argument uses neither Tate nor Artin–Tate.

**From ranks to exact points.** In all cases just proved, the arithmetic anti-rank is zero. The anti-twist has an additive $I_{2k}^*$ fiber, so its torsion has exponent two by injection into the geometric component group. For $S\in E(N)$ this implies $2S\in E(F)$. Section 12.41 proves that restriction modulo two is injective for every geometrically rational quadratic cover of the $m$-line. Hence $S$ is already in $E(\mathbb C(m))$; intersecting its coordinate field with $N$ gives $S\in E(F)$. This proves exact group equality, including saturation and torsion, without confusing arithmetic rank zero with geometric rank zero.

Section 12.37 proves that every nonboundary old elliptic image has a positive-genus center cover. Such a cover cannot be dominated by the rational geometric base of any conic above. The exceptional charts $n=0,\infty,\pm1,\pm i$ require at least two independent squareclasses, as established in Section 12.41, and cannot acquire points in a quadratic extension. Therefore $C(N)=C(F)$, exactly the old 128 points.

Their count programs are `count_twist_frobenius.py`, `count_remaining_twist.py`, and `count_conjugate_branch_twist.py`; the last theorem uses `conjugate_branch_prime17.json`. Model, discriminant and cover substitutions are certified by the three `verify_*models`, `verify_remaining_discriminants`, and `verify_remaining_cover_maps` programs in the same directory. ### 12.43. Complete exclusion of graph-image quadratic rational families

Let $X$ be the full-root surface with its degree-thirty-two projection to the Segre quadric $\mathbb P^1_m\times\mathbb P^1_n$. Its generic five radicals are
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_0&=(1+m^2)(1+n^2),\\
F_\pm&=F_0\pm4n(1-m^2),\\
G_\pm&=F_0\pm4m(1-n^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
Its deck group is $V=(\mathbb Z/2)^5$. A rational curve here means a curve defined over $\mathbb Q$ with normalization $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$ and meeting the admissible locus.

**Theorem (quadratic graph exclusion).** There is no such rational curve whose $m$-map has degree two and whose projection to its image on the Segre quadric also has degree two. Equivalently, no nonboundary rational quadratic $m$-cover carries a full-root point with $n\in\mathbb Q(m)$.

The distinction from an arbitrary quadratic $m$-map is essential. If the curve maps birationally to its image on the quadric, $n$ need not lie in $\mathbb Q(m)$, and the theorem does not apply. That remaining case has $M=2$, $N$ even and $10\le N\le26$ by Section 12.40; it is not excluded here.

**Deck reduction and fifteen complete quotient determinations.** More generally, the degree $d$ of a rational curve over its image on the quadric is $2^k$, with its elementary two-group acting faithfully on its normalization. A nonidentity involution of $\mathbb P^1$ has exactly two fixed points, and its point stabilizers are cyclic. Riemann–Hurwitz therefore gives
\[
-2=2^k(-2+b/2),
\]
where $b$ is the number of branch points on the quotient. It follows that $d\in\{1,2,4\}$; also $d\mid\gcd(M,N)$. For $M=2,d=2$, the image is a graph $n=f(m)$ and its stabilizer has a unique nonzero sign vector
\[
v=(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_{f+},\epsilon_{f-},\epsilon_{g+},\epsilon_{g-}).
\]
The graph supplies a $\mathbb Q(m)$-point on the generic quotient $C/\langle v\rangle$.

Every quotient with
\[
\epsilon_{f+}+\epsilon_{f-}+\epsilon_{g+}+\epsilon_{g-}=0\pmod2
\tag{U-QGRAPH-EVEN}
\]
has exactly 64 rational function-field points, all boundary. To prove this even when the individual offset roots do not descend, put $d_0=1-m^2$, $r=2n/(1-n^2)$ and write the four edge roots as $f_\pm,g_\pm$. Then
\[
U=\frac{f_+f_-}{d_0(1-n^2)},\qquad
V=\frac{g_+g_-}{d_0(1-n^2)},\qquad
Z=(\alpha\beta r^2,\alpha\beta rUV)\in E.
\]
Condition (U-QGRAPH-EVEN) fixes $Z$. The exact old group is $E(F)=\mathbb ZP\oplus E[2](F)$, and $\beta$ is a square in $F$. The first Kummer coordinate of $P$ is $[\alpha]$, while those of $O,T_0,T_A,T_B$ are
\[
1,\quad[\alpha\gamma],\quad[-1],\quad[-\alpha\gamma].
\]
The classes $[-1],[\alpha],[\gamma]$ are independent: the latter two have disjoint simple zero divisors, and $F$ is formally real. Thus the class $[x(Z)]=[\alpha]$ forces $Z$ to be an odd multiple of $P$ with no torsion translate. Furthermore its center is already a square:
\[
\frac{\beta(1+r^2)}4
=\left(\frac{(1+m^2)(1+n^2)}{2(1-m^2)(1-n^2)}\right)^2.
\]
The complete old-center theorem forces $Z=\pm P$, hence $n=\pm m,\pm1/m$.

No omitted chart supplies extra quotient points. At $n=0,\infty$ the radical span is generated by $1+m^2,1+m^2+4m,1+m^2-4m$ and has rank three; at $n=\pm1$ the rank-three span is generated by $2(1+m^2),2(3-m^2),2(3m^2-1)$. Even after an order-two quotient their residue degree is at least four. Nonzero torsion images are excluded by the displayed Kummer coordinates, and $n=\pm i$ is not in $\mathbb P^1(F)$. At each of the four boundary values the 32 full-root points give exactly 16 quotient points, proving the count 64. There are fifteen nonzero vectors satisfying (U-QGRAPH-EVEN).

For reference, a weight-one involution on the generic fiber fixes 32 points, and all other involutions act freely there. Riemann–Hurwitz gives quotient genus 17 in the five weight-one cases and 25 in the remaining 26 cases. These fiber genera do not replace the surface fixed-locus argument that follows.

**Eight further directions have no surface fixed point.** Projection to the four corner-root coordinates is everywhere defined: if all four vanished, the magic equations would force every projective root coordinate to vanish. At a projective fixed point of a deck vector, the projective scalar is therefore $+1$, so every sign-changed root must be zero.

There is no common zero of three of $F_+,F_-,G_+,G_-$ anywhere on the quadric. Homogeneously, a simultaneous zero of $F_+,F_-$ requires $F_0=0$ and $N_0N_1(M_0^2-M_1^2)=0$. If $N_0N_1=0$, then $m=\pm i$ and both $G$ values are nonzero; if $M_0^2=M_1^2$, then $n=\pm i$ and again both $G$ values are nonzero. Interchanging $m,n$ handles the other pair. Every triple contains one of these pairs, including the infinity charts. Thus the eight vectors changing three edge signs, with either central sign, act freely on the full surface. They cannot preserve a rational curve nontrivially, since the two fixed points on its normalization would map to surface fixed points. This remains true if the image curve is singular.

Only eight directions remain: a single edge sign, or the center together with a single edge sign.

**Center plus one edge.** For a center-plus-$F$ vector the possible fixed $m$-values are $\pm1,\pm i$; the corresponding points on the quadric are $m=\pm1,n=\pm i$ and $m=\pm i,n=0,\infty$. For center-plus-$G$ the values are $0,\infty,\pm i$, with the transposed loci. A double cover has two distinct branch values, and their unordered pair is Galois stable. The initially possible pairs are therefore $\{1,-1\}$ or $\{i,-i\}$ in the first case, and $\{0,\infty\}$ or $\{i,-i\}$ in the second.

The rational branch values are impossible. At any such value the graph $n=f(m)$ takes a value in $\mathbb P^1(\mathbb Q)$, whereas the fixed locus requires $n=\pm i$. Hence all four directions require the field $F(\sqrt{c(1+m^2)})$, with its constant $c$ retained. Section 12.42 excludes every such conic cover, so these four directions give no nonboundary rational family.

**A single edge.** Each ramification point of the quadratic rational $m$-map has the same residue field as its branch value, of degree at most two. The changed edge root vanishes there. If the center is nonzero, the opposite root divided by the center is $\sqrt2$, so the field is exactly $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)$. If the center is zero, the zero edge gives $x=\pm y$ in normalized offset coordinates; a nonzero projective point then has remaining entries proportional to $x,-x,2x$. Their root ratios require both $i$ and $\sqrt2$, impossible in a quadratic field. Thus only $K$ can occur.

We determine all these zero-edge points over $K$. It is totally real, so the center is nonzero. Normalize its root to one. After offset sign changes, write the zero edge as $x+y=1$, and put $q=x$. The four corner conditions make
\[
q,\quad1-q,\quad1+q,\quad2-q
\]
squares in $K$. The first three yield a point on $E_1:Y^2=X^3-X$ with $X=-q$.

An elementary two-isogeny descent gives $\operatorname{rank}E_1(\mathbb Q)=0$: its scalar image is $\{1,-1\}$, and the dual $Y^2=X^3+4X$ has image $\{1,2\}$, with class 2 witnessed by $(2,4)$. The quadratic twist $E_2:Y^2=X^3-4X$ has image $\{1,-1,2,-2\}$. Its dual has only class 1, because class 2 would require $W^2=2U^4+8V^4$ with primitive $U,V$, whose residues modulo 16 are $2,8,10$. The rank formula gives $\operatorname{rank}E_2(\mathbb Q)=0$, hence $\operatorname{rank}E_1(K)=0$.

The good primes 7 and 17 split in $K$ and give elliptic counts 8 and 16, so torsion has order at most eight. All eight points are
\[
O,(0,0),(1,0),(-1,0),
\quad(1+\sqrt2,\pm(2+\sqrt2)),
\quad(1-\sqrt2,\pm(2-\sqrt2)).
\]
The last four double to $(1,0)$. Since a square in $K$ is nonnegative at both real embeddings, the possible values of $q$ reduce to $0,1$. Both give degenerate full-root points.

For these points the paired corner roots are $(\pm1,\pm1)$ and $(0,\pm\sqrt2)$, in either order. The inverse Segre formula
\[
m=\frac{-u+v+w-z}{u+v+w+z}
\]
has nonzero denominator and, over all 64 sign/order charts, gives precisely $m=\pm1\pm\sqrt2$. The only Galois-stable pairs are $\{1+\sqrt2,1-\sqrt2\}$ and its negative. Thus, up to $m\mapsto-m$, the required quadratic field is exactly (U-CONIC-MIXED). Rationality of its normalization requires $c$ to be a norm from $K$; equivalently the conic must have a rational point. Section 12.42 excludes every such cover. This removes the last four directions and proves the theorem.

**Scope and certificates.** A birational image on the quadric does not have a nontrivial deck stabilizer, so none is supplied artificially in that remaining case. The proof above neither excludes isolated rational points nor gives an absolute bound on $M$ or on denominators. Exact deck, fixed-locus and sign computations appear in `simultaneous_units/quadratic_multisection_deck_reduction.md` and its verifier. The branch-field reduction is `rank4_next/uniform_center_intersections/quadratic_branch_field_reduction.md` with `verify_quadratic_branch_reduction.py/.json`; the independent zero-edge review and replay are `simultaneous_units/zero_edge_quadratic_field_review.md` and `verify_zero_edge_quadratic_field.py/.json`. The final constant-twist exclusions use the separately audited calculations in Section 12.42.


### 12.44. One surviving test-fiber cover and a genus-three height target

At $m=2$, Section 12.39 leaves sixteen genus-769 twists with boundary lifts. They are all isomorphic over $\mathbb Q$. This gives a single remaining cover, with a useful genus-three quotient. Section 12.46 completes the rational-point determination using this quotient and the original square conditions.

**Rational isomorphisms among the twists.** Retain the notation of Section 12.38:
\[
A=1+m^2,\ B=4(1-m^2),\ c=B/2,\ d=B^2/A,
\quad\alpha=m^2-3,\ \gamma=1-3m^2,\quad Z=(u+v)^2,
\]
\[
f_1=Z-d,\qquad f_2=Z-2B.
\]
The functions $g_1,g_2$ are obtained at $m'=(m-1)/(m+1)$ and $h=(n-1)/(n+1)$, with the exact root transformations from Section 12.38. Four rational automorphisms of the full curve are: flipping $u$; flipping the first $G$ root $a$; replacing $n$ by $1/n$, dividing every root by $n$ and interchanging the divided $a,b$; and replacing $n$ by $-n$ and interchanging $u,v$.

For the first automorphism $F$, the $g_i$ are fixed and
\[
f_1(FP)f_1(P)=(-\alpha\gamma)(2B/A)^2,
\quad
f_2(FP)f_2(P)=(c\gamma A)(4\sigma/A)^2.
\]
It therefore adds the full $T_0$ class to the $f$ pattern. The analogous $G$ flip does so for the $g$ pattern. For the reciprocal automorphism $I$, the $g_i$ are unchanged and
\[
f_1(IP)f_1(P)=\alpha\gamma\left(\frac Z{An}\right)^2,
\quad
f_2(IP)f_2(P)=-\gamma A
\left(\frac{2\sigma(u+v)}{An}\right)^2.
\]
The class added is exactly $\delta(P')\delta(Q')$. The negative-$n$ automorphism fixes the $f$ functions and makes the corresponding reciprocal change in $h$, giving the same addition in the $g$ pattern.

These are actual isomorphisms of covers. If $f(P)f(\tau P)=k b(P)^2$, the source equation is $z^2=f(P)/h_0$, and the target constant is $h_1$ with $h_0k/h_1$ square in $\mathbb Q$, then
\[
z'=\sqrt{h_0k/h_1}\,\frac{b(P)}{h_0z}
\]
satisfies $(z')^2=f(\tau P)/h_1$. Applying this in each affected coordinate gives an invertible function-field map, hence an isomorphism of the complete smooth projective curves. Poles in the displayed coordinates do not delete points.

In the bit convention of Section 12.39 these four transformations add $1,16,12,192$ to the joint mask. They are independent and give sixteen orbits of size sixteen among all 256 twists, uniformly in the nonsingular rational base. The orbit of joint mask $68=(4,4)$ is exactly $S\times S$ with $S=\{4,5,8,9\}$. Thus all surviving covers at $m=2$ form one rational isomorphism class. The transformations preserve the boundary set. Existence of a nonboundary point on $C_2$ is consequently equivalent to existence of one on this single representative, still with every original radical retained.

**Why ordinary Chabauty on the original fiber cannot apply.** The Jacobian of $C_2$ has rank at least $53$, greater than its genus $49$. Here is an exact lower-bound proof for the ten genus-two character factors, supplementing the already proved elliptic contribution of at least $33$.

For an even separable sextic, the $x$-minus-root homomorphism has target $L^*/L^{*2}\mathbb Q^*$ and kills twice a divisor class [49]. Injectivity is not assumed. Its image dimension $d$ gives $r+\dim J(\mathbb Q)[2]\ge d$. A rational boundary point supplies a degree-one divisor, so the map is defined on the full rational Jacobian in the uses here.

Four isomorphic factors have model
\[
y^2=-75q_0q_1q_2,\quad q_0=x^2+1,
\quad q_1=x^2-12x/5+1,\quad q_2=x^2-13/3.
\]
The component fields are $\mathbb Q(i),\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11}),\mathbb Q(\sqrt{39})$. Relative to $(2,5)$, the point differences from $(-2,35),(1/2,35/8),(-1/2,245/8)$, and the two branch-pair torsion classes for $q_0,q_1$, give respectively
\[
(5,-1,13),\ (5,-1,3),\ (1,-11,39),\ (30,66,3),\ (30,-3,10).
\tag{U-C2-GENUS2-EVEN-IMAGES}
\]
For a branch pair $q_i$ in $f=a\prod q_i$, its self-coordinate is $-a\prod_{j\ne i}q_j(\theta_i)$; the other coordinates are $q_i(\theta_j)$. Indeed, at a branch point $\alpha$ the local parameter $y$ gives $x-\alpha=y^2/f'(\alpha)+\cdots$, and the other root $\beta$ of $q_i$ contributes $(\beta-\alpha)/f'(\alpha)=-1/[a\prod_{j\ne i}q_j(\alpha)]$. This fixes both sign and leading scalar.

On the prime basis $(-1,2,3,5,11,13)$ the relation space from diagonal rational constants and the three field kernels $-1,11,39$ has dimension nine. Adding (U-C2-GENUS2-EVEN-IMAGES) gives dimension thirteen, hence image dimension four. The rational two-torsion has dimension two, since the three quadratic splitting characters are independent. Each such factor has rank at least two.

The other six factors occur in three pairs of odd-degree models. Put $A=1+m^2$, $B=4(1-m^2)$, $C=4m$ and $Q(t)=(t+1)^2-(B^2/A^2)t$. The four-factor quotient is
\[
z^2=tA(t+1)A^2Q(t)((A-C)t+A+C),
\]
at $m=2$ or $1/3$; the five-factor quotient is
\[
z^2=A(t+1)A^2Q(t)((A-C)t+A+C)((A+C)t+A-C)
\]
at $m=2$. For $z^2=a\prod(t-\theta_i)$, the change $X=at,Y=a^2z$ makes the quintic monic. The ordinary-point images are $a(t-\theta_i)$, and at a rational branch point $r$ its self-coordinate is $\prod_{\theta_i\ne r}(r-\theta_i)$, with the omitted $a^4$ a square. No diagonal rational quotient occurs.

The rows below are the two boundary points at $t=m^2,1/m^2$ and the three rational branch points. The last component is quadratic.

| Model | Quadratic field | Five image vectors |
|---|---|---|
| Four factors, $m=2$ | $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11})$ | $(-15,-3,5,-15)$; $(-15,-3,5,165)$; $(-39,-15,65,15)$; $(15,3,5,110)$; $(-65,-5,13,-110)$ |
| Four factors, $m=1/3$ | $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{39})$ | $(-5,-2,10,30)$; $(-5,-2,10,-130)$; $(-11,-5,55,5)$; $(5,3,15,130)$; $(-55,-15,33,-5)$ |
| Five factors, $m=2$ | $\mathbb Q(\sqrt{11})$ | $(-39,65,-15,-195)$; $(-39,65,-15,2145)$; $(39,65,15,1430)$; $(-65,130,-2,-1430)$; $(-15,2,-30,30)$ |

The single relation generated by $11$ or $39$ in the quadratic component has dimension one; adding each five-row table gives dimension six. Image dimension five and rational two-torsion dimension three again give rank at least two. Exact rational and quadratic-field square identities verify every representative. Thus the ten factors contribute at least twenty, and
\[
\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Jac}(C_2)(\mathbb Q)\ge33+20=53.
\tag{U-C2-JACOBIAN-RANK-LOWER}
\]
This is a lower bound and a restriction on the ordinary Chabauty method, not a rational-point exclusion.

**A genus-three quotient of the surviving cover.** Select the $f$ and $g$ patterns both equal to $P'$. At $m=2$ the first two $f$ representatives are $5,15$. Writing $\eta_f=5r^2$, $\eta_f+264/5=15s^2$, $R=5r$, $S=5s$ and $Y=10Rn$ yields the necessary curve
\[
G:\qquad 3S^2-R^2=264,\qquad
Y^2=(R^2+44)(R^2+144).
\tag{U-C2-GENUS3-TARGET}
\]
It contains the boundary point $(6,10,120)$. Its cover of the $R^2$ line adjoins three independent roots with branch set $0,-264,-44,-144,\infty$; Riemann–Hurwitz gives genus three. A rational parametrization of its conic is
\[
R=\frac{6(3t^2-10t+1)}{3t^2-1},\qquad
S=\frac{-2(15t^2-6t+5)}{3t^2-1}.
\]
With $D=3t^2-1$ and $w=YD^2/24$ the hyperelliptic equation is
\[
w^2=(45t^4-135t^3+222t^2-45t+5)
(45t^4-60t^3+82t^2-20t+5).
\]
The degree-eight polynomial is squarefree. Its two rational infinities correspond to finite $R$ values; the four points at $R$-infinity are not rational, since $S/R$ would square to $1/3$. There is no rational point with $R=0$, $S=0$ or $Y=0$, directly from the conic and quartic equations.

The three positive-genus characters give the rational isogeny
$\operatorname{Jac}(G)\sim E_a\times E_b\times E_c$, with maps

| Target | $x$ | $y$ |
|---|---|---|
| $E_a:y^2=x(x+44)(x+144)$ | $R^2$ | $RY$ |
| $E_b:y^2=x(x-660)(x-360)$ | $3(R^2+264)=9S^2$ | $9SY$ |
| $E_c:y^2=x(x+660)(x+110)$ | $132+34848/R^2$ | $8712SY/R^3$ |

Their differential characters are distinct and exhaust the genus. Their exact ranks are $1,1,2$, respectively, proved by complete scalar two-isogeny descent. For $y^2=x(x^2+ax+b)$, a squarefree signed divisor class $d\mid b$ requires
$N^2=dU^4+aU^2V^2+(b/d)V^4$ with primitive $U,V$. The dual coefficients are $-2a,a^2-4b$.

| Curve | Original image | Dual image | Rank |
|---|---|---|---:|
| $E_a$ | $\langle-1,11\rangle$ | $\langle5\rangle$ | $1$ |
| $E_b$ | $\langle10,66\rangle$ | $\langle15\rangle$ | $1$ |
| $E_c$ | $\langle-1,6,10,11\rangle$ | $\{1\}$ | $2$ |

The lower images are witnessed by rational two-torsion and $(36,720)$ on $E_a$, $(20,240)$ on its dual, $(900,10800)$ on $E_b$, $(60,3600)$ on its dual, and $(1100,48400),(-600,4200)$ on $E_c$. All omitted support classes are excluded by the following complete residue table; signs impossible over $\mathbb R$ are omitted before the table. Both primitive projective charts $(1,t)$ and $(pt,1)$ are enumerated at the indicated prime powers.

| Model | Modulus | Excluded classes |
|---|---:|---|
| $E_a$ | $256$ | $\pm2,\pm6,\pm22,\pm66$ |

| $E_b$ | $243$ | $2,5,33,330$ |

The formula $2^r=|\alpha(E)|\,|\alpha(E')|/4$ proves the ranks and hence $\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Jac}(G)(\mathbb Q)=4$.

Both rank-one curves have exact torsion $C_2^2$. Good-prime counts at $7,13,17,19$ are $8,16,16,24$ for $E_a$ and $12,16,20,24$ for $E_b$; the root-difference criterion excludes halving the nonzero two-torsion on $E_a$. The full Kummer vectors of $P_a=(36,720)$ and $P_b=(900,10800)$ are $(1,5,5)$ and $(1,15,15)$. Neither lies in the torsion Kummer span: the third-coordinate torsion span is trivial for $E_a$ and $\langle-10,3\rangle$ for $E_b$. Thus these points generate odd-index subgroups modulo torsion. Their index is not asserted to be one. They suffice for the invariant rank-one ratio $h_p(P)/\log_E(P)^2$.

There is also an exact partial-lifting consequence. Set $r=[R^2+44]=[R^2+144]$. The first Kummer coordinate of both elliptic images is a square. The torsion first-coordinate lists are $1,-1,11,-11$ on $E_a$ and $1,10,66,165$ on $E_b$. Their complete rank-one groups modulo two force $r\in\{1,5\}$ and $3r\in\{1,15\}$, respectively. Hence
\[
(R^2+44)/5=L^2,\qquad(R^2+144)/5=M^2
\tag{U-C2-GENUS3-PARTIAL-LIFT}
\]
for rational $L,M$. With $n=Y/(10R)$, the formulas
\[
u=(M-24n/M)/2,\qquad v=(M+24n/M)/2
\]
recover the two $F$ roots. The center root still requires
\[
\sigma^2=5(1+n^2)=\frac{3S^2(R^2+24)}{20R^2},
\quad\text{equivalently }R^2+24\in15\mathbb Q^{*2}.
\]
The $G$ roots and the second Kummer pattern also remain to be imposed. A rational point on this genus-three quotient alone is therefore not a magic-square solution.

**Height-method scope.** The three rational elliptic factors give at least three independent rational Néron–Severi classes. Thus $r=4<g+\rho-1$ with $g=3$, $\rho\ge3$. Lemma 3.2 of [23] supplies finiteness of the level-two Chabauty–Kim set at a good prime. This is a valid finiteness hypothesis, not an evaluated set. Moreover the pullbacks of $O$ under the first two maps are the same divisor of four points over $R$-infinity, each once. Their invariant differentials pull back to $dR/Y$ and $dS/Y$. A height difference can consequently use these two rank-one factors without a correction for unequal pole divisors. Section 12.46 determines the necessary analytic zeros and excludes every extra full-root lift with an auxiliary-prime argument.

### 12.45. Exact common-root quadratic descent and exclusion of trace zero

After Section 12.43, a remaining rational curve with $m$-degree two maps birationally to its image on the Segre quadric. Set $K=\mathbb Q(m)$, $L=\mathbb Q(t)$, $[L:K]=2$, and let $\sigma$ be the involution. Then $n\notin K$ and $L=K(n)$. Its degree $N$ is even, with $10\le N\le26$. The following descent retains the actual five roots in this one field.

Put
\[
S=n+\sigma n,\quad T=n\sigma n,\quad
\Delta=S^2-4T,\quad w=n-\sigma n.
\]
Thus $n=(S+w)/2$, $w^2=\Delta$, and $\Delta$ is nonsquare in $K$. Its squareclass has exactly two geometric branch places, and its conic normalization has a rational point. Let $A=1+m^2$, $B=4(1-m^2)$, $C=4m$. For any of the five quadratics $q_i(n)=a_i n^2+b_i n+c_i$, write its actual root as $z_i=(H_i+J_iw)/2$. The square equations are exactly
\[
H_iJ_i=a_iS+b_i,\qquad
H_i^2+\Delta J_i^2=2a_i(S^2-2T)+2b_iS+4c_i,
\tag{U-QTRACE-ACTUAL-ROOTS}
\]
where the five triples are
\[
(A,0,A),\ (A,B,A),\ (A,-B,A),\ (A-C,0,A+C),\ (A+C,0,A-C).
\]
These ten equations are equivalent to the common-root requirement; they permit zero traces and zero anti-invariant parts and divide by neither. Separate norm-square equations would be weaker. Explicitly, with $V=(T-1)^2+S^2$ and $D=(T+1)^2-S^2$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
N(F_0)&=A^2V,\\
N(F_\pm)&=A^2V+B^2T\pm ABS(T+1),\\
N(G_\pm)&=A^2V+C^2D\pm2AC(1-T^2).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-QTRACE-NORMS}
\]
For example, if $S=0$ the central norm is automatically square, whereas the central root still requires $[A(1-T)]$ to be either $1$ or $[\Delta]$. Equation (U-QTRACE-ACTUAL-ROOTS) keeps this condition.

**Only seven actual traces before exclusion.** Set $p=2m/(1-m^2)$, $r=2n/(1-n^2)$ and retain $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$. The actual roots supply
\[
U=\frac{f_+f_-}{(1-m^2)(1-n^2)},\quad
V_1=\frac{g_+g_-}{(1-m^2)(1-n^2)},\quad
Z=(\alpha\beta r^2,\alpha\beta rUV_1)=2Q+P
\]
for an actual point $Q\in E(L)$. The offset identification of Section 12.29 gives this preimage over $L$, unique up to the old two-torsion.

The degree of the resulting rational $p$-cover is $e=4$. Section 12.40 gives
\[
h_L(Q),h_L(Q+P)\le6e+r_0/2+r_o\le26,
\qquad h_L(P)=6,
\]
because $r_0+r_o\le e-2=2$. The height here is the Shioda pairing. Write $Q+\sigma Q=kP+T_0$ using the exact arithmetic group over $K$. Galois invariance and Cauchy–Schwarz give
\[
6k^2\le4h_L(Q)\le104,\qquad
6(k+2)^2\le4h_L(Q+P)\le104.
\]
Hence $-4\le k\le2$. Doubling kills $T_0$, proving
\[
Z+\sigma Z=2jP,\qquad j\in\{-3,-2,-1,0,1,2,3\}.
\tag{U-QTRACE-SEVEN}
\]
No rank hypothesis on the new cover enters this finite trace restriction.

For a useful necessary elimination equation, put $a=\alpha\beta$, $A_E=\beta^2+\alpha\gamma$, $B_E=\beta^2\alpha\gamma$. The two abscissae have sum and product
\[
\Sigma=\frac{4a\{S^2(1+T^2)-2T(T+1)^2\}}{D^2},
\qquad \Pi=\frac{16a^2T^2}{D^2}.
\]
For $j=1,2,3$, write $c_j=x(2jP)$. The addition biquadratic is
\[
(\Pi-B_E)^2-2c_j\{\Sigma(\Pi+B_E)+2A_E\Pi\}
+c_j^2(\Sigma^2-4\Pi)=0.
\tag{U-QTRACE-ADDITION}
\]
It is necessary for either signed trace with that abscissa. It does not replace the signed group equation or the ten actual-root equations: sign elimination and clearing denominators can introduce extra solutions.

**An exact auxiliary elliptic group.** The trace-zero exclusion uses
\[
E_C:y^2=x(x+\beta)(x-\alpha p^2),
\qquad P_C=(p^2\beta,2p^2\beta\sqrt\beta),
\qquad T_B=(\alpha p^2,0),
\tag{U-QTRACE-CENTER-FACTOR}
\]
where $\sqrt\beta=(1+m^2)/(1-m^2)$. Its complete arithmetic group is
\[
E_C(K)=\mathbb ZQ_C\oplus C_2^2,
\qquad 2Q_C=P_C,\qquad h_K(Q_C)=1,
\tag{U-QTRACE-CENTER-GROUP}
\]
and a point whose three Kummer coordinates are $[\alpha,1,\alpha]$ lies exactly in $\mathbb ZP_C+T_B$.

Here is the rank and saturation justification. Put $z=p^2$ and descend to $y^2=x(x+z+1)(x-z(z-3))$. The biquadratic extension $K/\mathbb Q(z)$ has characters $z,z+1$. The four twist ranks for $1,z,z+1,z(z+1)$ are respectively $0,0,1,0$. The untwisted rational elliptic surface has geometric rank one, with free-line character $\chi_{-2}$ witnessed by $(-2z,\sqrt{-2}\,z(z-1))$, so its arithmetic rank is zero. The $z+1$ twist is a K3 surface with root rank seventeen and the nontorsion point $(z(z+1)^2,2z(z+1)^3)$, giving exact rank one.

The two other twists have root rank seventeen. For the $z$ twist, independent good reductions at $5,7$ leave residual polynomials $(T-5)(T^2+2T+25)$ and $(T-7)(T^2+6T+49)$. The K3 discriminant argument of Section 12.32, with [43]–[44], gives incompatible classes $-6,-10$ if characteristic-zero Picard rank were twenty; hence its geometric rank is zero. The $z(z+1)$ twist has residual polynomial $(T+5)(T^2-2T+25)$ at 5, while all nineteen trivial classes have eigenvalue $+5$. Absence of another $+5$ proves arithmetic rank zero. Its geometric rank is not inferred. The resolved good models have branch contacts with unit leading coefficients away from $2,3$; the full local models and independent counts are recorded in the certificates below.

The half-generator has
\[
x(Q_C)=\frac{2m(m^2+1)(3m^2-1)}{(m-1)^4(m+1)^2},
\quad
y(Q_C)=\frac{-2m(m^2+1)(3m^2-1)(m^2+2m-1)^2}
{(m-1)^6(m+1)^4}.
\]
Exact duplication gives $2Q_C=P_C$. On the $z+1$ twist the point has height one: its component corrections are $3/2,1,1/2$ at $-1,\infty,0$, with zero intersection with $O$. The degree-four base change gives $h_K(P_C)=4$ and $h_K(Q_C)=1$. The $m$-surface has ten $I_4$ and four $I_2$ fibers, so all section heights belong to $\frac14\mathbb Z$. A nonprimitive $Q_C$ could only be twice a generator modulo torsion. But every torsion translate of $Q_C$ has odd first-coordinate valuation at $m=0$, excluding divisibility by two. Geometric torsion has exponent dividing four from this fiber configuration, and no nonzero rational two-torsion can be halved: that would require one of $\alpha,-\alpha,-1$ to be a square. Hence the exact rational torsion is $C_2^2$.

Finally the odd $m=0$ valuation forces the free coefficient of any point with Kummer vector $[\alpha,1,\alpha]$ to be even. Independence of $\alpha,-1$ determines its torsion translate uniquely as $T_B$. This proves the asserted coset, without requiring $r$ itself to be rational over $K$.

**Exclusion of trace zero.** If $j=0$, then $\sigma Z=-Z$. Equality of abscissae and $n\notin K$ give exactly
\[
\sigma n=-n,\qquad \sigma n=1/n,
\qquad\text{or}\qquad\sigma n=-1/n.
\]
The last has $T=-1$, so (U-QTRACE-NORMS) gives $N(F_0)=A^2\Delta$, a nonsquare. It is impossible for an actual squared root norm.

First suppose $\sigma n=-n$. The two $F$ roots are exchanged with the same sign, so $U$ is invariant. As $r$ is anti-invariant and the signed image $Z$ is anti-invariant, $V_1$ is invariant as well. Also $W=(1+n^2)/(1-n^2)$ is invariant. Their equations are
\[
U^2=\alpha r^2+\beta,\qquad V_1^2=\beta r^2+\gamma,
\qquad W^2=1+r^2.
\]
They give the actual point
\[
C_0=\left(\frac{\alpha\beta(1+r^2)}4,
\frac{\alpha\beta UV_1W}8\right)\in E_C(K),
\]
whose Kummer vector is $[\alpha,1,\alpha]$. Thus $C_0=kP_C+T_B$.

There is a small multiplier cutoff without knowing any generators on $L$. Put $d=1-m^2$, $a=-3m^4+10m^2-3$, $b=(1+m^2)^2$. The global minimal $m$-model has $X=d^4x$ and $\chi=4$, giving
\[
X(C_0)=ab(1+r^2)/4,\qquad
h_K(C_0)\le8+h_m(X(C_0))\le16+2N\le68.
\]
Indeed $\deg_t r=2N$, $r^2\in K$ and $[L:K]=2$ imply $\deg_m(r^2)=2N$. Finite negative valuations of $X$ give twice the intersection with $O$; the minimal infinity coordinate $m^{-8}X$ can only lower that contribution. Since $h_K(P_C)=4$, this proves $|k|\le4$.

Define $q_k=4x(kP_C+T_B)/(\alpha\beta)-1$. Negative $k$ gives the same abscissa. Exact addition, substitution $z=4m^2/(1-m^2)^2$, and squarefree decomposition yield:

| $|k|$ | Odd divisor places over the $m$-line | Quadratic cover |
|---:|---:|---|
| $0$ | $4$ | genus $1$ |
| $1$ | $0$ | split, $q_1=p^2$ |
| $2$ | $20$ | genus $9$ |
| $3$ | $36$ | genus $17$ |
| $4$ | $68$ | genus $33$ |

For example, $q_0=(3z-1)/(z+1)$, and
\[
q_2=\frac{(3z^2+6z-1)(z^3+7z^2-z+9)}{(z+1)(z^2-6z-3)^2},
\]
\[
q_3=\frac{(z^4-4z^3+54z^2+28z-15)(z^5+4z^4+6z^3-4z^2+33z+24)}
{(z^2-2z-7)^2(3z^2+2z+3)^2}.
\]
For $q_4$, the numerator is the product of degree-eight and degree-nine polynomials in $z$, and the denominator is $(z+1)$ times a squared degree-eight polynomial; their complete coefficients are in the finite certificate. After substitution, the odd numerator degrees for $k=2,3,4$ are respectively $(4,4,6,6)$, $(8,8,10,10)$, $(16,16,18,18)$. All denominator and infinity valuations are even, and all odd factors are squarefree and pairwise coprime. Independent division-polynomial calculations reproduce these degrees without importing the addition code.

The nonzero anti-invariant $r$ generates $L=K(\sqrt{q_k})$. Positive genus contradicts $L=\mathbb Q(t)$ in four cases; the split case contradicts $r\notin K$. This exhausts $\sigma n=-n$.

For $\sigma n=1/n$, the original $r,U,V_1,W$ are all anti-invariant. Apply $m'=(m-1)/(m+1)$, $n'=(n-1)/(n+1)$. The five radicands transform by the common square $4/((m+1)^2(n+1)^2)$ and permutation $(0,4,3,2,1)$. Moreover
\[
p'=-1/p,\quad r'=-1/r,\quad
U'=V_1/(pr),\quad V_1'=U/(pr),\quad W'=W/r.
\]
Thus $U',V_1',W'$ are invariant, $r'$ is anti-invariant, and the transformed signed elliptic image is anti-invariant. This verifies the trace-zero hypothesis after transformation, in addition to $\sigma n'=-n'$. Both map degrees are preserved, so the preceding exclusion applies. The identities are in function fields and lose no projective denominator chart.

Consequently every remaining nongraph rational quadratic family must satisfy
\[
\boxed{Z+\sigma Z\in\{\pm2P,\pm4P,\pm6P\}.}
\tag{U-QTRACE-NONZERO-ONLY}
\]
**Sharper degrees for each remaining trace.** Let $A_-=Q-\sigma Q$, so the invariant and anti-invariant height components are orthogonal. Since $Q+\sigma Q=(j-1)P+T_0$ and $h_L(P)=6$, the two height bounds with $B_0=24+r_0/2+r_o$ give
\[
h_L(A_-)\le4B_0-6(|j|+1)^2,\qquad
h_L(Z)=6j^2+h_L(A_-)\le4B_0-12|j|-6.
\]
The lower bound from Section 12.40 is $h_L(Z)\ge4N-12-2r_\alpha-r_\gamma$. Combining them with $r_0+r_o+r_\alpha+r_\gamma\le2$ gives
\[
4N\le102-12|j|+2r_0+4r_o+2r_\alpha+r_\gamma
\le110-12|j|.
\]
As $N$ is even, the remaining ranges are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
|j|&1&2&3\\\hline
N&10,12,\ldots,24&10,12,\ldots,20&10,12,\ldots,18.
\end{array}
\tag{U-QTRACE-DEGREE-REFINEMENT}
\]
In particular $N=26$ is excluded entirely, and the root degree in this quadratic stratum is at most $26$. The six signed systems in these smaller ranges remain unresolved. The finite trace list and bounded map degrees are not a bound on rational coefficient heights or on isolated point denominators.

The auxiliary group is proved in `coupled_lifts/center_triple_factor.md`, with symbolic and twist-count programs, and independently audited in `rank4_next/beta_twist_audit/center_triple_rank_review.md`. The finite genus calculation is `coupled_lifts/trace_zero_center_sections.py/.json`; the independent division-polynomial replay is `next_pythagorean_cover/verify_trace_zero_center_independent.py/.json`. ### 12.46. Complete rational-point determination of the test fiber

**Theorem (complete test fiber).** The smooth projective curve
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sigma^2&=5(n^2+1),\\
u^2&=5n^2-12n+5,&v^2&=5n^2+12n+5,\\
a^2&=13-3n^2,&b^2&=13n^2-3
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-C2-COMPLETE-EQUATIONS}
\]
has exactly 128 rational points. They are the independent five-root sign choices above $n=2,-2,1/2,-1/2$. Thus the fiber $m=2$ has no admissible magic-square point. This is a complete fixed-fiber theorem, not a denominator bound or a statement about every rational base.

**A short descent to the genus-three target.** The proof can use one of the two elliptic descents rather than the full joint cover. Set $D=5(1+n^2)$ and $\eta=2D-144/5+2uv$. The first three roots give
\[
(\eta,2\sigma\eta)\in E':y^2=x(x+264/5)(x+24/5).
\]
The integral model $Y^2=X(X+1320)(X+120)$ has exact rank two by Section 12.39. With roots ordered $0,-1320,-120$, the four actual Kummer basis vectors for the two torsion points and two boundary points are
\[
(11,330,30),\quad(-330,110,-3),\quad
(5,15,3),\quad(-55,33,-15).
\]
Assign them masks $1,2,4,8$. They span the full sixteen-element image. Complete reductions of all five original roots give these possible masks:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l}
19&2,3,4,5,8,9,14,15\\
23&4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11.
\end{array}
\]
Their intersection is $\{4,5,8,9\}$. These are good reductions, including all zero-root and infinity charts; Section 12.39 supplies the exhaustive certificates.

Changing the sign of $u$ adds mask $1$. The rational automorphism
\[
n\mapsto1/n,\qquad
(\sigma,u,v,a,b)\mapsto(\sigma,u,v,b,a)/n
\]
adds mask $12$. The exact square multipliers are proved in Section 12.44. These operations preserve every root equation and the boundary set, and act transitively on the four masks. Every hypothetical point can therefore be normalized to mask $4$. Writing $\eta=5r^2$, $\eta+264/5=15s^2$, $R=5r$, $S=5s$, $Y=10Rn$ gives
\[
G:\quad 3S^2-R^2=264,\qquad
Y^2=(R^2+44)(R^2+144),\qquad n=Y/(10R).
\tag{U-C2-COMPLETE-GENUS3}
\]
All five equations (U-C2-COMPLETE-EQUATIONS) remain necessary at this $n$. There is no rational $R=0$ point, since $6336$ is nonsquare, or rational $R$-infinity point, since the conic would require $\sqrt3$. Thus this reduction loses no rational chart.

It remains to prove that the only rational points of (U-C2-COMPLETE-GENUS3) satisfying those five square conditions are
\[
(R,S,Y)=(\pm6,\pm10,\pm120).
\tag{U-C2-COMPLETE-EIGHT}
\]
We do not assert that these exhaust the larger set $G(\mathbb Q)$ without the five square conditions.

**Compatible quadratic heights.** Use the rank-one curves and maps of Section 12.44:
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_a&:y^2=x(x+44)(x+144),&P_a&=(R^2,RY),&A&=(36,720),\\
E_b&:y^2=x(x-660)(x-360),&P_b&=(3(R^2+264),9SY),&B&=(900,10800).
\end{aligned}
\]
Both have exact rank one and torsion $C_2^2$. The points $A,B$ need not be primitive to compute their height-to-logarithm ratios.

Here the local and global normalizations are explicit. Fix $\log_{13}(13)=0$. For $y^2=x^3+a_2x^2+a_4x$, put $t=-x/y$ and $X=x+a_2/3$. Let $z$ be the elliptic logarithm for $dx/(2y)$, and take the algebraic short-Weierstrass sigma series, with $\Sigma(z)=z+O(z^5)$, $\zeta=d\log\Sigma/dz$, $d\zeta/dz=-X$. On the formal group set $\lambda_{13}=-2\log_{13}\Sigma$. The universal addition and multiplication identities are [50]
\[
\frac{\Sigma(z+w)\Sigma(z-w)}{\Sigma(z)^2\Sigma(w)^2}=x(w)-x(z),
\qquad \Sigma(2z)=-2y(z)\Sigma(z)^4.
\tag{U-C2-SIGMA-IDENTITIES}
\]
These rational formal identities hold for the convergent $13$-adic series. Since both reductions have order $16$, every local point enters the formal group after multiplication by $16$. With the corresponding division polynomial, extend by
\[
\lambda_{13}(P)=\frac{\lambda_{13}(16P)+2\log_{13}\psi_{16}(P)}{256}.
\tag{U-C2-LOCAL-HEIGHT-EXTENSION}
\]
The simultaneous zero at a nonzero $16$-torsion point cancels, giving the analytic continuation. This is the algebraic sigma splitting; no unit-root splitting is assumed.

At each finite $q\ne13$, use the doubled, model-dependent height
\[
\lambda_q(P)=\bigl(\max(0,-v_q(x(P)))-\mu_q(P)\bigr)\log_{13}(q),
\]
with the homogeneous duplication correction $\mu_q$ of [24]. Its near-origin normalization is $2v_q(t)\log_{13}(q)$, with no discriminant constant. Its duplication identity is
$\lambda_q(2P)=4\lambda_q(P)+2v_q(2y(P))\log_{13}(q)$.
The sigma parallelogram identity has right side $-2\log_{13}(x(P)-x(Q))$, while the finite identity has right side $2v_q(x(P)-x(Q))\log_{13}(q)$. The rational product formula cancels them. Hence
\[
h(P)=\lambda_{13}(P)+\sum_{q\ne13}\lambda_q(P)
\]
is an even quadratic height on $E(\mathbb Q)$ and vanishes on torsion. Rank one therefore gives
\[
h_a(P)=\alpha_a\ell_a(P)^2,\quad \alpha_a=h_a(A)/\ell_a(A)^2,
\qquad
h_b(P)=\alpha_b\ell_b(P)^2,\quad \alpha_b=h_b(B)/\ell_b(B)^2.
\]
Changing $\Sigma$ by $\exp(cz^2)\Sigma$ changes a local height and its $\alpha$ by the same quadratic-logarithm term. Thus the function
\[
\rho=\lambda_{13}(P_a)-\lambda_{13}(P_b)
-\alpha_a\ell_a(P_a)^2+\alpha_b\ell_b(P_b)^2
\tag{U-C2-HEIGHT-FUNCTION}
\]
is unchanged. The two identity divisors pull back to the same four points, so there is no extra nonconstant rational-log term.

**Complete finite local levels.** Put $W_q=(\lambda_q(P_a)-\lambda_q(P_b))/\log_{13}(q)$. The exhaustive values are
\[
W_2=W_{11}=0,\quad W_3=\tfrac12,\qquad
W_5=\begin{cases}0&R\equiv\pm2\pmod5,\\1/4&R\equiv\pm1\pmod5,
\end{cases}
\]
and $W_q=0$ at all other $q\ne13$. Consequently rational points have only the two levels
\[
L_0=-\tfrac12\log_{13}3,\qquad
L_b=-\tfrac12\log_{13}3-\tfrac14\log_{13}5.
\tag{U-C2-HEIGHT-LEVELS}
\]

The complete domain and tail justification is as follows. At $2$, the conic excludes nonintegral and odd $R$, and valuations at least two; writing $R=2r$ the quartic then forces $r\equiv\pm3\pmod{16}$. Thus $R\in\pm6+32\mathbb Z_2$. At $3$ one obtains exactly $v_3(R)=1$. At $5$ nonunits and negative valuations are excluded; for $R\equiv\pm1$ the conic requires $R^2\equiv11\pmod{25}$, so the two abscissae lie in $11+25\mathbb Z_5$ and $25\mathbb Z_5$. For $R\equiv\pm2$ both corrections vanish. At $11$, positive $v_{11}(R)$ is impossible; unit abscissae are nonsingular and nonintegral abscissae have equal valuations, with zero corrections. At every other good prime the same denominator cancellation applies.

For the indicated balls, the homogeneous forms
\[
\Delta_1=(X^2-bZ^2)^2,\qquad
\Delta_2=4XZ(X^2+aXZ+bZ^2)
\]
give the following nonzero correction prefixes and totals:

| Prime | Prefix for $E_a$ | $\mu_a$ | Prefix for $E_b$ | $\mu_b$ |
|---:|---|---:|---|---:|
| $2$ | $8$ | $2$ | $8$ | $2$ |
| $3$ | $4$ | $1$ | $6$ | $3/2$ |
| $5$, $R\equiv\pm1$ | $2,4$ | $3/4$ | $4$ | $1$ |

The polynomial ball calculation removes these common valuations uniformly, checks primitivity for every residue, and follows the entire projective residue orbit thereafter. No subsequent simultaneous zero occurs, so each remaining correction tail is identically zero on the whole ball. This is not a sample of local points. It also covers the locally possible $S=0$ branch at $5$ and all nonintegral charts at other primes.

**The complete $13$-adic domain.** Direct enumeration of $G$ modulo $13$ gives sixteen affine and four infinity points. Only the eight reductions (U-C2-COMPLETE-EIGHT) satisfy the necessary original root conditions. The four $S=0$ points map to $n=\pm5$ and fail an original root test; the four $Y=0$ points map to $n=0$ with nonsquare central residue $5$. The infinity points fail the corresponding scaled central condition. Although the original full curve has bad reduction at $13$, this direct argument is sufficient: if $n$ is nonintegral then $\sigma^2/n^2$ has nonsquare residue $5$; nonintegral $R$ forces nonintegral $n$, and there is no $R=0$ point of $G(\mathbb F_{13})$. Thus every possible rational lift lies in one of the eight indicated affine disks.

Independent signs in $R,S,Y$ negate the two elliptic images independently and leave $\rho$ unchanged. It suffices to study
\[
R=6+13T,\quad S\equiv10,\quad Y\equiv120\pmod{13},
\quad T\in\mathbb Z_{13}.
\tag{U-C2-HEIGHT-DISK}
\]
The two roots $S,Y$ are unique analytic functions there, and $R$ is a local coordinate.

**Exact leading coefficients.** Four rational doublings of $A,B$ give $v_{13}(t(16A))=v_{13}(t(16B))=1$. The formulas $\ell=t+O(t^3)$, $\lambda=-2\log t+O(t^2)$ on the formal group and
\[
\lambda(P)=\lambda(16P)/256
+2\sum_{j=0}^3\frac{\log_{13}(2y(2^jP))}{4^{j+1}}
\]
reduce the leading constants to Fermat quotients modulo $169$. The result, with every entry taken modulo $13$, is

| Quantity | At $A$ | At $B$ |
|---|---:|---:|
| $\ell(P)/13$ | $10$ | $7$ |
| $\lambda_{13}(P)/13$ | $12$ | $2$ |
| $h(P)/13$ | $4$ | $8$ |
| $13\alpha$ | $12$ | $6$ |
| $\zeta(P)$ | $3$ | $10$ |

In particular both $\alpha$ have valuation $-1$. The zeta residues are also obtained independently from $\zeta(2P)=2\zeta(P)+(3x^2+2a_2x+a_4)/(2y)$ and $\zeta=1/t-a_2t/3+O(t^3)$ at the formal multiple. No fitted values enter these constants.

The pulled-back invariant differentials $dR/Y,dS/Y$ give
\[
\ell_a(P_a)/13\equiv10+9T,\qquad
\ell_b(P_b)/13\equiv7+7T\pmod{13}.
\]
As $d\lambda=-2\zeta\,d\ell$, the derivative of the local height difference with respect to $R$ is $8$ modulo $13$, and its value divided by $13$ at $T=0$ is $10$. Hence
\[
\rho/13\equiv10+8T-12(10+9T)^2+6(7+7T)^2
\equiv1+9T+11T^2\pmod{13}.
\]
The logarithms of $3,5$, divided by $13$, have residues $5,12$. Therefore
\[
\frac{\rho-L_0}{13}\equiv11T^2+9T+10,
\qquad
\frac{\rho-L_b}{13}\equiv11T^2+9T\pmod{13}.
\tag{U-C2-HEIGHT-POLYNOMIALS}
\]

**Whole-disk validity and exact zero count.** These are reductions of restricted integral power series on the entire disk, not just congruences at sampled points. Write $s=R-6$. The implicit square-root equations make $S,Y$ and the pulled-back differentials integral power series in $s$, with unit denominators. Since $d\zeta=-(x+a_2/3)d\ell$, one integration may introduce a denominator $k$. A second integration for $\lambda$ gives, after $s=13T$, the coefficient bound
\[
v_{13}([T^n](\lambda-\lambda(0)-13\lambda'(0)T))
\ge n-v_{13}(n)-\lfloor\log_{13}(n-1)\rfloor\ge2
\quad(n\ge2).
\tag{U-C2-HEIGHT-TAIL}
\]
The lower bound tends to infinity. The logarithm has the stronger bound $n-v_{13}(n)$ for its higher terms. Thus both discarded tails are divisible by $169$ and restricted; since $v_{13}(\alpha)=-1$, (U-C2-HEIGHT-POLYNOMIALS) holds coefficientwise in $\mathbb Z_{13}\langle T\rangle$.

For completeness, the local height is analytic even if $16P$ reaches zero inside the disk. The unique $16$-torsion lift $D$ of its elliptic residue point exists by the prime-to-$13$ étale multiplication map. In the formal coordinate of $P-D$, the division polynomial has a simple zero $tV(t)$ with $V$ an integral unit, and the sigma term is $16tU(t)$. The $\log t$ terms cancel in (U-C2-LOCAL-HEIGHT-EXTENSION). The formal coefficients of $\log U$ have valuation at least $-2\lfloor\log_{13}k\rfloor$, accounting for both integrations. On (U-C2-HEIGHT-DISK), coefficients of $t(T)^k$ in degree $q$ have valuation at least $\max(k,q)$. Their composition therefore has higher-degree valuation at least two and restricted convergence, independently confirming the analytic continuation and tail claim.

The first polynomial in (U-C2-HEIGHT-POLYNOMIALS) has no root in $\mathbb F_{13}$; its discriminant is the nonsquare $5$. The second has exactly two simple roots, $T=0,11$, with derivatives $9,4$. Hensel uniqueness gives exactly one zero in each corresponding residue disk and no others. The zero in $T\equiv0$ is the exact known boundary point $T=0$. Any other rational point would have
\[
R\equiv149\pmod{169},\qquad
\ell_a(P_a)/\ell_a(A)\equiv7\pmod{13},
\tag{U-C2-EXTRA-HEIGHT-BRANCH}
\]
or the negative coefficient after a sign change.

**An exact auxiliary-prime contradiction.** At $109$, every simultaneous square residue in the original five equations occurs at $n=\pm2,\pm1/2$, with nonzero roots. Exhausting $x_0=R^2$ using
\[
3S^2=x_0+264,\quad100x_0n^2=(x_0+44)(x_0+144),
\quad P_a=(x_0,10x_0n)
\]
leaves only $n=2,-2$ and $x_0=36$, so $P_a$ reduces to $\pm A$. This enumeration includes every possible rational lift: nonintegral $n$ is excluded by the nonsquare residue $13$ in $b^2/n^2$; nonintegral $R$ forces nonintegral $n$, and $109\mid R$ would likewise do so since $6336\not\equiv0$.

The elliptic group $E_a(\mathbb F_{109})$ has order $104=8\cdot13$, and $\bar A$ has order $13$. In particular the global rank-one index of $A$ is prime to $13$: a point in $13E_a(\mathbb Q)$ plus rational two-torsion has zero $13$-primary reduction. Writing $A=kG$ and $P_a=jG$ modulo torsion, with $13\nmid k$, shows that the logarithm ratio $j/k$ transports to the order-$13$ reduction without assuming full saturation.

Explicitly, $T_0=[8]\bar A=(43,88)$ has order $13$. The full-root reductions require
\[
[8]\bar P_a\in\{(43,88),(43,21)\}=\{T_0,-T_0\}.
\]
But (U-C2-EXTRA-HEIGHT-BRANCH) requires
\[
[8]\bar P_a\in\{(81,5),(81,104)\}=\{7T_0,-7T_0\},
\]
a disjoint set. This excludes the sole extra analytic branch, independently of its higher digits.

Only (U-C2-COMPLETE-EIGHT) remain. Their normalized $n$ values are $\pm2$; reversing the boundary-preserving normalization yields exactly $n=\pm2,\pm1/2$. Each has five nonzero rational square radicands, giving 32 independent signs and 128 points in total. Infinity would require $\sqrt5$, so no extra projective point is missing. This proves the theorem.

### 12.47. Three squareclass exclusions for the signed trace two cases

Within the remaining nongraph rational quadratic stratum of Section 12.45, the traces $Z+\sigma Z=\pm2P$ satisfy a sharper restriction. The half-trace has no nonzero two-torsion translate. These auxiliary groups alone do not exclude the last pattern; Section 12.48 completes its exclusion by a different finite elliptic reduction.

Write $K=\mathbb Q(m)$, $L=K(\sqrt D)$, $p=2m/(1-m^2)$, and retain $\alpha,\beta,\gamma$, $d_0=p^2-1$. Put $\kappa=p^4-6p^2+1$. Suppose first that $Z+\sigma Z=2P$. Then
\[
W=Z-P=2Q,\qquad \sigma W=-W,
\qquad M=x(W)\in K.
\]
We initially separate $W=O$ and $W\in E[2]$. Away from those cases the ordinate is nonzero and anti-invariant. Because $W$ is an actual double, the three functions $M,M+\beta^2,M+\alpha\gamma$ become squares in $L$. Their classes over $K$ are each $1$ or $D$, with odd product $D$. There are exactly four patterns, $100,010,001,111$, where a $1$ denotes class $D$.

**An exact center-norm condition.** The center function is $H(Z)=(x(Z)+\alpha\beta)/(4\alpha)$ and is an actual square in $L$. Writing $s=x(P)=\alpha\beta p^2$, the addition law gives
\[
H(W+P)H(-W+P)
=\frac{\beta^4(M+\beta^2)(M+\kappa^2/\beta^2)}{16(M-s)^2}.
\tag{U-TRACE2-CENTER-NORM}
\]
The constant $\beta^4/16$ is retained and is square. Thus the product of the two displayed linear factors is a square in $K$. The possible pole chart $M=s$ would make $W=\pm P$ old and nontorsion, inconsistent with anti-invariance. A zero factor would make an actual center zero and is outside the admissible stratum. As a divisor check, $x(P+T_A)=-\alpha\beta$, $x(2P+T_A)=-\kappa^2/\beta^2$, and the value at $W=O$ is $H(P)^2=\beta^4/16$.

**Two extremal auxiliary groups.** Set $a=\beta^2$, $b=\alpha\gamma$, $d=\kappa^2/\beta^2$. The identities
\[
a-b=4d_0^2,\qquad d-b=4d_0^4/\beta^2,
\qquad a-d=16p^2d_0^2/\beta^2
\]
give an exact isomorphism
\[
J:Y^2=(M+a)(M+b)(M+d)
\ \cong\ J_*:y^2=x(x+\beta^2)(x+d_0^2),
\]
\[
x=\frac{\beta^2(M+b)}{4d_0^2},\qquad
y=\frac{\beta^3Y}{8d_0^3}.
\tag{U-TRACE2-FIRST-AUXILIARY}
\]
Over the $p$-line the discriminant of $J_*$ is $256p^4\beta^4d_0^4$, giving six $I_4$ fibers at $0,\infty,\pm1,\pm i$, with unit $c_4$ at each. The surface is K3 and its trivial lattice has rank $20=h^{1,1}$, so its geometric Mordell–Weil rank is zero. On the beta-square $m$-cover, ramification only at $p=\pm i$ gives $2I_8+8I_4$, with $\chi=4$ and trivial rank $40=h^{1,1}$. Its geometric rank stays zero.

The second group is
\[
J_0:Y^2=M(M+a)(M+d).
\tag{U-TRACE2-SECOND-AUXILIARY}
\]
Put $q=2p/(1-p^2)$ and $\lambda=d_0^2/\beta$. Then $\lambda^2(q^2+1)^2=a$ and $\lambda^2(q^2-1)^2=d$, so $J_0$ is the scaled pullback of $J_*(q)$. The composite degree-four $m\mapsto q$ cover is totally ramified above $\pm i$ and otherwise unramified. Its fibers are $2I_{16}+16I_4$, with $\chi=8$ and trivial rank $80=h^{1,1}$. Again the geometric rank is zero. These rank conclusions follow directly from fiber configurations and the Hodge bound, without specialization assumptions or point counts.

Both arithmetic groups over $K$ are exactly $C_4\times C_2$. For $y^2=x(x+u^2)(x+v^2)$ the four halves of $(0,0)$ have $x=\pm uv$. The other two-torsion points cannot halve over the formally real field $K$, since a relevant Kummer coordinate is $-1$. On $J_*$ the order-four first coordinates have classes $\pm d_0$, since $\beta$ is square in $K$; on $J_0$ they have classes $\pm\kappa$. Each is nonsquare, with simple zero divisors on the $m$-line. Thus none can halve, excluding eight-torsion. Odd torsion is impossible: all fiber component groups are two-groups, and a nonzero torsion section meeting every identity component would have positive height $2\chi+2(R\cdot O)$. This determines the entire torsion, hence the entire rank-zero group.

Two exact consequences of the eight-point lists are needed. A finite $J(K)$ point with $M+b$ square must have $M=-b$: its corresponding first coordinate on $J_*$ is square, and among its eight points only $O,(0,0)$ qualify. The other two-torsion points have negative-square first coordinates, and the order-four points have classes $\pm d_0$. Also a $J_0(K)$ point with all three Kummer coordinates square lies in $2J_0(K)=\{O,(0,0)\}$; a finite such point has $M=0$. These torsion possibilities are retained rather than treating either list as empty.

**Excluding the three mixed patterns.** In pattern $100$, $M+a,M+b$ are squares; (U-TRACE2-CENTER-NORM) also makes $M+d$ square. This supplies a $J$ point with square $M+b$, forcing $M=-b$, contrary to the non-two-torsion chart. In pattern $010$, $M,M+b$ are squares and $(M+a)(M+d)$ is square, giving the same $J$ contradiction. In pattern $001$, $M,M+a,M+d$ are all squares, giving a $J_0$ point in its doubling image and forcing $M=0$, again two-torsion. Therefore necessarily
\[
\boxed{[M]=[M+\beta^2]=[M+\alpha\gamma]
=[M+\kappa^2/\beta^2]=[D].}
\tag{U-TRACE2-SURVIVING-CLASS}
\]
None of the four is square in $K$; all become square in the same quadratic field.

The separated old-torsion cases produce no additional nongraph family. If $W=2Q$ is old torsion, the uniform no-new-halves theorem of Section 12.41 forces $Q$ to be an old geometric section. Section 12.37 then excludes a nonboundary center on a rational base cover. Merely knowing that $W$ was old would not suffice; the actual halving condition is used.

**The exact half-trace.** Choose square roots $r_i^2=M-e_i$, with $r_1r_2r_3=-y(W)$ for the three roots of the original elliptic cubic. In (U-TRACE2-SURVIVING-CLASS) all three $r_i$ are anti-invariant. The halving formulas
\[
x(Q)=M+r_1r_2+r_2r_3+r_3r_1,
\]
\[
y(Q)=-y(W)-(r_1+r_2+r_3)(r_1r_2+r_2r_3+r_3r_1)
\]
make $x(Q)$ invariant and $y(Q)$ anti-invariant. An even number of root sign changes gives each of the four halves, so this applies to the actual $Q$. Thus
\[
Q+\sigma Q=O\quad\text{if }Z+\sigma Z=2P.
\tag{U-TRACE2-HALF-TRACE}
\]
Negating $Z$ preserves its abscissa, center and full-root conditions and replaces $Q$ by $-Q-P$. Therefore $Q+\sigma Q=-2P$ when $Z+\sigma Z=-2P$. All three previously possible nonzero two-torsion translates of these half-traces are excluded.

After these auxiliary tests the last pattern is still a genuine compatibility condition. Its three ratios $(M+a)/M,(M+b)/M,(M+d)/M$ must all be squares in $K$. This is a genus-one three-radical cover with rational points over $M=\infty$; it is not eliminated by the two extremal groups. Its quartic quotient is $Y^2=M(M+a)(M+b)(M+d)$, with cubic model isomorphic to $y^2=x(x-d_0^2)(x-\kappa^2/\beta^2)$. The dual two-isogenous model, after scaling, is $y^2=x(x+\alpha^2p^4)(x+\gamma^2)$. No rank-zero assertion is inferred for this different curve. The complete trace-two exclusion in Section 12.48 instead uses the exact signed-trace quartic and a different rank-one elliptic group.

The exact norm identity, isomorphisms, halving formulas and pattern implications are certified in `simultaneous_units/trace_two_auxiliary_restriction.md` and `verify_trace_two_auxiliary.py/.json`. The independent proof and symbolic replay are `rank4_next/trace_center_norm/auxiliary_k3_review.md` and `verify_auxiliary_k3.py/.json`, including the complete torsion lists and the previously separated old-torsion exceptions.


### 12.48. Complete exclusion of rational quadratic families in the five-square pencil

Let a rational curve on the full-root surface have normalization $\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}$, with nonconstant five-square parameters $m,n$ of degrees $M,N$. Then a nondegenerate such curve cannot have $M=2$ or $N=2$. This concerns rational families with the indicated projection degree. It neither excludes isolated rational points on specialized fibers nor bounds their denominators.

Section 12.43 already excludes the graph-image cases with $M=2$. In the remaining case, put $K=\mathbb Q(m)$, $L=\mathbb Q(t)$ with $[L:K]=2$, and let $\sigma$ be the involution. Here $n\notin K$. Set
\[
S=n+\sigma n,\qquad T=n\sigma n,\qquad
\Delta=S^2-4T,\qquad D=(T+1)^2-S^2.
\tag{U-QF-SYMMETRIC-DATA}
\]
Primitivity requires $\Delta$ nonsquare in $K$. The function $D=(1-n^2)(1-(\sigma n)^2)$ is nonzero. Use the actual offset point $Z=2Q+P$ and the notation
\[
p=\frac{2m}{1-m^2},\quad \alpha=p^2-3,\quad
\beta=p^2+1,\quad\gamma=1-3p^2,
\]
\[
E:y^2=x(x+\beta^2)(x+\alpha\gamma),\qquad
P=(\alpha\beta p^2,\alpha\beta p(p^2-1)^2).
\]
Section 12.45 excludes trace zero and proves
\[
Z+\sigma Z=2jP,\quad |j|\in\{1,2,3\},\qquad
N\le24,20,18\quad\text{respectively}.
\tag{U-QF-TRACE-INPUT}
\]
Changing an offset ordinate sign negates $Z$ and preserves the full-square conditions, so it suffices to take $j=1,2,3$. The corresponding actual half is replaced by $-Q-P$. No independent choice of trace sign is imposed on a reconstructed point.

**An actual rational quartic point.** Write $A_E=\beta^2+\alpha\gamma$, $B_E=\beta^2\alpha\gamma$, $a=\alpha\beta$, $b=\beta\gamma$, and $J=jP=(x_J,y_J)$. The doubling formulas supply rational functions
\[
s=\frac{x_J^2-B_E}{2y_J},\qquad
v=\frac{x_J^2+2\beta^2x_J+B_E}{2y_J},\qquad
w=\frac{x_J^2+2\alpha\gamma x_J+B_E}{2y_J}.
\]
Then $c=x(2jP)=s^2$, $v^2=c+\beta^2$, $w^2=c+\alpha\gamma$, and $y(2jP)=svw$. In particular $k=vw$ satisfies $k^2=c^2+A_Ec+B_E$. These functions are nonzero, since $P$ is nontorsion. It is essential that $c=x(2jP)$, rather than $x(jP)$.

Set $r=2n/(1-n^2)$ and $r'=\sigma r$, so $x(Z)=ar^2$ and $x(\sigma Z)=ar'^2$. The abscissa addition relation for target $2jP$ factors as
\[
\bigl[xx'+B_E-c(x+x')\bigr]^2-4xx'k^2=0.
\]
Since $xx'=a^2r^2r'^2$, one of $\epsilon=\pm1$ gives
\[
a^2r^2r'^2+B_E-ca(r^2+r'^2)+2\epsilon akrr'=0.
\]
Using $rr'=4T/D$ and
$r^2+r'^2=4[S^2(1+T^2)-2T(T+1)^2]/D^2$ yields
\[
bD^2+[4c(1+T^2)+\epsilon8kT]D
       +16aT^2-4c(T^2-1)^2=0.
\tag{U-QF-TRACE-QUADRATIC}
\]
This is a necessary equation for the actual signed trace; the abscissa relation alone is not declared sufficient. Define, using the actual $s\in K$,
\[
V=\frac{bD+2c(1+T^2)+\epsilon4kT}{2s}.
\]
Completing the square proves
\[
V^2=(c+b)(T^4+1)+\epsilon4k(T^3+T)
                   +(6c+4A_E-2b)T^2=:L_{j,\epsilon}(T).
\tag{U-QF-ACTUAL-QUARTIC}
\]
No norm square root is assumed: the displayed $V$ is an actual element of $K$. Consequently no unspecified quadratic twist enters this reduction.

**All six quartics are one fixed elliptic curve.** Put
\[
\ell=\beta^2-\alpha\gamma=4(p^2-1)^2,\qquad
A_D=\beta p^2-\gamma,\qquad d=v+\epsilon w.
\]
The identity $d(v-\epsilon w)=\ell$ ensures $d\ne0$. The transformation
\[
z=d\frac{T+1}{T-1},\qquad W=\frac{2dV}{(T-1)^2}
\]
gives the fixed smooth quartic
\[
W^2=z^4-8A_Dz^2+\ell^2.
\tag{U-QF-FIXED-QUARTIC}
\]
For an exact coefficient check,
\[
4d^2L_{j,\epsilon}(T)=d^4(T+1)^4
 -8A_Dd^2(T^2-1)^2+\ell^2(T-1)^4.
\]
With $\zeta=(W+\ell)/z^2$, the formulas
\[
X=\frac{-8A_D+2\ell\zeta}{16},\qquad
Y=\frac{\ell z(\zeta^2-1)}{32}
\]
give precisely the previously determined elliptic curve
\[
E_D:Y^2=X(X-\gamma)(X+\beta p^2).
\tag{U-QF-FIXED-ELLIPTIC}
\]
The inverses are
\[
z=\frac{\ell X}{2Y},\quad
W=\frac{(8X+4A_D)z^2}{\ell}-\ell,\quad
T=\frac{z+d}{z-d},\quad V=\frac{W(T-1)^2}{2d}.
\tag{U-QF-INVERSE-MAPS}
\]
Thus these are isomorphisms of the smooth projective curves, not merely equality of their Jacobian invariants. Their exceptional charts are explicit: $(z,W)=(0,\ell),(0,-\ell)$ give $O,(0,0)$ on $E_D$, both with $T=-1$; the two infinities give $(\gamma,0),(-\beta p^2,0)$, both with $T=1$. In particular the rational point at $T=1$ is not the origin under this displayed map.

The reciprocal of the group theorem in Section 12.45 gives
\[
E_D(K)=\mathbb ZG\oplus E_D[2](K),\qquad
E_D[2](K)\cong C_2^2,\qquad\widehat h(G)=1.
\tag{U-QF-EXACT-GROUP}
\]
An explicit primitive generator is
\[
X(G)=\frac{-2(m^2+1)(m^2-4m+1)}{(m-1)^3(m+1)^3},\qquad
Y(G)=\frac{2(m^2+1)(m^2-4m+1)(m^2+2m-1)^2}{(m-1)^5(m+1)^5}.
\]
For $B=(1+m^2)/(1-m^2)$, one has $B^2=\beta$ and
$2G=(\beta,2p\beta B)$. The four torsion points are $O,T_0=(0,0),T_\gamma=(\gamma,0),T_-=(-\beta p^2,0)$. Here $\widehat h$ is the Shioda self-pairing over the $m$-line, not a specialized number-field height.

**A proved finite multiplier bound.** Let the actual image on $E_D$ be $A=qG+T_i$. Put $g=1-m^2$ and use the global minimal model $\widetilde X=g^4X$, $\widetilde Y=g^6Y$, with $\chi=4$. Then
\[
z=f\frac{\widetilde X}{\widetilde Y},\qquad
f=\frac{2(-m^4+6m^2-1)^2}{g^2}.
\]
At a finite intersection with the zero section, $\widetilde X/\widetilde Y$ has zero order equal to the intersection multiplicity. The finite poles of $f$ have total degree four. At infinity the minimal local quotient acquires $m^{-4}$, and $f/m^4$ is a unit. Consequently, writing $h_K$ for rational-function degree,
\[
A\cdot O\le h_K(z)+4,\qquad
\widehat h(A)\le8+2(A\cdot O)\le16+2h_K(z).
\]
Also $2h_K(T)=h_L(T)\le2N$, and $h_K(z)\le h_K(d)+N$. The doubling roots simplify to $d_+=y(jP)/x(jP)$ and $d_-=\ell x(jP)/y(jP)$. Reduced numerator and denominator degrees give the following exact finite bounds.

| $j$ | $h_K(d_+)$ | $h_K(d_-)$ | Upper bound for $N$ | Upper bound for $\widehat h(A)$ | Bound for $|q|$ |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 8 | 2 | 24 | 80 | 8 |
| 2 | 12 | 14 | 20 | 84 | 9 |
| 3 | 32 | 26 | 18 | 116 | 10 |

Since $\widehat h(A)=q^2$, these bounds are exhaustive. There are $2(16+18+20)4=432$ nonzero-multiplier cases, including both quartic signs and all torsion translates. This finite list is not an experimental height cutoff.

**Exclusion of all 432 cases.** For each point in the list recover $z,W,T,V$ and then
\[
D=\frac{2sV-2c(1+T^2)-\epsilon4kT}{b},\qquad
S^2=(T+1)^2-D.
\tag{U-QF-RECONSTRUCTION}
\]
For 428 cases the exact certificate records a regular specialization $m=m_0$ modulo $101$ at which the reconstructed nonzero $S^2$ is a nonsquare. Every denominator used in that reconstruction is nonzero and every point lies on a smooth specialized elliptic curve. If $S^2$ were a square in $\mathbb Q(m)$, its regular rational specialization would be a square; its nonzero reduction at this prime would then be a square. Each recorded nonsquare is therefore a proof of exclusion of the rational-function identity. This argument does not depend on failure to find rational points.

The remaining four cases all have $j=1$ and admit exact symbolic reconstruction:

| $\epsilon$ | $A$ | $T$ | $S^2$ | $\Delta=S^2-4T$ |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| $+1$ | $2G+T_0$ | $-(B-1)^2/p^2$ | $0$ | $4(B-1)^2/p^2$ |
| $+1$ | $-2G+T_0$ | $-(B+1)^2/p^2$ | $0$ | $4(B+1)^2/p^2$ |
| $-1$ | $2G+T_-$ | $(B+1)^2/p^2$ | $4T$ | $0$ |
| $-1$ | $-2G+T_-$ | $(B-1)^2/p^2$ | $4T$ | $0$ |

The identities $(B-1)/p=m$, $(B+1)/p=1/m$ make the nonzero discriminants $4m^2$ and $4/m^2$. Each is square or zero, contradicting $n\notin K$. Thus none of the four surviving auxiliary points defines the required quadratic extension.

**Every exceptional chart.** A torsion point on $E_D$ gives $T=\pm1$. If $T=-1$, then $\sigma n=-1/n$. For the actual central root $f_0^2=(1+m^2)(1+n^2)$ one obtains $(\sigma f_0/f_0)^2=1/n^2$, so $\sigma f_0/f_0=\pm1/n$. Applying $\sigma$ again gives $-1=1$, a contradiction. Equivalently the central norm square would equal $(1+m^2)^2\Delta$, with $\Delta$ nonsquare.

If $T=1$, then $\sigma r=-r$ and $x(\sigma Z)=x(Z)$. Hence $\sigma Z=\pm Z$. The negative sign gives the already excluded zero trace. With the positive sign $Z$ is old. The actual equation $2Q=Z-P$ and the geometric no-new-halves theorem of Section 12.41 force $Q$ old as well. The old-center theorem of Section 12.37 then permits only boundary points on a rational base cover. Knowing only that $Z$ was old would not justify this last step; the actual half is used.

The same argument removes any equal-abscissa chart before the addition formula. A point with $z=d$ identically would give $T=\infty$ identically, impossible for the field element $n\sigma n\in K$; isolated poles are retained on the smooth projective models. Nonzero $j$ excludes vanishing duplication denominators identically, and $D=0$ would require the removed constant boundary $n=\pm1$.

This exhausts the nongraph quadratic case. Together with Section 12.43 it excludes every nondegenerate rational family with $M=2$. The symmetric interchange of $m,n$ excludes $N=2$. Combining with the earlier degree-one exclusion, every remaining nondegenerate rational family satisfies $M,N\ge3$. The conclusion is about curves; it is not an arithmetic confinement of all individual rational points to curves of these degrees.

The complete proof and exact maps are `next_pythagorean_cover/fixed_trace_quartic_reduction.md` and `simultaneous_units/nongraph_quadratic_fixed_elliptic_exclusion.md`. The producer certificates are `verify_fixed_trace_quartic.py/.json`, `verify_fixed_elliptic_height_inputs.py/.json`, and `verify_nongraph_fixed_elliptic.py/.json`. The independent replay `verify_fixed_trace_witnesses_independent.py/.json` constructs the generator by different halving formulas, uses sequential elliptic arithmetic and homogeneous reconstruction, and verifies all 428 witnesses. `verify_fixed_trace_survivors_independent.py/.json` separately verifies the degree bounds and all four exact split cases. The independent review `simultaneous_units/fixed_trace_quartic_review.md/.json` checks the twist, every exceptional chart, and the height-contact inequality. The previous group, primitivity, degree and zero-trace theorems are retained as explicit dependencies.


### 12.49. The uniform surviving genus-three quotient and its three exact generic groups

The genus-three quotient used in Section 12.46 exists uniformly on the surviving first-family Kummer cover. Its three elliptic factors all have generic arithmetic rank one, with explicit primitive generators. This gives exact common squareclass and height relations on that cover. A specialized fiber can have larger rank; the third factor already does so at $m=2$. Nor is every rational fiber asserted to reduce to this particular Kummer class.

In this section use the local notation
\[
h=1-m^2,\quad A=1+m^2,\quad\alpha=m^2-3,\quad\gamma=1-3m^2,
\qquad B=4h,\quad d=B^2/A.
\]
These $\alpha,\gamma$ are polynomials in $m$, rather than the polynomials in $p$ of the preceding section. For a fixed rational $m\ne0,\pm1$, all four functions $h,A,\alpha,\gamma$ are nonzero. The five roots are
\[
\sigma^2=A(1+n^2),\quad u^2=A(1+n^2)+Bn,\quad
v^2=A(1+n^2)-Bn,
\]
\[
a^2=A(1+n^2)+4m(1-n^2),\qquad
b^2=A(1+n^2)-4m(1-n^2).
\]
Put $\eta=2A(1+n^2)-d+2uv$. On the actual Kummer class of the boundary point $P'$ at $n=m$, write
\[
\eta=\frac{B^2\alpha}{4A}r^2,\qquad
\eta+d-2B=-BA s^2.
\]
The resulting quotient is
\[
G_m:\quad h\alpha r^2+A^2s^2=-2\gamma,\qquad
y^2=(\alpha r^2+4)(h^2r^2-\gamma),\qquad n=\frac{y}{Ar}.
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-MODEL}
\]
It has boundary point $(r,s,y)=(1,1,Am)$, and retains
$uv=(\eta-2A(1+n^2)+d)/2$ with
$(uv)^2=A^2(1+n^2)^2-B^2n^2$. An arbitrary rational point of $G_m$ must still satisfy the original five root conditions to supply a full-root point.

**Smooth genus three and the exact quotient maps.** Over the $x=r^2$ line the three independent radical classes are
\[
x,\qquad -h\alpha x-2\gamma,\qquad
(\alpha x+4)(h^2x-\gamma).
\]
Their four distinct finite branch points are $0,-2\gamma/(h\alpha),-4/\alpha,\gamma/h^2$; infinity is the fifth branch point. The first two radicals have the same nonzero inertia there. The branch differences are nonzero multiples or quotients of $h,\alpha,\gamma,A$, so no collision occurs at an allowed rational base. The degree-eight cover has $2g-2=-16+5\cdot4=4$, hence $g=3$.

The three positive-genus character quotients are
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_A &: Y^2=X(X+4h^2)(X-\alpha\gamma),\\
E_B &: Y^2=X(X-2\alpha h^2A)(X-\alpha h\gamma A),\\
E_C &: Y^2=X(X-2\alpha\gamma A)(X+4h\gamma A).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-FACTORS}
\]
Their maps are
\[
\begin{aligned}
(X_A,Y_A)&=(\alpha h^2r^2,\alpha h^2ry),\\
(X_B,Y_B)&=(\alpha h^2A^2s^2,-\alpha^2h^3Asy),\\
(X_C,Y_C)&=(-4\gamma A^2s^2/r^2,8\gamma^2Asy/r^3).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-MAPS}
\]
Their pulled-back invariant differentials are respectively $dr/y$, $r\,dr/(Asy)$, and $-dr/(Asy)$. The other four nontrivial characters have genus zero, proving
\[
\operatorname{Jac}(G_m)\sim_{\mathbb Q}E_A\times E_B\times E_C.
\]
The maps extend over the smooth projective models. No rational point lies over $r=0$, since the conic and quartic would force the ratio of two nonzero rational squares to be $1/(2A^2)$. At $r=\infty$ the $n$-map has a pole, which cannot give a full-root point by the complete exceptional-parameter classification. This does not assert that $G_m$ itself has no rational points at infinity.

**Exact groups over $K=\mathbb Q(m)$.** The boundary images are
\[
\begin{aligned}
A_m&=(\alpha h^2,\alpha h^2Am),\\
B_m&=(\alpha h^2A^2,-\alpha^2h^3A^2m),\\
C_m&=(-4\gamma A^2,8\gamma^2A^2m).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
\boxed{E_A(K)=\mathbb ZA_m\oplus C_2^2,\qquad
E_B(K)=\mathbb ZB_m\oplus C_2^2,\qquad
E_C(K)=\mathbb ZC_m\oplus C_2^2.}
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-EXACT-GROUPS}
\]
