For $E_A$, the translation $X=x+\alpha\gamma$ identifies it with the previously determined alternate pencil $y^2=x(x+A^2)(x+\alpha\gamma)$, since $A^2-\alpha\gamma=4h^2$. It carries its primitive section to $A_m$, so its exact group is already established.

For $E_B,E_C$ apply scalar two-isogeny descent to $Y^2=X(X^2+aX+b)$. At any discrete valuation where $a$ is integral and $b$ a unit, $v(X)$ is even: for $v(X)<0$ the cubic term is uniquely minimal, and for $v(X)>0$ the linear term is uniquely minimal. Apply this at every unsupported irreducible polynomial and at every odd-prime Gauss valuation. The original and dual $b$ polynomials have content a power of two. Thus every original and dual scalar image lies in the complete seven-dimensional class space
\[
\mathcal V=\langle-1,2,m-1,m+1,\alpha,A,\gamma\rangle
\subset K^\times/K^{\times2}.
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-CLASS-SUPPORT}
\]
In particular no arbitrary odd-prime constant class is omitted. At $m=4$ this basis becomes $(-1,2,3,5,13,17,-47)$, which is independent. Evaluation is therefore injective on $\mathcal V$. The models are smooth over the parameter DVR at $m=4$ and at $m=2$; the support representatives are units there. Functoriality of the isogeny connecting map makes evaluation agree with the specialized scalar Kummer map, including sections specializing to $O$ or two-torsion. This uses injectivity on a finite squareclass space, not an assumed injective Mordell–Weil specialization.

At $m=4$ the original coefficient pairs are
\[
E_B:(a,b)=(-255255,15494807250),\qquad
E_C:(a,b)=(68714,995905560),
\]
and the dual pairs are $(510510,3175886025)$ and $(-137428,737991556)$. Exact primitive quartic congruences give an original image of size eight and trivial dual image for $E_B$; for $E_C$ they give at most sixteen original classes and trivial dual image. Every possible signed squarefree divisor is covered by the quartic
\[
N^2=dU^4+aU^2V^2+(b/d)V^4
\]
on both primitive projective charts, possibly after translation by a known actual image class. The recorded translations and obstructing prime powers form the finite certificate.

For $E_B$ the eight actual boundary classes
$\langle2\alpha A,\alpha h\gamma A,\alpha\rangle$ attain the upper bound. For $E_C$, the exact $m=2$ original image is $\langle-1,6,10,11\rangle$. Of the sixteen candidates at $m=4$, exactly eight evaluate into this second image. The excluded half is listed to make this second use of specialization precise.

| Candidate class at $m=4$ | Evaluation at $m=2$ of its unique $\mathcal V$ representative |
|---:|---:|
| $17$ | $5$ |
| $-705$ | $-33$ |
| $-1222$ | $-22$ |
| $6630$ | $30$ |
| $799$ | $55$ |
| $-15$ | $-3$ |
| $-26$ | $-2$ |
| $311610$ | $330$ |

The remaining eight are precisely the actual generic span
$\langle2\alpha\gamma A,-h\gamma A,-\gamma\rangle$. The original and dual image sizes $(8,1)$ prove rank one in both cases by the two-isogeny formula $2^r=|\alpha(E)|\,|\alpha(E')|/4$.

**Torsion and primitivity.** The displayed integral models are globally minimal, with
\[
\Delta_B=64\alpha^6h^8\gamma^2A^8,\qquad
\Delta_C=4096\alpha^2h^2\gamma^6A^8.
\]
Their degrees are $48,36$, with smooth infinity fibers and $\chi_B=4$, $\chi_C=3$. The finite fiber configurations are:

| Surface | $I_2^*$ fibers | $I_0^*$ fibers | $I_2$ fibers |
|---|---|---|---|
| $E_B$ | $h=0$, $A=0$ | $\alpha=0$ | $\gamma=0$ |
| $E_C$ | $A=0$ | $\gamma=0$ | $\alpha=0$, $h=0$ |

Each listed quadratic has two simple geometric roots. At an additive $D_6$ fiber, torsion injects into the component group $C_2^2$, because the additive identity component and formal kernel have no torsion in characteristic zero. The visible full two-torsion is therefore the entire geometric torsion.

For $B_m$ at $h=0$, the two nonzero cubic roots have valuations $2,1$ and $v(X)=2$, $v(Y)=3$, with distance of valuation $3$ to the closer root. The section meets a spinor tip of $D_6$, with correction $3/2$. At $A=0$ on both surfaces the nonzero roots have valuation $1$ and their difference valuation $2$, while $v(X)=v(Y)=2$; the section follows the isolated root and meets the vector tip, correction $1$. At each $I_0^*$ fiber it meets an outer $D_4$ component, correction $1$. It avoids all $I_2$ nodes. These local root distances determine the stated components in the minimal resolutions.

The infinity scalings give $B_m\cdot O=1$ and $C_m\cdot O=0$. Their correction sums are $7,4$, respectively, hence
\[
\widehat h(B_m)=8+2-7=3,\qquad
\widehat h(C_m)=6-4=2.
\]
All section heights on these surfaces lie in $\frac12\mathbb Z$. If $B_m$ had free index $j$, then $6/j^2$ would be integral, forcing $j=1$. For $C_m$ only $j=2$ remains possible; its scalar class $-\gamma$ lies outside the torsion span $\langle2\alpha\gamma A,-h\gamma A\rangle$, excluding doubling modulo torsion. This proves the primitive generators and the exact groups, and gives generic Jacobian rank three. Specialized ranks are not bounded by this generic rank statement.

**A common squareclass and two height relations.** On an actual nondegenerate full-root point define
\[
q=[\alpha r^2+4]=[h^2r^2-\gamma].
\]
The equality follows from the $y$ equation. With the root orders of (U-UNIFORM-G3-FACTORS), the full Kummer vectors of its three images are exactly
\[
\delta_A=(\alpha,q,\alpha q),\quad
\delta_B=(\alpha,-\alpha hq,-hq),\quad
\delta_C=(-\gamma,2q,-2\gamma q).
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-COMMON-CLASS}
\]
The boundary has $q=A$. These are simultaneous constraints on one class, rather than three independently selectable images. At a specialized fiber, certified subgroups give a finite intersection of allowed $q$ classes, or an explicit rank-gain condition when an actual vector lies outside a certified span. The actual specialized ranks and saturation must be established before converting these alternatives into an exclusion.

Let $D_i$ denote the pullback of the origin under the three maps. Then
\[
D_A=D_B=\sum_{r=\infty}P,\qquad D_C=\sum_{r=0}P,
\qquad\operatorname{div}(r)=D_C-D_A,
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-HEIGHT-DIVISORS}
\]
with four geometric points in each sum, of multiplicity one. Thus the first pair has identical pole divisors, as required for the completed height-difference method. The first and third differ by the explicit principal divisor, giving compensator $-2\log_p r$ and finite contribution $2v_q(r)\log_p q$ in the doubled normalization.

The entire-disk proof of Section 12.46 consequently has a reusable conditional form. For a fiber reduced to this cover, certify two rank-one factors, their finite local-height levels, good-prime full-root residue disks, integral initial zeta data and the relevant prime-specific saturation. On the boundary disk $r=1+pT$, with nonzero boundary logarithms of valuation one, write
\[
\ell_A/p\equiv a_0+a_1T,\quad
\ell_B/p\equiv b_0+b_1T,\qquad
a_1=1/(Am),\quad b_1=1/(A^2m)\pmod p.
\]
For $c_i=p\alpha_i$ the scaled global-height ratios, $c_0=(\lambda_A-\lambda_B)(A_m,B_m)/p$, and $d_0=-2\zeta_Aa_1+2\zeta_Bb_1$, one obtains
\[
\rho/p\equiv c_0+d_0T-c_A(a_0+a_1T)^2+c_B(b_0+b_1T)^2\pmod p.
\tag{U-UNIFORM-G3-HEIGHT-PREDICATE}
\]
Here $p\ge5$ avoids the model denominators; the stated coefficients and ratios must be integral, with consistent constant changes under any model scaling. The all-orders two-integration estimate, rather than interpolation, justifies this expression on the full disk. Subtract each finite target level. Simple residual roots give unique analytic zeros; an exact auxiliary-prime coefficient sieve retaining all five roots can then exclude nonboundary branches. Targets outside $p\mathbb Z_p$ are discarded only after certifying $\rho\in p\mathbb Z_p$. These hypotheses were all proved at $m=2$; they are not automatically inherited by other bases.

The uniform maps, branch separation, differentials, common class and divisor identities are certified in `varying_primes/uniform_survivor_genus3.md/.py/.json`. The exact rank, support, finite descents, section valuations and heights are in `coupled_lifts/uniform_genus3_groups.md/.py/.json`. Independent reviews are `varying_primes/uniform_genus3_rank_review.md` and `rank4_next/trace_center_norm/uniform_genus3_group_review.md`; the latter includes the local components, torsion and primitive saturation. The quotient and group theorems are unconditional. The varying-fiber height exclusion remains conditional on its explicitly listed arithmetic certificates.


### 12.50. Full saturation on every rational base cover

For the alternate offset pencil over $K=\mathbb C(m)$, with $p=2m/(1-m^2)$, the old geometric group remains saturated after every nonconstant rational substitution $m=f(t)$:
\[
Q\in E(\mathbb C(t)),\quad [a]Q\in E(\mathbb C(m)),\quad
a\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Q\in E(\mathbb C(m)).
\tag{U-ALL-RATIONAL-SATURATION}
\]
Here $E:y^2=x(x+\beta^2)(x+\alpha\gamma)$, $\alpha=p^2-3$, $\beta=p^2+1$, $\gamma=1-3p^2$. In particular no rational cover adds torsion. The assertion permits new independent nontorsion sections; it rules out division of old sections as their source.

**An explicit dihedral Legendre base change.** Put
\[
\lambda=\frac{\alpha\gamma}{\beta^2},\qquad
z=\frac{m+i}{m-i}.
\]
The exact identity
\[
\lambda=-1-z^4-z^{-4}
\tag{U-SATURATION-DIHEDRAL-MAP}
\]
identifies $\mathbb C(m)/\mathbb C(\lambda)$ as a degree-eight Galois extension. Its dihedral group is generated by $z\mapsto iz$ and $z\mapsto1/z$. The branch values are $-3,1,\infty$, as is also seen from
$(\lambda+3)z^4=-(z^4-1)^2$ and
$(\lambda-1)z^4=-(z^4+1)^2$.
The substitution $x=-\beta^2X$, $y=i\beta^3Y$ identifies $E$ with the Legendre curve $Y^2=X(X-1)(X-\lambda)$.

For an odd prime $\ell$, its two vanishing-cycle monodromies at $\lambda=0,1$ are
\[
\begin{pmatrix}1&2\\0&1\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\-2&1\end{pmatrix}.
\tag{U-SATURATION-LEGENDRE-MATRICES}
\]
The explicit Picard–Lefschetz calculation is given in [51], pages 19–21. Their reductions generate $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)$: taking powers gives all upper and lower elementary unipotents. Only these matrices are imported; no convention about the full integral monodromy group is needed.

Remove $0,1,\infty,-3$ from the $\lambda$-line and their preimages from the $m$-line. The resulting cover is connected, étale and Galois of degree eight. Thus the pulled-back monodromy image is a normal subgroup of $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)$ with quotient of order dividing eight. Since the latter group is generated by elements of odd order $\ell$, it has no nontrivial quotient that is a two-group. Therefore
\[
\operatorname{Gal}\bigl(K(E[\ell])/K\bigr)
=\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)
\qquad(\ell\text{ odd}).
\tag{U-SATURATION-ODD-MONODROMY}
\]
The extra puncture $-3$ has trivial elliptic monodromy. Removing it to describe the finite base cover creates no additional ramification in the elliptic division fields.

**All possible odd-prime division components.** Fix an old point $R\in E(K)$. Its $\ell^2$ division points form an affine space under $V=\mathbb F_\ell^2$. The Galois group $G$ of their splitting field acts affinely and projects onto the full linear group above. Its translation kernel is a stable subgroup of $V$, hence either $0$ or $V$ by irreducibility.

If the kernel is $V$, the division scheme is connected of degree $\ell^2$. If it is zero, $G$ projects isomorphically onto $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)$. The unique lift of the central element $-I$ is then central in $G$, and has the form $v\mapsto-v+b$. It has a unique fixed point $b/2$, which is consequently fixed by every element of $G$. Translating this point to the origin gives the standard linear action, with orbits of sizes $1$ and $\ell^2-1$. Thus all division-component degrees are
\[
1,\qquad \ell^2-1,\qquad\ell^2.
\tag{U-SATURATION-ORBIT-DEGREES}
\]
Degree one means an old division point. This argument proves the needed affine splitting directly; it does not assume a vanishing cohomology group without calculation.

**Exact genera, including every branch place.** The minimal $m$-surface has $2I_8+4I_4+8I_2$, hence fourteen bad fibers. Every multiplicity is prime to odd $\ell$. At a good place, multiplication by $\ell$ on the smooth elliptic group is étale, and the algebraically closed residue field supplies local division points. Thus division fields are unramified there.

At an $I_n$ place over $\mathbb C((u))$, the identity component has quotient $\mathbb C^\times$ and a formal kernel with logarithm $u\mathbb C[[u]]$. Both are $\ell$-divisible. The component group is $\mathbb Z/n$, on which multiplication by $\ell$ is invertible. Lifting the requisite component and then dividing in the identity component shows that every old point is locally $\ell$-divisible. Choosing a local division point as affine origin conjugates the inertia action to its linear action. The $I_n$ monodromy is an $n$-fold Dehn twist, so its reduction is a nontrivial transvection of order $\ell$.

A transvection has $\ell$ fixed points on $V$ and $\ell-1$ cycles of length $\ell$. Its ramification contribution is $(\ell-1)^2$. On $V\setminus\{0\}$ there are $\ell-1$ fixed points and the same nontrivial cycles, giving the same contribution. Riemann–Hurwitz at all fourteen places therefore gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
g_{\ell^2}
&=1-\ell^2+7(\ell-1)^2=2(3\ell-4)(\ell-1),\\
g_{\ell^2-1}
&=2-\ell^2+7(\ell-1)^2=g_{\ell^2}+1.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-SATURATION-DIVISION-GENERA}
\]
Both are positive; the smallest values are $20,21$, at $\ell=3$. A new division point in $\mathbb C(t)$ would embed the function field of one of these positive-genus components in $\mathbb C(t)$, contrary to Lüroth's theorem or Riemann–Hurwitz. Thus every rational cover preserves division by every odd prime. More quantitatively, a base curve acquiring a new odd-prime division of an old point must have genus at least twenty. No such genus restriction is asserted for independent new sections.

**The prime two in arbitrary degree.** The complete old group has free basis $P,Q_0$ and torsion generated by $W,T_0$, of orders four and two. Set
$v=(p+\sqrt3)(p-1/\sqrt3)$ and $d_0=p^2-1$. Its audited first two Kummer slots are
\[
P:(\alpha,1),\qquad Q_0:(v,d_0),\qquad
W:(\alpha,d_0),\qquad T_0:(\alpha\gamma,1).
\tag{U-SATURATION-TWO-SLOTS}
\]
They represent the entire quotient $E(K)/2E(K)$. Every nonzero class has a nontrivial individual slot among
\[
\alpha,\gamma,\alpha\gamma,v,\alpha v,\gamma v,
\alpha\gamma v,d_0.
\]
Seven of these quadratic function fields have four branch points on the $m$-line and genus one; $\alpha\gamma$ has eight and genus three. The exact supports and the absence of an omitted infinity branch were proved in Section 12.41. Thus any old nondivisible point becoming twice a point on a rational cover would force a positive-genus quadratic subfield of $\mathbb C(t)$, again impossible. This uses an individual nontrivial slot and applies even when the full halving field is biquadratic, or the rational base cover has arbitrarily large degree.

All old two-torsion is already rational. Hence if an old point has an old half, every other half differs from it by old torsion. Together with the odd-prime argument, this proves saturation for each prime, and removing prime factors successively proves (U-ALL-RATIONAL-SATURATION).

**Consequences for all rational families.** If a rational cover has no geometric rank gain, saturation gives exact equality of its entire elliptic group with the old group. The old-section center theorem then excludes every nonboundary full-root point on the ordinary chart. The exceptional charts require a separate check in arbitrary degree. At $n=\pm1$ their required radicals force the genus-one subfield
\[
\mathbb C(m)\left(\sqrt{(1+m^2)(3-m^2)}\right);
\]
at $n=0,\infty$ they force
$\sqrt{(1+m^2)(1+m^2+4m)}$; and at $n=\pm i$ they force
$\sqrt{m(1-m^2)}$. Each displayed squarefree polynomial has three or four distinct roots and defines a genus-one curve. None can embed in a rational function field. Thus with no geometric rank gain the full-root curve still has exactly its 128 boundary points.

For a $\mathbb Q$-defined rational cover, an old geometric section also belonging to $\mathbb Q(t)$ descends to $\mathbb Q(m)$, since the constants remain $\mathbb Q$. The same saturation conclusion holds arithmetically. The old arithmetic and geometric ranks are one and two; every nonboundary full-root rational family therefore forces arithmetic rank at least two and geometric rank at least three, with a new section independent of the old group.

For later trace bounds, let $L/K$ be any rational cover of degree $M$ and define
$A=M Q-\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}(Q)$. If $A$ were torsion, it would be old by saturation, and then $MQ$ would be old. Saturation would make $Q$ old, contradicting the completed old-center theorem for a nonboundary family. Therefore
\[
\widehat h_L\!\left(MQ-\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}Q\right)>0
\tag{U-SATURATION-POSITIVE-RESIDUAL}
\]
for every remaining nondegenerate rational family. Non-isotriviality makes the canonical height positive on nontorsion sections. This restriction holds in arbitrary degree, but does not classify the independent sections or individual specialized rational points.

The proof and exact identities are recorded in simultaneous_units/rational_cover_full_saturation.md and verify_rational_cover_saturation.py/.json. The two-primary support uses the complete prior geometric group and Kummer certificate in adjacent_center/rational_quadratic_cover_obstruction.md. The odd-prime formulas are proved uniformly in $\ell$; enumerated cycle examples in the script are checks of that proof, not a replacement for it.


### 12.51. General signed-trace bounds and the cubic projection stratum

Let a nondegenerate full-root rational curve have five-square projection degrees $M,N$. Section 12.48 excludes either degree being two; the following necessary bounds begin the next stratum $M=3$. They do not exclude that stratum or bound the denominators of specialized solutions.

**Parity from the actual central root.** Write $m=M_1/M_0$, $n=N_1/N_0$ with coprime real homogeneous forms of degrees $M,N$. The central radical makes
\[
(M_0^2+M_1^2)(N_0^2+N_1^2)
\]
a square. Each factor is nonzero on the real projective line. Taking the common squarefree homogeneous part gives
$M_0^2+M_1^2=cRF^2$,
$N_0^2+N_1^2=dRG^2$.
Neither $F$ nor $G$ has a real projective zero. A real homogeneous binary form of odd degree must have such a zero, so both degrees are even. Comparing degrees proves
\[
M-N=\deg F-\deg G\equiv0\pmod2.
\tag{U-GENERAL-TRACE-PARITY}
\]
This argument uses only the common central root and real rational maps, independently of the earlier even root-degree theorem.

The full-root cover of the $(m,n)$ quadric is elementary abelian of degree $32$. On a curve, the extension generated by the restricted roots still has degree a power of two. Its degree from the normalization to the $(m,n)$ image also divides $M$. For $M=3$ it must therefore be one. Thus a cubic $m$-curve is automatically birational to its $(m,n)$ image, and $n$ generates $L=\mathbb Q(t)$ over $K=\mathbb Q(m)$.

**An exact trace inequality in every degree.** Use the actual offset point $Z=2Q+P$. The prior common-center intersection and ramification bounds give
\[
\widehat h_L(Q),\widehat h_L(Q+P)\le
B=12M+\frac{r_0}{2}+r_o,\qquad
r_0+r_o+r_\alpha+r_\gamma\le2M-2,\qquad
\widehat h_L(P)=3M.
\tag{U-GENERAL-TRACE-HEIGHT-INPUT}
\]
The symbols $r_0,r_o,r_\alpha,r_\gamma$ retain the meanings in Section 12.40: ramification over the good $p$ values $0,\infty$, the other good values, and the two indicated bad-fiber sets. The mandatory ramification of $p=2m/(1-m^2)$ above $\pm i$ has already been deducted from the budget.

Since $E(K)=\mathbb ZP\oplus C_2^2$, write
\[
\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}Q=kP+T,\qquad
\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}Z=uP,\qquad u=2k+M.
\tag{U-GENERAL-TRACE-COSET}
\]
Here $T$ is two-torsion and disappears on doubling. Orthogonal projection for the canonical pairing, after passing to a Galois closure if necessary, gives
\[
\frac{3k^2}{M}\le B,\qquad
\frac{3(k+M)^2}{M}\le B.
\tag{U-GENERAL-TRACE-RANGE}
\]
This is a trace over all embeddings. No involution is assumed when the extension is non-Galois.

More precisely, for $A=M Q-\operatorname{Tr}_{L/K}Q$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat h_L(Q)&=\frac{3k^2}{M}+\frac{\widehat h_L(A)}{M^2},\\
\widehat h_L(Q+P)&=\frac{3(k+M)^2}{M}+\frac{\widehat h_L(A)}{M^2},\\
\widehat h_L(Z)&=\frac{3u^2}{M}+\frac{4\widehat h_L(A)}{M^2}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Combining both upper bounds yields
$\widehat h_L(Z)\le4B-6|u|-3M$.
The coordinate and component calculation in Section 12.40 gives
$\widehat h_L(Z)\ge4N-6M-2r_\alpha-r_\gamma$.
Consequently
\[
\boxed{4N\le51M-6|u|+2r_0+4r_o+2r_\alpha+r_\gamma
\le59M-8-6|u|.}
\tag{U-GENERAL-TRACE-DEGREE}
\]
This refines the previous degree estimate whenever the trace is nonzero.

**The complete cubic trace range.** At $M=3$, one has $B\le40$. Thus $k^2\le40$ and $(k+3)^2\le40$, giving $-6\le k\le3$. The trace coefficient is therefore one of
\[
u=\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9.
\tag{U-CUBIC-TRACE-LIST}
\]
There is no zero-trace case. Imposing the odd parity of $N$ in (U-GENERAL-TRACE-DEGREE) gives:

| $|u|$ | Maximum $N$ | Maximum root degree $M+N$ |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 39 | 42 |
| 3 | 37 | 40 |
| 5 | 33 | 36 |
| 7 | 31 | 34 |
| 9 | 27 | 30 |

By Section 12.50 the residual point $A$ is nontorsion on every remaining nonboundary rational family. For $|u|=9$ the invariant part of one of $Q,Q+P$ already has height $36$, so
\[
0<\widehat h_L(A)\le\frac92r_0+9r_o.
\tag{U-CUBIC-MAXIMAL-TRACE-RAMIFICATION}
\]
Thus at least one of the four residual ramification units lies over a good $p$ fiber. The entirely bad-fiber branch pattern is excluded in this trace stratum.

At the five maximal $N$ values in the table, the ramification weight
$2r_0+4r_o+2r_\alpha+r_\gamma$ must be at least $9,13,9,13,9$, respectively. With total budget four, weight at least nine forces $r_o\ge1$, and weight at least thirteen forces $r_o\ge3$. These restrictions do not exclude those endpoint degrees outright.

**What the center-only reduction supplies.** The double cover of the offset elliptic curve imposing the center square has genus two and model
\[
C_H:Y_0^2=(4H^2-\beta)(\alpha H^2+\beta)(H^2-p^2).
\tag{U-CUBIC-CENTER-ONLY-GENUS-TWO}
\]
Its two elliptic quotients are the original $E$ and the fixed $E_D$ of Section 12.48. Their exact maps are
\[
x_E=4\alpha H^2-\alpha\beta,\quad y_E=4\alpha Y_0,
\]
\[
X_D=\frac{\beta p^2}{H^2}-4p^2,\qquad
Y_D=\frac{B p^2Y_0}{H^3},\qquad B^2=\beta,\quad
E_D:Y_D^2=X_D(X_D-\gamma)(X_D+\beta p^2).
\tag{U-CUBIC-CENTER-ONLY-QUOTIENTS}
\]
Direct substitution proves the equations, including the square constant $B\in K$. The rational Weierstrass point $H=p$ supplies a base point, and the two distinct quotient differentials give $\operatorname{Jac}(C_H)\sim_K E\times E_D$.

For every degree-three line bundle on a genus-two curve, Riemann–Roch gives $h^0=2$, since the residual canonical degree is $-1$. Hence even a fixed rational degree-three divisor class leaves a projective line of effective divisors. Fixing both elliptic traces, up to the finite isogeny kernel, therefore does not finish the cubic calculation. The extra offset-halving and common-root conditions must be retained. This explains precisely the limitation of transferring the quadratic norm argument using only these two factors.

The trace and parity proof is in simultaneous_units/cubic_trace_reduction.md. The independent review root_cubic_trace_review.md checks the general orthogonal-height calculation, the cubic integer bounds, endpoint ramification weights, and both genus-two quotient identities. The original height and component inequalities and the new full-saturation theorem remain explicit dependencies. The existence or exclusion of the remaining cubic full-root curves is not asserted here.


### 12.52. The genus-five center curve and its exact rational Jacobian

The genus-two reduction in Section 12.51 leaves a projective line of effective degree-three divisors in a fixed divisor class. Retaining all three center roots removes that ambiguity. The resulting curve has gonality four, and its Jacobian admits an explicit degree-32 isogeny, with a completely determined rational image.

Put
\[
 K=\mathbf Q(m),\qquad p=\frac{2m}{1-m^2},\qquad
 B=\frac{1+m^2}{1-m^2},\qquad
 \alpha=p^2-3,\quad\beta=p^2+1=B^2,\quad\gamma=1-3p^2.
\]
Let \(C\) be the smooth projective curve
\[
 W^2=r^2+t^2,\qquad
 U^2=\alpha r^2+\beta t^2,\qquad
 V^2=\beta r^2+\gamma t^2
 \tag{12.52.1}
\]
in \(\mathbf P^4_{[r:W:U:V:t]}\). We use the rational point
\[
 B_0=(p:B:p^2-1:p^2-1:1)
 \tag{12.52.2}
\]
as basepoint. All assertions below concern the function field \(K\); they do not assert that ranks remain unchanged on specialization.

#### Genus, gonality and effective cubic divisors

The map \(r^2/t^2:C\to\mathbf P^1\) is a Galois cover with group \((\mathbf Z/2)^4\), branched at
\[
 0,\quad -1,\quad-\beta/\alpha,\quad-\gamma/\beta,\quad\infty.
\]
These five places are distinct. Each has inertia of order two, so Riemann--Hurwitz gives
\[
 2g(C)-2=-32+5\cdot8=8,\qquad g(C)=5.
\]
Equivalently, (12.52.1) is a smooth complete intersection of three quadrics, with canonical bundle \(\mathcal O_C(1)\).

The conic \(W^2=r^2+t^2\) gives a degree-four map to \(\mathbf P^1\). No map of smaller degree exists over \(\overline K\). For completeness, consider the subgroup \((\mathbf Z/2)^3\) that changes the signs of \(W,U,V\). A single sign change has eight fixed points, whereas a product of two or three has none. If \(C\) were hyperelliptic, its central hyperelliptic involution would belong to this subgroup: otherwise the subgroup would inject into \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\), which has no elementary abelian subgroup of order eight. That involution would need twelve fixed points, a contradiction. A trigonal pencil would be unique, since two distinct such pencils give a birational \((3,3)\)-model in \(\mathbf P^1\times\mathbf P^1\), of arithmetic genus four. The sign subgroup would therefore act on its base, faithfully because a kernel involution cannot act within an extension of odd degree three. This gives the same contradiction. Thus
\[
 \operatorname{gon}_{\overline K}(C)=4.
 \tag{12.52.3}
\]
In particular, the Abel map \(\operatorname{Sym}^3C\to\operatorname{Pic}^3C\) is injective on geometric points. Two distinct effective cubic divisors in one class would give a pencil of degree at most three after removing their common fixed part.

#### Five elliptic quotients and the primitive isogeny

On \(t=1\), the following degree-eight maps \(\phi_i\) are defined over \(K\).

| Factor | Weierstrass equation | \(x\circ\phi_i\) | \(y\circ\phi_i\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(E_C\) | \(y^2=x(x+\beta)(x-\alpha p^2)\) | \(\alpha\beta W^2/4\) | \(\alpha\beta WUV/8\) |
| \(E_Z\) | \(y^2=x(x+\beta^2)(x+\alpha\gamma)\) | \(\alpha\beta r^2\) | \(\alpha\beta rUV\) |
| \(E_V\) | \(y^2=x(x+\beta)(x+\gamma)\) | \(\beta r^2\) | \(\beta rWV\) |
| \(E_U\) | \(y^2=x(x+\alpha)(x+\beta)\) | \(\alpha r^2\) | \(\alpha rWU\) |
| \(E_D\) | \(y^2=x(x-\gamma)(x+\beta p^2)\) | \(\beta\gamma W^2/(4r^2)\) | \(\beta\gamma WUV/(8r^3)\) |

These rational formulas extend to morphisms of smooth projective curves. Their pulled-back differentials are nonzero constant multiples of
\[
 \frac{r\,dr}{WUV},\quad\frac{dr}{UV},\quad
 \frac{dr}{WV},\quad\frac{dr}{WU},\quad\frac{dr}{WUV},
\]
which belong to distinct sign characters and form a basis of \(H^0(C,\Omega^1)\).

Label the coordinate sign involutions by \(\tau_0,\ldots,\tau_4\), in coordinate order \(r,W,U,V,t\); their product is the identity. On the affine chart their masks are \(1,2,4,8,15\). The quotient by \(\tau_i\) has genus one, because \(\tau_i\) has eight fixed points. The corresponding factor order is
\[
 (E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3,E_4)=(E_C,E_Z,E_V,E_U,E_D).
\]
After using the image of \(B_0\) as origin, the residual degree-four quotient in \(\phi_i\) is the quotient by the full two-torsion: its deck group consists of three fixed-point-free involutions. Hence the primitive quotient is \(K\)-isomorphic to the displayed \(E_i\), and there is a degree-two map \(q_i:C\to E_i\) satisfying
\[
 q_i(B_0)=O,\qquad [2]q_i=\phi_i-\phi_i(B_0).
 \tag{12.52.4}
\]
In particular, there is no unspecified quadratic twist in these identifications.

Write \(J=\operatorname{Jac}(C)\), \(A=E_C\times E_Z\times E_V\times E_U\times E_D\), and let
\[
 \Phi=(q_{i*})_i:J\longrightarrow A,\qquad
 \Psi=\sum_iq_i^*:A\longrightarrow J.
\]
Distinct character factors are orthogonal: a sign automorphism acting oppositely on two factors negates the cross homomorphism, so that homomorphism vanishes. Norm followed by pullback on one factor is multiplication by two. Consequently
\[
 \Phi\Psi=[2]_A,\qquad\Psi\Phi=[2]_J,
 \qquad\deg\Phi=\deg\Psi=32.
 \tag{12.52.5}
\]
Both kernels are geometrically \((\mathbf Z/2)^5\). Moreover, \(\ker\Psi\subset A[2]\) is constant because all three roots of every displayed cubic lie in \(K\). Cartier duality, with \(\mu_2\subset K\), shows that \(\ker\Phi\) is constant too. Thus a rational target tuple has either no rational preimage or exactly 32 rational preimages.

#### Explicit gluing by principal boundary divisors

Let \(B_g=g(B_0)\) for the sixteen sign classes \(g\). On each factor label the three nonzero two-torsion points by \(T_{i0},T_{i1},T_{i2}\), in the following root order; \(T_{i2}=T_{i0}+T_{i1}\).

| Factor | Root order \((e_{i0},e_{i1},e_{i2})\) | Radical sign order |
|---|---|---|
| \(C\) | \((0,-\beta,\alpha p^2)\) | \((W,U,V)\) |
| \(Z\) | \((0,-\beta^2,-\alpha\gamma)\) | \((r,U,V)\) |
| \(V\) | \((0,-\beta,-\gamma)\) | \((r,W,V)\) |
| \(U\) | \((0,-\alpha,-\beta)\) | \((r,W,U)\) |
| \(D\) | \((0,\gamma,-\beta p^2)\) | \((W/r,U/r,V/r)\) |

For distinct \(i,j,k\), the action \(\tau_j\tau_k\) on \(E_i\) is translation by a two-torsion point \(T_i^{jk}\). Exactly two signs in the last column change; the unchanged slot gives its root label. The resulting ten triangle vectors are as follows. Each row lists the three root indices in its increasing factor-index order.

| Triangle \(ijk\) | Root indices on \(E_i,E_j,E_k\) |
|---|---|
| 012 | 2,2,2 |
| 013 | 1,1,2 |
| 014 | 0,0,0 |
| 023 | 0,1,1 |
| 024 | 1,0,1 |
| 034 | 2,0,2 |
| 123 | 0,0,0 |
| 124 | 1,1,2 |
| 134 | 2,1,1 |
| 234 | 2,2,0 |

Here is a uniform principal-divisor proof of their relations. Set \(x=(r,W,U,V,t)\), and put
\[
 L_{ab,\pm}=\frac{x_a}{x_a(B_0)}\pm\frac{x_b}{x_b(B_0)}.
\]
Each hyperplane has eight simple boundary zeros. Indeed, the five normalized coordinate squares are distinct affine functions of \(r^2/t^2\), all equal to one at \(r^2/t^2=p^2\); equality of any two therefore cuts out precisely those boundary points. For a three-element subset \(S=\{i,j,k\}\), define the degree-zero rational function
\[
 f_S=\frac{(L_{01,+}L_{01,-})^3}
 {\displaystyle\prod_{a\in S,\ b\notin S}L_{ab,-}}.
 \tag{12.52.6}
\]
Changing the order of an index pair changes only an irrelevant constant. At a boundary sign point its divisor coefficient is three minus the number of cross pairs \((a,b)\) whose signs agree. This gives exactly
\[
 \operatorname{div}(f_S)=
 \sum_{i\in S}\bigl(B_{\tau_j\tau_k}+B_{\tau_i\tau_j\tau_k}
                         -B_0-B_{\tau_i}\bigr),
 \qquad\{j,k\}=S\setminus\{i\}.
 \tag{12.52.7}
\]
The summand is \(q_i^*(T_i^{jk}-O)\). Thus each triangle vector belongs to \(\ker\Psi\). Row reduction over \(\mathbf F_2\), with the displayed root labels, gives dimension five. Since the kernel already has order 32, these vectors generate the entire kernel.

#### The exact rational image

For \(A_i\in E_i(K)\), write \(a_i,b_i\in K^*/K^{*2}\) for its full two-Kummer slots corresponding to \(x-e_{i0}\) and \(x-e_{i1}\). At \(O\) both are one. At the two basis points their values are
\[
 \delta_2(T_{i0})=(e_{i1}e_{i2},-e_{i1}),\qquad
 \delta_2(T_{i1})=(e_{i1},e_{i1}(e_{i1}-e_{i2})).
 \tag{12.52.8}
\]
The cohomology coordinates in the point basis \((T_{i0},T_{i1})\) are \((b_i,a_i)\): the Kummer slots are Weil-dual and must be interchanged.

Choose halves \(2H=A'\) of a tuple \(A'\in A(K)\). Then \(\Phi(\Psi H)=A'\), and its descent obstruction is \(\Psi_*\delta_2(A')\). Since all relevant two-torsion modules are constant, the triangle kernel makes this obstruction vanish exactly when the following five classes are squares:
\[
\begin{split}
 &a_Cb_Ca_Zb_Za_Vb_V,\qquad a_Cb_Vb_U,\\
 &a_Cb_Cb_Zb_Va_U,\qquad a_Ca_Zb_Zb_Vb_D,\qquad a_Ca_Za_D.
\end{split}
 \tag{12.52.9}
\]
This criterion is necessary and sufficient for \(A'\in\Phi J(K)\).

Use the established primitive generators \(G_i\), with
\[
 E_i(K)=\mathbf ZG_i\oplus(\mathbf Z/2)^2,
 \qquad(\widehat h(G_C),\widehat h(G_Z),\widehat h(G_V),
        \widehat h(G_U),\widehat h(G_D))=(1,3,3/2,3/2,1).
 \tag{12.52.10}
\]
The generator abscissae, fixing the Kummer normalization, are
\[
\begin{split}
 x(G_C)&=pB(p+B)(B-2),&x(G_Z)&=\alpha\beta p^2,\\
 x(G_V)&=B(B+2p),&x(G_U)&=B(B+2),\\
 x(G_D)&=B(1+B)(B-2p).
\end{split}
\]
Choose the signs by
\[
 G_U=(B(B+2),-2pB(B+2)),\quad
 G_V=(B(B+2p),-2B(B+2p)),
\]
\[
 G_Z=P,\qquad
 2G_C=(p^2\beta,2p^2\beta B),\qquad
 2G_D=(\beta,2p\beta B).
\]
In particular the signed boundary images in factor order \(C,Z,V,U,D\) are
\[
 \bigl(-2G_C+T_{C2},\ G_Z,\ 2G_V,\ 2G_U+T_{U0},\ -2G_D+T_{D1}\bigr).
 \tag{12.52.11}
\]
The exact elliptic groups in (12.52.10) use the previously established rank and torsion calculations. For the pair factors, primitivity can also be read off directly: the boundary point has height six, its displayed half has height \(3/2\), and all heights on the \(4I_4+4I_2\) surface belong to \(\tfrac14\mathbf Z\). A putative further index \(d>1\) would require \(d^2\mid6\).

Write
\[
 A_i=f_iG_i+t_{i0}T_{i0}+t_{i1}T_{i1},\qquad
 f_i\in\mathbf Z,\quad t_{ij}\in\mathbf F_2.
\]
Substitution in (12.52.9), retaining the rational constant squareclasses as well as polynomial factors, gives precisely eleven independent parity equations:
\[
\begin{gathered}
 f_C=f_V=f_U=f_D=0,\qquad
 f_Z=t_{U0}+t_{U1}+t_{D0}+t_{D1},\\
 t_{C0}=t_{U0}+t_{U1},\qquad t_{C1}=t_{U0},\\
 t_{Z0}=t_{D0}+t_{D1},\qquad t_{Z1}=t_{U1}+t_{D0},\\
 t_{V0}=t_{D0}+t_{D1},\qquad t_{V1}=t_{D0}.
\end{gathered}
 \tag{12.52.12}
\]
All these equalities are in \(\mathbf F_2\). The four bits \(t_{U0},t_{U1},t_{D0},t_{D1}\) are free. Therefore
\[
 |\Phi J(K)/2A(K)|=16,\qquad[A(K):\Phi J(K)]=2^{11}=2048.
 \tag{12.52.13}
\]
The free image lattice is \(2\mathbf Z\oplus\mathbf Z\oplus2\mathbf Z\oplus2\mathbf Z\oplus2\mathbf Z\). For either fixed parity of \(f_Z\), exactly eight torsion tuples occur.

#### The full Jacobian group and concrete free generators

Setting every \(f_i=0\) in (12.52.12) leaves a torsion image \(B_{\rm tor}\subset A[2]\) of order eight. Each target has 32 rational preimages, all torsion, whence \(|J(K)_{\rm tor}|=256\). The triangle table gives
\[
 |B_{\rm tor}\cap\ker\Psi|=4.
\]
For a torsion lift \(R\), the identity \(2R=\Psi\Phi(R)\) shows that the doubling image has order \(8/4=2\), and that the torsion exponent divides four. Consequently
\[
 \boxed{J(K)\simeq\mathbf Z^5\oplus\mathbf Z/4\oplus(\mathbf Z/2)^6.}
 \tag{12.52.14}
\]

The boundary divisor differences alone do not give a full free basis. Their free images form
\[
 \operatorname{diag}(-2,1,2,2,-2)D_5,
 \qquad D_5=\{(z_i)\in\mathbf Z^5:\textstyle\sum z_i\equiv0\pmod2\},
 \tag{12.52.15}
\]
which has index 32 in \(\mathbf Z^5\), whereas the full free image has index 16. A single explicit degree-two fiber supplies the missing index two.

Let \(H=q_U^*(G_U-O)\), and put
\[
 D_6=-p^6+3p^4+p^2+1,\qquad N_6=p^6-p^4+3p^2+1.
\]
The fiber \(q_U^{-1}(G_U)\) is the rational effective degree-two divisor \(F\) given by
\[
 r=\frac{2p(p^2-1)\beta}{D_6},\qquad
 W=\frac{N_6}{D_6},\qquad
 U=\frac{B(p^6-p^4-5p^2+1)}{D_6},\qquad
 V=\pm\sqrt{\beta r^2+\gamma}.
 \tag{12.52.16}
\]
Thus \(H=[F-B_0-B_{\tau_3}]\). One verification uses the raw half map
\[
 x(L_U)=\frac{B(B+U)}{W-1},\qquad
 2L_U=\phi_U+T_{U0},\qquad L_U(B_0)=G_U,
\]
so \(q_U=L_U-G_U\); substitution of (12.52.16) gives \(L_U=2G_U\), including the ordinate sign. More explicitly, the halving roots for \(\phi_U+T_{U0}\) are \((B/r,U/r,BW/r)\), whose product is the negative of that point's ordinate, fixing this half.

For \(i=0,1,2,4\), set \(D_i=[B_{\tau_i\tau_3}-B_0]\). Then the five classes
\[
 D_0+H,\qquad-D_1-H,\qquad-D_2-H,\qquad H,\qquad D_4+H
 \tag{12.52.17}
\]
have free images \(2e_C,e_Z,2e_V,2e_U,2e_D\). They form a basis of \(J(K)\) modulo torsion. This is a constructive basis supported on boundary points and the single quadratic fiber (12.52.16).

The exact identities and finite linear algebra above have complementary certificates: the five maps and their signs are checked by polynomial identities; the primitive isogeny also has integral homology cokernel \((\mathbf Z/2)^5\); the ten principal-divisor relations give an explicit arithmetic kernel; and the image computation factors all fifteen generator/torsion squareclasses over \(\mathbf Q(m)\), including constant classes \(-1,2,3\). Independent enumeration of all \(2^{15}\) parity tuples reproduces exactly the sixteen solutions of (12.52.12). The quadratic fiber and all five free images in (12.52.17) are checked by exact elliptic addition.

These results remove the positive-dimensional degree-three Abel fibers from the smaller genus-two target and determine the exact rational Jacobian group available for reconstruction. Given a five-factor target satisfying (12.52.9), there are exactly 32 rational Jacobian preimages and at most 32 effective cubic divisors. Effectiveness, irreducibility, the original individual roots and the genus-zero condition on the cubic field remain additional requirements. No cubic-cover exclusion follows from the Jacobian calculation alone.

The detailed certificates are next_pythagorean_cover/verify_center_five_maps.py/.json, verify_center_five_isogeny_kernel.py/.json, verify_center_gluing_triangles.py/.json and verify_center_jacobian_image_independent.py/.json, together with simultaneous_units/center_jacobian_kummer_image.py/.json, verify_center_jacobian_kummer_image_independent.py/.json and verify_center_free_basis_fiber.py/.json. Independent geometric and arithmetic reviews are center_five_gonality_isogeny_review.md, center_jacobian_kummer_image_review.md and sections_12_52_53_review.md in simultaneous_units. These records retain the exact model labels, constant squareclasses and sign conventions used above.


### 12.53. Finite cubic trace boxes with the full square-root cover retained

The five-factor Jacobian description does not itself decide which degree-three divisor classes are effective, or which points lift to all five original roots. This section gives a finite trace domain and a proper specialization test that retains those roots. Section 12.56 completes the primitive trace and divisor-effectiveness calculation and excludes the entire rational cubic projection stratum.

**A coefficient-height bound independent of parameter coefficients.** Let $L=\mathbb Q(t)$ be a full-root rational cover of $K=\mathbb Q(m)$, with projection degrees $M,N$. In the notation of Section 12.52 the displayed elliptic images have traces
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_Z&=uP,\\
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_U&=2k_UQ_U+M T_0,&
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_V&=2k_VQ_V,\\
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_C&=2k_CQ_C+M T_B,&
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_D&=2k_DQ_D+M T_\gamma.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-CUBIC-FIVE-TRACE-COSETS}
\]
These are the actual full-two-Kummer cosets, so there is no arbitrary torsion translate to add to these displayed traces. The primitive generator heights over $K$ are $3/2,3/2,1,1$ on $U,V,C,D$.

Put $g=1-m^2$ and
\[
a=4m^2-3g^2,\qquad b=(1+m^2)^2,\qquad c=g^2-12m^2.
\]
The pair surfaces have globally minimal abscissa $X=g^2x$ and fundamental line bundle $\mathcal O(2)$. Their image abscissae are $ar^2,br^2$, with coefficients regular in every $\mathcal O(4)$ frame, including infinity. The two triple surfaces have $X=g^4x$, fundamental line bundle $\mathcal O(4)$, and image abscissae
\[
\frac{ab}{4}(1+r^2),\qquad \frac{bc}{4}(1+r^{-2}).
\]
Their coefficients are regular sections of $\mathcal O(8)$. These surfaces are semistable, so arbitrary base change preserves minimality and multiplies their Euler characteristics by $M$.

Since $r=2n/(1-n^2)$ has degree $2N$, each of these four sections meets the zero section with total multiplicity at most $2N$. Indeed a pole of $r$ of order $k$ gives an abscissa pole of order at most $2k$; the $D$ map uses $1/r$ instead. The regular coefficient cannot create another pole. The height formula, with nonnegative local corrections, gives
\[
\widehat h_L(\phi_U),\widehat h_L(\phi_V)\le4M+4N,\qquad
\widehat h_L(\phi_C),\widehat h_L(\phi_D)\le8M+4N.
\]
For any finite, possibly non-Galois, extension,
$\widehat h_K(\operatorname{Tr} A)\le M\widehat h_L(A)$.
To see this, take a Galois closure of degree $d$ over $K$; each of the $M$ conjugates has height $(d/M)\widehat h_L(A)$, apply Cauchy–Schwarz to their sum, and divide by $d$. Consequently
\[
k_U^2,k_V^2\le\frac{2M(M+N)}3,\qquad
k_C^2,k_D^2\le M(2M+N).
\tag{U-CUBIC-FIVE-CONSERVATIVE-HEIGHT-BOX}
\]

**The mandatory local correction sharpens the box.** At a minimal multiplicative fiber write the cubic locally as
$y^2=x(x+D)(x+J)$, with $v(D)=\delta>0$, $v(J)=0$. Suppose the actual abscissa has the form $x=Cf^2$ with $v(C)=\delta$, and put $k=\max(0,-v(f))$. If $f$ is regular, the point meets the midpoint of the $I_{2\delta}$ fiber and has correction $\delta/2$. If $0<k<\delta/2$, its component is $\delta-2k$ up to sign and its correction is $\delta/2-2k^2/\delta$. If $k\ge\delta/2$, it lies in the identity component and its zero-section contact is $\max(0,k-\delta/2)$. The midpoint conclusion also holds when the abscissa approaches either colliding two-torsion point more closely; the local resolution or Tate parameter places both on that same component. Thus in every permitted case
\[
2k-2(\phi_i\cdot O)_v+\operatorname{contr}_v(\phi_i)\ge\delta/2.
\tag{U-CUBIC-MANDATORY-LOCAL-LOSS}
\]
No transversality is assumed.

For $U$, use $C=a$, $f=r$; its four simple coefficient zeros are the colliding-root $I_2$ fibers. For $V$, first translate by $T_0$, which leaves canonical height unchanged and gives minimal abscissa $c/r^2$; use $C=c$, $f=1/r$. For $C,D$, write the abscissae as $(ab/4)R^2$ and $(bc/4)(R/r)^2$. The simple $a$ or $c$ zeros have $\delta=1$ before base change, and the two double $b$ zeros have $\delta=2$; in each case the third cubic root is a unit. The same statements multiply by the local ramification index on the rational base cover. The coefficient zero totals are $4M,4M,8M,8M$, with no additional infinity zero in the minimal frames. Each of $r,1/r,R,R/r$ has pole degree $2N$. Summing (U-CUBIC-MANDATORY-LOCAL-LOSS) therefore yields
\[
\widehat h_L(\phi_U),\widehat h_L(\phi_V)\le2M+4N,\qquad
\widehat h_L(\phi_C),\widehat h_L(\phi_D)\le4M+4N.
\]
The trace inequality now gives the stronger bound
\[
\boxed{k_U^2,k_V^2\le\frac{M(M+2N)}3,\qquad
k_C^2,k_D^2\le M(M+N).}
\tag{U-CUBIC-FIVE-HEIGHT-BOX}
\]

**Every cubic trace inequality is strict.** Put $z=p^2$. For the five targets, the Legendre parameters can be chosen as
\[
\lambda_U=\frac{z+1}{z-3},\quad
\lambda_V=\frac{1-3z}{z+1},\quad
\lambda_Z=\frac{(z-3)(1-3z)}{(z+1)^2},\quad
\lambda_C=-\frac{z(z-3)}{z+1},\quad
\lambda_D=-\frac{z(z+1)}{1-3z}.
\tag{U-CUBIC-FIVE-LEGENDRE-PARAMETERS}
\]
In each case $\mathbb C(\lambda_i)\subset\mathbb C(z)\subset\mathbb C(p)\subset\mathbb C(m)$ is a tower of extensions of degree one or two. Adjoining the square root required to remove the Weierstrass twist adds at most another quadratic extension. Its Galois closure therefore has a two-group as Galois group. The Legendre vanishing-cycle matrices from Section 12.50 generate $\operatorname{SL}_2(\mathbb F_\ell)$ for every odd prime $\ell$. Restriction to the normal two-power cover preserves that entire image, since a group generated by odd-order unipotents has no nontrivial two-group quotient. Thus the geometric odd-prime monodromy is full for every target.

The affine division argument in Section 12.50 then gives old-point division components of degrees $1,\ell^2-1,\ell^2$. None except one can occur inside a cubic extension. At two, full rational two-torsion makes every halving field an elementary two-extension, so it too cannot acquire a new point inside a cubic extension. Prime-by-prime induction proves old-group saturation and absence of new torsion on any cubic cover, for all five targets.

If equality held in the trace Cauchy–Schwarz inequality for an image point $A_i$, then $3A_i-\operatorname{Tr}A_i$ would have height zero and would be torsion. The saturation just proved would make $A_i$ old. But each character map $\phi_i:C_5\to E_i$ is Galois of degree eight, with constant elementary two-group deck group. Every closed point in a fiber over an old rational point therefore has degree a power of two, including ramified fibers. An irreducible cubic point cannot lie in such a fiber. The cubic center point is primitive: if its image were old, the remaining degree-eight root cover would again have only two-power residue degrees. Consequently
\[
k_U^2,k_V^2<\frac{M(M+2N)}3,\qquad
k_C^2,k_D^2<M(M+N)\qquad(M=3)
\tag{U-CUBIC-STRICT-FIVE-HEIGHT-BOX}
\]
for every remaining full-root cubic rational family.

At $M=3$, Section 12.51 and the exact Jacobian image in Section 12.52 therefore give the following complete domain. All four $k_i$ are odd.

| $|u|$ | Maximum $N$ | Maximum $|k_U|,|k_V|$ before parity | Maximum $|k_C|,|k_D|$ before parity |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 39 | 8 | 11 |
| 3 | 37 | 8 | 10 |
| 5 | 33 | 8 | 10 |
| 7 | 31 | 8 | 10 |
| 9 | 27 | 7 | 9 |

Including both signs of $u$, these inequalities and parities give exactly $69\,632$ integer trace tuples. The conservative bound above gives $85\,632$; the mandatory local corrections first reduce this to $80\,000$ by removing $k_C=\pm11$ or $k_D=\pm11$ from the $|u|=3$ row. Strictness then removes $k_U=\pm9$ or $k_V=\pm9$ from the $|u|=1$ row. This is a bound on function-field section coefficients, obtained from the projection degrees; it does not posit a bound on the rational coefficients of an unknown parameterization.

**The exact full-root map.** To avoid confusing $a,b$ above with individual roots, write the original five-square curve over $K$ as
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sigma^2&=F_0=A(1+n^2),\\
u_+^2&=F_+=F_0+4hn,&u_-^2&=F_-=F_0-4hn,\\
v_+^2&=G_+=F_0+4m(1-n^2),&
v_-^2&=G_-=F_0-4m(1-n^2),
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-CUBIC-FULL-ROOT-CURVE}
\]
where $A=1+m^2$, $h=1-m^2$. The morphism to the genus-five center curve is
\[
r=\frac{2n}{1-n^2},\qquad R=\frac{1+n^2}{1-n^2},\qquad
U=\frac{u_+u_-}{h(1-n^2)},\qquad
V=\frac{v_+v_-}{h(1-n^2)}.
\tag{U-CUBIC-FULL-TO-CENTER}
\]
Indeed
\[
F_+F_-=h^2(1-n^2)^2(\alpha r^2+\beta),\qquad
G_+G_-=h^2(1-n^2)^2(\beta r^2+\gamma).
\]
The central root and the two individual root choices are additional data. The center curve has degree four over the $n$-line, while the full curve has degree 32; the displayed map has degree eight.

These formulas have proper extensions at every omitted coordinate chart. At $n=\pm1$, use the center infinity chart:
\[
R/r=n,\qquad U/r=\frac{u_+u_-}{2nh},\qquad
V/r=\frac{v_+v_-}{2nh}.
\]
At $n=\infty$, normalize the homogeneous $n$ coordinate to one. The map has
$r=0$, $R=-1$, $U=-u_+u_-/h$, $V=-v_+v_-/h$.
At $n=0$ the ordinary finite formulas apply. These charts matter in every closed-point enumeration.

**A complete proper finite-field necessary test.** Choose an odd prime $q$ and an integral base $m_0$ where all five homogeneous branch quadratics are separable and pairwise coprime, and where the elliptic targets are smooth. Their ten distinct geometric branch points give genus 49 by
$2g-2=-64+10\cdot16=96$.
Enumerate the full curve over $\mathbb F_q,\mathbb F_{q^2},\mathbb F_{q^3}$, including its projective infinity points and any branch points. Frobenius orbits of lengths one, two and three give every closed point of degree at most three. Every rational effective degree-three divisor has exactly one of the types
\[
1+1+1,\qquad 1+2,\qquad 3,
\tag{U-CUBIC-CLOSED-CYCLE-TYPES}
\]
with repeated rational points permitted. For each such cycle, add its five elliptic images with the indicated multiplicities and Frobenius traces. This is the full image of $\operatorname{Sym}^3(C_{49})(\mathbb F_q)$ under the five displayed trace maps.

A degree-three full-root point over $K$ gives a rational section of the relative proper symmetric cube. It extends at any chosen smooth rational base $m_0$ by properness. The resulting rational effective cycle specializes again at a good prime, also by properness. Therefore its trace tuple must lie in each computed image. This argument makes no assumption about bounded denominators of the unknown parameterization. A degree-two closed point above a rational center point must be retained in the $1+2$ type even if the center point itself has no rational full-root lift.

The exact implementation records the field polynomials, all projective points, all Frobenius orbit lengths and complete image sets. It checks every elliptic equation and that traces land in the prime field. The sixteen center boundary points lift to the 128 full-root boundary points; their 816 degree-three center cycles give 432 distinct integer trace tuples, all of which must survive every correct sieve. This is a required internal control, not evidence that no other tuples survive.

**A short exact surviving list.** An additional full-root symmetry is
\[
(m,n)\longmapsto
\left(\frac{1-m}{1+m},\frac{1-n}{1+n}\right).
\tag{U-CUBIC-RECIPROCAL-ROOT-SYMMETRY}
\]
It interchanges the two noncentral root pairs; all five roots acquire the common rational multiplier $2/((1+m)(1+n))$. Direct substitution in the elliptic maps, with their fixed torsion cosets and signed generators, gives the trace action
\[
(u,k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D)\longmapsto
(u,-k_V,-k_U,k_D,k_C).
\tag{U-CUBIC-RECIPROCAL-TRACE-SYMMETRY}
\]
Thus both a trace tuple and this image must pass every necessary local test.

The exact full-root tests at $(q,m_0)=(59,2),(67,2),(71,2)$, together with this symmetry, reduce the proved finite domain to 544 tuples. Of these, 432 are the boundary triple sums. The other 112 comprise the following seven sign orbits, in coordinate order $(u,k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D)$:

| Absolute values | Product of the five signs | Number of tuples |
|---|---:|---:|
| $(1,1,1,1,1)$ | $+1$ | 16 |
| $(1,1,1,5,1)$ or $(1,1,1,1,5)$ | $-1$ | 32 |
| $(1,1,1,7,1)$ or $(1,1,1,1,7)$ | $+1$ | 32 |
| $(1,1,1,11,1)$ or $(1,1,1,1,11)$ | $-1$ | 32 |

Here the sign action is all even sign changes of the five trace coordinates. It comes from the four independent center coordinate sign changes and lifts to the full root cover. For example, $n\mapsto-n$ changes only the center coordinate $r$, after exchanging $u_+,u_-$; changing one individual $u$ or $v$ sign changes only $U$ or $V$. The substitution $n\mapsto-1/n$, with the exchanged roots divided by $n$, changes $(R,U,V)$ to $(-R,-U,-V)$; combining it with the previous root sign changes isolates the $R$ change. Their four independent character actions generate every even sign change. All trace coordinates are odd and nonzero, so each orbit has sixteen elements. The 432 boundary tuples give 27 orbits, for 34 remaining trace orbits in total.

This finite list is a necessary restriction, established by complete local image sets and exact group arithmetic. It is not a list of rational cubic points. The standalone certificate certified_sieve.py/.json starts from the proved integer box and uses only the full-root records full_cycles_q59_m2.json, full_cycles_q67_m2.json and full_cycles_q71_m2.json, plus verify_reciprocity.py/.json. It has no dependency on the exploratory center-only sieve.

**Effectiveness and irreducibility remain distinct gates.** On the smaller center curve there are unavoidable reducible divisors
$B+q_i^{-1}(T)$, where $B$ is any rational boundary point and $q_i$ is a primitive degree-two elliptic quotient. These vary with $T\in E_i(K)$ and pass every correct center-only local test. Their trace tuples need not equal a sum of three boundary traces. Thus a center-only sieve cannot legitimately discard all tuples outside the 432 boundary sums.

Moreover the displayed degree-eight maps are twice the primitive maps. An integer free trace vector alone does not identify a Jacobian class: the allowed primitive torsion tuples and the 32-element kernel must still be handled. Once the primitive elliptic tuple and a Jacobian preimage are fixed, gonality four makes its effective cubic divisor unique if it exists. That divisor must be irreducible of degree three and must lift through the remaining roots; a reducible divisor or a passing trace tuple is not a rational family.

**Actual root equations for a cubic residue field.** Write the irreducible cubic of $n$ as
$n^3-S_1n^2+S_2n-S_3=0$. Every required root is uniquely
$z_j=a_j+b_jn+c_jn^2$. If its specified radicand is
$A_j+B_jn+C_jn^2$, the square equation is exactly the following three identities in $K$:
\[
\begin{aligned}
a_j^2+2b_jc_jS_3+c_j^2S_1S_3&=A_j,\\
2a_jb_j-2b_jc_jS_2+c_j^2(S_3-S_1S_2)&=B_j,\\
b_j^2+2a_jc_j+2b_jc_jS_1+c_j^2(S_1^2-S_2)&=C_j.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-CUBIC-FIFTEEN-ACTUAL-ROOT-EQUATIONS}
\]
Apply these to all five radicands in (U-CUBIC-FULL-ROOT-CURVE). The resulting fifteen equations retain individual square roots, not only their norms. Irreducibility, the genus-zero normalization of the resulting degree-three function field, and the nonboundary conditions are still required. The cubic discriminant alone does not prove genus zero.

The independent global-frame, local-component and trace-height proof is rank4_next/trace_center_norm/cubic_five_trace_height_review.md, with exact coefficient-chart certificate verify_cubic_five_height.py/.json and a separate local-loss audit in simultaneous_units. The exact generic generators and full Kummer cosets are in simultaneous_units/center_pair_exact_groups.md and the earlier triple-group certificates. The complete proper finite-field implementation and scope proof are in coupled_lifts/cubic_center_sieve; its surviving lists are computational progress, not a completed cubic exclusion. The original cubic root equations and the injective Abel reduction are independently certified in next_pythagorean_cover/cubic_center_abel_reduction.md and verify_cubic_actual_root_descent.py/.json.


### 12.54. The unramified root covers and the exact limit of their norm tests

The two remaining noncentral root conditions define an étale cover of the genus-five center curve. Their individual square classes remain relevant in a cubic field. Their norms, however, impose no further restriction on any rational divisor class of the generic center curve.

Retain the notation of Section 12.52, and put
\[
 g=1-m^2,\qquad A=1+m^2,\qquad
 n=\frac r{W+1},\qquad
 r=\frac{2n}{1-n^2},\qquad W=\frac{1+n^2}{1-n^2}.
\]
The five radicands in the full-root chart are
\[
 F_0=A(1+n^2),\qquad
 F_\pm=F_0\pm4gn,\qquad
 G_\pm=F_0\pm4m(1-n^2).
 \tag{12.54.1}
\]
The center equations give the exact identities
\[
 F_+F_-=g^2(1-n^2)^2U^2,\qquad
 G_+G_-=g^2(1-n^2)^2V^2.
 \tag{12.54.2}
\]

#### The intermediate étale cover

The divisors of \(F_+\) and \(G_+\) on \(C\) are even. Their simple zeros on the \(n\)-line are ramification points of the existing \(U\)- or \(V\)-cover, while their poles at infinity already have even order. Their geometric square classes are independent: the four quadratic polynomials \(F_+,F_-,G_+,G_-\) have disjoint simple branch supports, and the two classes already adjoined in \(K(C)/K(n)\) are their pair products. Thus
\[
 C^{\mathrm{et}}:\quad K(C^{\mathrm{et}})=K(C)(\sqrt{F_+},\sqrt{G_+})
 \tag{12.54.3}
\]
is a connected étale cover of degree four. Since \(g(C)=5\), its genus is
\[
 g(C^{\mathrm{et}})=1+4(5-1)=17.
\]
The complete full-root curve further adjoins \(\sqrt{F_0}\). The two zeros of \(F_0\) on the \(n\)-line are disjoint from all four noncentral branch supports. They therefore lift to 32 simple zeros on \(C^{\mathrm{et}}\); the poles remain even. This last double cover has 32 branch points and genus
\[
 2g(C^{\mathrm{et}})-1+32/2=49.
 \tag{12.54.4}
\]
Accordingly, the full-root map to \(C\) has degree eight: an étale degree-four step followed by a ramified central double cover.

#### Evaluation homomorphisms and the five elliptic fibers

For \(f=F_+\) or \(G_+\), the even divisor of \(f\) defines a homomorphism
\[
 \operatorname{ev}_f:J(K)\longrightarrow K^*/K^{*2}.
 \tag{12.54.5}
\]
On a degree-zero divisor disjoint from its zeros and poles, this is the product of residue-field norms of the values of \(f\), counted with multiplicities. Weil reciprocity shows that changing the divisor by a principal divisor multiplies this product by a square, since \(\operatorname{div}(f)\) is twice a divisor. Moving representatives gives the evaluation on every class.

Every boundary point has \(n\in\{m,-m,1/m,-1/m\}\), and both \(F_+\) and \(G_+\) are squares there. For example, at \(n=m\) both are \((m^2-2m-1)^2\); the other values follow from (12.54.2) and inversion. Hence the two homomorphisms vanish on all boundary divisor differences.

Set \(H_i=q_i^*(G_i-O)\) for the five primitive elliptic quotients of Section 12.52. The next table gives the action of each quotient involution on \(n\), and an invariant square root of the corresponding function-field norm.

| Factor | Involution on \(n\) | Square root of \(F_+\tau_i(F_+)\) | Square root of \(G_+\tau_i(G_+)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(C\) | \(-n\) | \(g(1-n^2)U\) | \(G_+\) |
| \(Z\) | \(-1/n\) | \(2gU/r\) | \(2gV/r\) |
| \(V\) | \(n\) | \(F_+\) | \(G_+\) |
| \(U\) | \(n\) | \(F_+\) | \(G_+\) |
| \(D\) | \(1/n\) | \(2AW/r+4g\) | \(2gV/r\) |

These are squares in the quotient function fields themselves. For \(C\), the quantities \(n^2,U\) are fixed. For \(Z\), the quantities \(r,U,V\) are fixed. For \(D\), the ratios \(W/r,V/r\) are fixed, and
\[
 F_+/n=A(n+n^{-1})+4g=2AW/r+4g.
\]
The other two involutions fix \(n\). The table follows directly from (12.54.2), so it remains valid independently of any choice of elliptic generator.

Evaluating these norm identities on the degree-two fibers over \(G_i\) and \(O\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{ev}_{F_+}(H_i)=\operatorname{ev}_{G_+}(H_i)=1
 \quad\text{for every }i.
 \tag{12.54.6}
\]
In particular, the correction \(H_U\) needed for the free basis in Section 12.52 is invisible to both tests. Its explicit quadratic fiber has two points with the same rational \(n\) and opposite \(V\)-signs, making this special case immediate.

#### Completeness, including the additional torsion

The boundary differences and the five classes \(H_i\) generate all of \(J(K)\), including its torsion. Here is a proof that does not presume saturation of the boundary subgroup. Their boundary images under \(\Phi\) span all sixteen allowed classes modulo \(2A(K)\), using the exact equations (12.52.12), while
\[
 \Phi(H_i)=2G_i
\]
in the corresponding factor. Hence they map onto \(\Phi J(K)\). They also contain \(\ker\Phi=\Psi(A[2])\): every pullback of an elliptic two-torsion point is supported on boundary points, explicitly
\[
 q_i^*(T_i^{jk}-O)=B_{\tau_j\tau_k}+B_{\tau_i\tau_j\tau_k}-B_0-B_{\tau_i}.
 \tag{12.54.7}
\]
Surjectivity on the image and containment of the kernel prove the generation assertion.

For an explicit check of the torsion not generated by the boundary kernel alone, write \(\Delta_h=[B_h-B_0]\), with the affine sign masks on \((r,W,U,V)\). The following classes have the indicated exact orders:
\[
\begin{array}{c|l|c}
 &\text{divisor class}&\text{order}\\\hline
 T_2&\Delta_2-H_C+H_V+H_U-H_D&2\\
 T_9&\Delta_9-H_C+H_U&2\\
 T_5&\Delta_5-H_C+H_V&4.
\end{array}
 \tag{12.54.8}
\]
Their images in the product, in factor order \((C,Z,V,U,D)\), are respectively
\[
\begin{split}
 &(T_{C1},O,T_{V1},T_{U2},T_{D2}),\\
 &(O,T_{Z1},T_{V1},O,T_{D2}),\\
 &(T_{C0},T_{Z2},T_{V0},T_{U1},T_{D1}).
\end{split}
\]
These generate the eight-point torsion image. The first two lie in \(\ker\Psi\); the third does not, so (12.52.5) gives the orders in (12.54.8). Together with the boundary-supported kernel, they account for \(\mathbf Z/4\oplus(\mathbf Z/2)^6\). These exact classes are also independently checked by the constructive generator certificate, which computes all sixteen boundary images in the fixed model torsion bases.

By (12.54.6) and full generation, both evaluations vanish on the entire rational Jacobian:
\[
 \boxed{\operatorname{ev}_{F_+}\equiv\operatorname{ev}_{G_+}\equiv1
        \quad\text{on }J(C)(\mathbf Q(m)).}
 \tag{12.54.9}
\]

#### Consequence for the cubic reduction

If \(D\) is any rational effective divisor of degree three away from the zeros and poles in question, then \([D-3B_0]\in J(K)\). Since both values at \(B_0\) are squares, (12.54.9) implies
\[
 \operatorname{Norm}_D(F_+)\in K^{*2},\qquad
 \operatorname{Norm}_D(G_+)\in K^{*2}.
 \tag{12.54.10}
\]
Thus the two norm-square tests remove no rational cubic Abel class and give no further congruence on the elliptic trace coefficients or torsion choices. This is a limitation of taking norms, not of the original root conditions. A nonsquare in a cubic field can have square norm. The individual classes of \(F_+\) and \(G_+\) in that field, their simultaneous lift to (12.54.3), and the separate central root must still be retained in the finite reconstruction problem. In particular, (12.54.9) neither constructs nor excludes a primitive cubic full-root family.

The norm identities and complete-generation proof are recorded in simultaneous_units/center_unramified_norm_limit.md and verify_center_unramified_norms.py/.json, with independent center_unramified_norm_review.md/.json. The constructive torsion representatives and all five generator fibers are certified in next_pythagorean_cover/verify_center_constructive_generators.py/.json and verify_center_generator_fibers.py/.json. Evaluation at a divisor meeting a zero or pole uses a moved representative; the quotient norm identities are identities of rational functions, so their trivial evaluation conclusion does not treat a zero value as a nonzero squareclass.


### 12.55. Uniform specialized lower ranks, Kummer parity and effective height bands

The surviving genus-three cover of Section 12.49 gives arithmetic
restrictions on isolated points at varying rational bases. The results
below do not require a rational family of such points. They retain the
assumption that the full-root point lies on the actual boundary $P'$
Kummer representative: no uniform reduction of every fiber to that
representative is asserted. Specialized ranks may increase, and generic
primitivity is not used as a specialization theorem.

Put
\[
h=1-m^2,\quad A=1+m^2,\quad\alpha=m^2-3,\quad\gamma=1-3m^2,
\qquad m\in\mathbb Q\setminus\{0,1,-1\}.
\]
The cover and its map to the original parameter are
\[
h\alpha r^2+A^2s^2=-2\gamma,\qquad
y^2=(\alpha r^2+4)(h^2r^2-\gamma),\qquad n=y/(Ar).
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-COVER}
\]
Every original square condition remains imposed:
\[
\sigma^2=A(1+n^2),\quad u^2=A(1+n^2)+4hn,\quad
v^2=A(1+n^2)-4hn,
\]
\[
a^2=A(1+n^2)+4m(1-n^2),\qquad
b^2=A(1+n^2)-4m(1-n^2).
\]
The three elliptic factors, their images $Q_i$, and their boundary
points $P_i$ are
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_A &:Y^2=X(X+4h^2)(X-\alpha\gamma),\\
Q_A&=(\alpha h^2r^2,\alpha h^2ry),\qquad
P_A=(\alpha h^2,\alpha h^2Am),\\
E_B &:Y^2=X(X-2\alpha h^2A)(X-\alpha h\gamma A),\\
Q_B&=(\alpha h^2A^2s^2,-\alpha^2h^3Asy),\qquad
P_B=(\alpha h^2A^2,-\alpha^2h^3A^2m),\\
E_C &:Y^2=X(X-2\alpha\gamma A)(X+4h\gamma A),\\
Q_C&=(-4\gamma A^2s^2/r^2,8\gamma^2Asy/r^3),\qquad
P_C=(-4\gamma A^2,8\gamma^2A^2m).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-FACTORS}
\]
All models are nonsingular at the allowed rational bases. Their maps
extend to the smooth projective models, and their product gives the
Jacobian isogeny of Section 12.49.

**Every boundary section remains nontorsion.** For every allowed
rational $m$, all three points $P_A,P_B,P_C$ have infinite order.
Consequently every specialized elliptic rank is at least one and
\[
\operatorname{rank}\operatorname{Jac}(G_m)(\mathbb Q)\ge3.
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-LOWER-RANK}
\]
Thus the ordinary rank-below-genus Chabauty criterion is unavailable
on every one of these genus-three fibers; extra maps or height
relations remain essential.
To prove this uniformly, put $t=m^2$ and write a boundary point on
$Y^2=X^3+aX^2+bX$ as $(x(t),m y_0(t))$. Exact doubling uses
\[
L=\frac{3x^2+2ax+b}{2t y_0},\qquad
x_2=tL^2-a-2x,\qquad y_2=-y_0+L(x-x_2),
\]
so $2P=(x_2,m y_2)$. The three models have full rational two-torsion.
Mazur's torsion classification, III §5, Theorem 5.1, printed p.156
of *Modular curves and the Eisenstein ideal* [52], therefore permits only
orders $1,2,3,4,6,8$ for a torsion boundary point. Orders $1,2$ are
excluded by the finite nonzero boundary ordinate. Order $4$ requires
$y_2=0$, order $8$ requires $y_4=0$, and orders $3,6$ require
\[
\psi_3(x_2)=3x_2^4+4ax_2^3+6bx_2^2-b^2=0.
\]
The complete rational zero lists in the $t$-line are:

| Boundary point | $y_2$ | $y_4$ | $\psi_3(x_2)$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| $P_A$ | $1,-1$ | none | $-1$ |
| $P_B$ | none | none | none |
| $P_C$ | $1,-1/5$ | none | none |

No entry is an allowed $t=m^2>0$, $t\ne1$. Every rational pole of the
reduced expressions is likewise nonpositive or $t=1$. The certificate
computes the exact factorizations and independently applies the
rational-root theorem to each factor; no unproved irreducibility or
bounded parameter search is used.

**The full roots force simultaneous parity.** Put
$q_0=[\alpha r^2+4]=[h^2r^2-\gamma]$ in
$\mathbb Q^\times/\mathbb Q^{\times2}$, on the nondegenerate full-root
locus. The original roots, together with the defining $P'$ Kummer
representative, give
\[
(u+v)^2=\frac{4h^2}{A}(\alpha r^2+4),
\qquad q_0=[A].
\]
Thus the common-squareclass condition is automatic after imposing
these original roots. The full Kummer vectors, ordered by the roots
in (U-VARYING-HEIGHT-FACTORS), are
\[
\delta_A=(\alpha,q_0,\alpha q_0),\quad
\delta_B=(\alpha,-\alpha hq_0,-hq_0),\quad
\delta_C=(-\gamma,2q_0,-2\gamma q_0).
\]
They equal their boundary vectors. Injectivity of the full Kummer
map on $E_i(\mathbb Q)/2E_i(\mathbb Q)$ proves
\[
\boxed{Q_i-P_i\in2E_i(\mathbb Q)\quad(i=A,B,C).}
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-PARITY}
\]
This conclusion makes no assumption about specialized ranks, indices,
or additional torsion. The omitted rational full-root charts are the
ones already classified in Section 12.49.

**A point-independent bound for the height differences.** Write
$m=p/q$ in lowest terms with $q>0$, and set $H=\max(|p|,q)$. Use the
doubled canonical height
\[
\mathcal H_E(Q)=\lim_{j\to\infty}4^{-j}h(x(2^jQ)),
\qquad h([a:b])=\log\max(|a|,|b|)
\]
for primitive projective integer coordinates. This is twice the usual
canonical height; it is invariant under rational Weierstrass
isomorphisms and satisfies $\mathcal H_E(kQ)=k^2\mathcal H_E(Q)$.
Then every rational point of $G_m$ satisfies
\[
\begin{aligned}
|\mathcal H_A(Q_A)-\mathcal H_B(Q_B)|&\le C_{AB}(H),\\
|\mathcal H_A(Q_A)-\mathcal H_C(Q_C)|&\le C_{AC}(H),
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-BANDS}
\]
where
\[
\begin{aligned}
C_{AB}(H)&=120\log H+\log22
 +\frac{2\log40320+7\log1569+7\log48077}{3},\\
C_{AC}(H)&=\frac{310}{3}\log H+\log253
 +\frac{2\log40320+7\log1569+7\log751925}{3}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-CONSTANTS}
\]
In particular the bounds are independent of the height of the
putative nonboundary point.

Here is a direct proof retaining all constants. For an integral
nonsingular model $Y^2=X^3+aX^2+bX$, the duplication map on the
projective $x$-line is $[F:G]$, where
\[
F=(X^2-bZ^2)^2,\qquad G=4XZ(X^2+aXZ+bZ^2).
\]
Form the $8\times8$ integer matrix of $(U,V)\mapsto UF+VG$ for
homogeneous cubics $U,V$. Its determinant $R$ is nonzero. Two columns
of its adjugate give
\[
U_0F+V_0G=RX^7,\qquad U_7F+V_7G=RZ^7.
\]
For primitive $(X,Z)$, the gcd of $F(X,Z),G(X,Z)$ divides $R$. If $L$
is the larger coefficient $1$-norm of these two adjugate columns,
the identities also bound their maximum absolute value below by
$|R|\max(|X|,|Z|)^4/L$. Put
$D=5+4|a|+6|b|+b^2$. The quartic coefficient norms are at most $D$,
and the adjugate column norms are at most $8\cdot7!D^7=40320D^7$.
Reducing the projective coordinates therefore gives
\[
|h(x(2Q))-4h(x(Q))|\le\log40320+7\log D.
\]
Telescoping proves
\[
|\mathcal H_E(Q)-h(x(Q))|
 \le\frac{\log40320+7\log D}{3}.
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-DUPLICATION}
\]
The calculation includes the origin, two-torsion and all projective
charts, and does not require a minimal model.

Let $h_0=q^2-p^2$, $A_0=q^2+p^2$, $\alpha_0=p^2-3q^2$ and
$\gamma_0=q^2-3p^2$. Integralize the three models by scaling their
$x$-coordinates by $q^4,q^8,q^6$, respectively. Their coefficients
satisfy:

| Model | Bound for $\lvert a\rvert$ | Bound for $\lvert b\rvert$ | Bound for $D$ |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $E_A$ | $13H^4$ | $36H^8$ | $1569H^{16}$ |
| $E_B$ | $30H^8$ | $216H^{16}$ | $48077H^{32}$ |
| $E_C$ | $60H^6$ | $864H^{12}$ | $751925H^{24}$ |

In these integral coordinates the exact Möbius relations are
\[
X_B=-\alpha_0h_0X_A-2\alpha_0\gamma_0h_0^2,
\qquad
X_C=4\alpha_0\gamma_0h_0+
 \frac{8\alpha_0\gamma_0^2h_0^2}{X_A}.
\]
The sums of absolute matrix entries are at most $22H^8,253H^{10}$.
An integer Möbius matrix and its adjugate show that the associated
naive heights differ by at most the logarithm of that sum. Combining
this with (U-VARYING-HEIGHT-DUPLICATION) gives exactly the constants
in (U-VARYING-HEIGHT-CONSTANTS).

**Effective specialized divisibility bounds.** A separate elementary
argument bounds specialized indices; this is not inferred from the
generic group theorem. Suppose
$|\mathcal H_E(Q)-h(x(Q))|\le K/3$. Choose an integer
$M\ge\exp(1+K/3)$ and put $N=3M^2+1$. Every nontorsion rational
point satisfies
\[
\mathcal H_E(Q)>1/N^2.
\]
Otherwise the $N$ distinct rational numbers $x(kQ)$, $1\le k\le N$,
would have heights at most $1+K/3$. There are at most
$(2M+1)M\le3M^2$ rational numbers with reduced numerator and positive
denominator bounded by $M$, a contradiction. Distinctness follows
because equal $x$-coordinates imply $kQ=\pm lQ$.

For the three factors define
\[
\begin{gathered}
(d_A,e_A)=(1569,16),\quad(d_B,e_B)=(48077,32),\quad
(d_C,e_C)=(751925,24),\\
\mathcal B_i=40320(d_iH^{e_i})^7,\quad
M_i=3\lceil\sqrt[3]{\mathcal B_i}\rceil,\quad N_i=3M_i^2+1,\\
L_A=3H^6,\qquad L_B=12H^{10},\qquad L_C=48H^6.
\end{gathered}
\]
The boundary $x$-heights are at most $\log L_i$, while
$M_i\ge\exp(1+\log\mathcal B_i/3)$ since Euler's number is less than
$3$. Thus any rational
division relation $P_i=jQ+T$, with $T$ torsion, obeys
\[
\boxed{|j|<N_i\sqrt{\log L_i+\tfrac13\log\mathcal B_i}.}
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-INDEX}
\]
This holds in every specialized rank. For rank-one fibers it bounds
the actual free indices of the boundary points. In particular their
effective growth bounds are
\[
j_A=O(H^{224/3}\sqrt{\log(2H)}),\quad
j_B=O(H^{448/3}\sqrt{\log(2H)}),\quad
j_C=O(H^{112}\sqrt{\log(2H)}),
\]
with every constant supplied by (U-VARYING-HEIGHT-INDEX).

Once rank one is certified, a primitive generator $G_i$ also satisfies
\[
h(x(G_i))\le\log L_i+\tfrac23\log\mathcal B_i,
\]
because its canonical height is at most that of $P_i$. Every torsion
point has $x$-height at most $\frac13\log\mathcal B_i$. Thus finite
enumeration of rational $x$-coordinates with reduced numerator and
positive denominator at most
$L_i\lceil\sqrt[3]{\mathcal B_i}\rceil^2$, followed by exact rational
$y$ tests, contains a primitive generator and all torsion. Together
with $O$, it generates the entire rank-one group. This is a proved
finite arithmetic saturation procedure, not a claim that it has been
executed uniformly; its bound concerns generators rather than
arbitrary full-root image points.

**The remaining arithmetic alternative.** At each allowed base,
either some factor has rank at least two, or all three ranks equal
one. In the latter case choose primitive free generators $G_i$ and
write $P_i=j_iG_i+\text{torsion}$, $j_i>0$. Parity gives free
coefficients $Q_i=(j_i+2k_i)G_i+\text{torsion}$ for integers $k_i$.
Put $c_i=1+2k_i/j_i$ and
$\mathcal H_i=\mathcal H_{E_i}(P_i)>0$. Then
\[
|c_A^2\mathcal H_A-c_B^2\mathcal H_B|\le C_{AB}(H),\qquad
|c_A^2\mathcal H_A-c_C^2\mathcal H_C|\le C_{AC}(H).
\tag{U-VARYING-HEIGHT-COEFFICIENTS}
\]
For $c_A\ne0$, these imply simultaneous rational approximations
\[
\left||c_i/c_A|-\sqrt{\mathcal H_A/\mathcal H_i}\right|
\le\frac{C_{Ai}(H)}{\sqrt{\mathcal H_A\mathcal H_i}\,c_A^2}
\qquad(i=B,C).
\]
The indices in these expressions are the actual specialized indices,
bounded as above; their oddness or equality to one is not assumed.

These are necessary arithmetic restrictions, not a varying-base
exclusion. The index bound controls coefficient denominators but not
their numerators. No estimate is proved here that bounds the latter
from simultaneous approximation to the specialized canonical-height
ratios. Those real heights cannot be replaced by rational generic
surface heights. Rank-jump fibers also remain in the first alternative.
At a fixed fiber the duplication estimate computes certified height
intervals, and an additional coefficient bound or local logarithm sieve
can turn these bands into a finite obstruction. No absolute center or
MSOS denominator bound follows at present.

Certificates are `varying_primes/uniform_specialized_rank_lower.md/.py/.json`
and `varying_primes/uniform_height_tube.md/.py/.json`; the Section 12.49
review and full-root parity clarification are saved in
`varying_primes/section_12_49_review.md`. The independent nontorsion
audit and successful certificate replay are recorded in
`coupled_lifts/uniform_specialized_rank_audit.md`. The independent arithmetic
height and index audit, including a successful certificate replay, is
`rank4_next/trace_center_norm/uniform_height_tube_review.md`.


### 12.56. Complete exclusion of rational families of projection degree three

The preceding trace bounds and the exact genus-five Jacobian computation
now give a complete exclusion, rather than a finite necessary condition.

**Theorem 12.56.1.** A nondegenerate full-root rational family over
\(\mathbb Q\) has neither projection degree three. Together with the
completed degree-one and degree-two results, both nonconstant projection
degrees of every remaining rational family are at least four.

This is a theorem about rational families on the full-root surface. It
does not assert nonexistence of isolated rational points on specialized
fibers.

#### 12.56.1. The cubic divisor and the exact finite trace box

Set \(K=\mathbb Q(m)\) and
\[
 p=\frac{2m}{1-m^2},\quad B=\frac{1+m^2}{1-m^2},\quad
 \alpha=p^2-3,\quad\beta=p^2+1=B^2,\quad
 \gamma=1-3p^2,\quad d=p^2-1.
\]
Suppose a rational full-root family has \(m\)-degree three. The degree
from its normalization to its \((m,n)\)-image divides both three and the
degree 32 elementary two-cover defining the full-root surface. It is
therefore one. Thus \(L=K(n)\) has degree three. The actual roots give a
point on
\[
 C_5:\quad R^2=r^2+t^2,\quad
 U^2=\alpha r^2+\beta t^2,\quad
 V^2=\beta r^2+\gamma t^2,                         \tag{12.56.1}
\]
where, on the affine chart,
\[
 r=\frac{2n}{1-n^2},\quad R=\frac{1+n^2}{1-n^2},\quad
 U=\frac{f_+f_-}{(1-m^2)(1-n^2)},\quad
 V=\frac{g_+g_-}{(1-m^2)(1-n^2)}.
\]
The inverse projective coordinate is
\([N_1:N_0]=[r:R+t]\), with fallback \([R-t:r]\). Consequently the
center point still has residue field \(L\), and its conjugates form an
irreducible effective divisor \(D\) of degree three on \(C_5/K\).

The central root gives the parity relation \(N\equiv M\pmod2\). The
actual offset trace is \(uP\), where
\[
 u\in\{\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9\},\qquad
 N\le39,37,33,31,27
\]
for the five respective absolute values. The strict common-lift height
bounds and the complete Jacobian image give
\[
 k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D\text{ odd},\qquad
 k_U^2,k_V^2<3+2N,\qquad
 k_C^2,k_D^2<3(3+N).                              \tag{12.56.2}
\]
The strictness uses the actual primitive cubic center point: a rational
image under any degree-eight character quotient would lie in a fiber
whose residue degrees are powers of two, which cannot contain that
point. The previously proved division-orbit argument rules out equality
in the corresponding trace-height inequalities.

Thus the displayed trace tuple
\(t=(u,k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D)\) lies in the following exact box:

| \(|u|\) | \(N\) bound | Pair coefficients \(k_U,k_V\) | Triple coefficients \(k_C,k_D\) |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 1 | 39 | \(\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7\) | \(\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9,\pm11\) |
| 3 | 37 | \(\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7\) | \(\pm1,\pm3,\pm5,\pm7,\pm9\) |
| 5 | 33 | same | same |
| 7 | 31 | same | same |
| 9 | 27 | same | same |

There are exactly 69,632 tuples, with both signs of \(u\) included.
All torsion possibilities remain in the next step.

#### 12.56.2. Proper normalized quotient maps and their torsion

The degree-eight displayed maps have the following abscissae and
ordinates; the listed ordered roots define each elliptic cubic.

| Factor | Ordered roots | \(x(\phi_i)\) | \(y(\phi_i)\) |
|---|---|---|---|
| \(Z\) | \(0,-\beta^2,-\alpha\gamma\) | \(\alpha\beta r^2\) | \(\alpha\beta rUV\) |
| \(U\) | \(0,-\alpha,-\beta\) | \(\alpha r^2\) | \(\alpha rRU\) |
| \(V\) | \(0,-\beta,-\gamma\) | \(\beta r^2\) | \(\beta rRV\) |
| \(C\) | \(0,-\beta,\alpha p^2\) | \(\alpha\beta R^2/4\) | \(\alpha\beta RUV/8\) |
| \(D\) | \(0,\gamma,-\beta p^2\) | \(\beta\gamma R^2/(4r^2)\) | \(\beta\gamma RUV/(8r^3)\) |

The primitive maps \(q_i\) have degree two and are normalized to vanish
at \(B_0=(p,B,d,d)\). They satisfy
\[
 2q_i=\phi_i-\phi_i(B_0).                         \tag{12.56.3}
\]
Here is an explicit proper construction, so (12.56.3) is not used to
make an arbitrary choice of a half at a finite-field point. For roots
\(s_i^2=x(S)-e_i\) with \(s_0s_1s_2=-y(S)\), put
\[
 h_x=s_0^2+s_0s_1+s_0s_2+s_1s_2,\quad
 h_y=s_0s_1s_2-(s_0+s_1+s_2)(s_0s_1+s_0s_2+s_1s_2).
\]
Then \(2h=S\). The following root triples give the required rational
halves; subtract their value at \(B_0\) to obtain \(q_i\).

| Factor | \(S\) | Root triple |
|---|---|---|
| \(Z\) | \(\phi_Z-P\) | \(\big((pUV+rd^2)/(r^2-p^2),d(rV+pU)/(r^2-p^2),d(rU+pV)/(r^2-p^2)\big)\) |
| \(U\) | \(\phi_U+T_0\) | \((B/r,U/r,BR/r)\) |
| \(V\) | \(\phi_V\) | \((-Br,BR,V)\) |
| \(C\) | \(\phi_C+T_{\alpha p^2}\) | \((pBU/V,dBR/V,2pd/V)\) |
| \(D\) | \(\phi_D+T_\gamma\) | \((BV/U,2rd/U,dBR/U)\) |

All missing charts have exact algebraic extensions. At \(r=0\), the
\(U\)-half is respectively \(O,T_{-\alpha},T_{-\beta},T_0\) when
\((R,U)=(1,B),(1,-B),(-1,B),(-1,-B)\). At \(V=0\), write
\(a=BU/(2d),b=BR/(2p)\). The \(C\)-half for
\((a,b)=(++),(+-),(-+),(--)\) is respectively
\(O,T_{-\beta},T_0,T_{\alpha p^2}\). At \(U=0\), use
\(a=BV/(2rd),b=V/(dR)\); the \(D\)-half is respectively
\(O,T_{-\beta p^2},T_\gamma,T_0\) in that same sign order.

For the \(Z\)-half, write \(r=e_rp,U=e_Ud,V=e_Vd\) and
\(\kappa=p^4-6p^2+1\). If \(e_re_Ue_V=-1\), the finite limiting
roots are
\[
 \left(-\frac{d\beta}{2e_rp},\frac{e_V\beta^2}{2e_rp},
                         \frac{e_U\kappa}{2e_rp}\right).
\]
If the sign product is positive, the half is \(O\) for
\((e_U,e_V)=(1,1)\), \(T_0\) for \((-1,-1)\),
\(T_{-\alpha\gamma}\) for \((-1,1)\), and
\(T_{-\beta^2}\) for \((1,-1)\).

At infinity put \(u_\infty=U/r,v_\infty=V/r,w_\infty=R/r\).
Their squares are \(\alpha,\beta,1\). The finite root triples for
\(Z,U,C,D\) are
\[
 (pu_\infty v_\infty,dv_\infty,du_\infty),\quad
 (0,u_\infty,Bw_\infty),\quad
