 (pBu_\infty/v_\infty,dBw_\infty/v_\infty,0),\quad
 (Bv_\infty/u_\infty,2d/u_\infty,dBw_\infty/u_\infty).
\]
The \(V\)-half is \(T_0,T_{-\beta},T_{-\gamma},O\) for
\((w_\infty,v_\infty)=(1,B),(1,-B),(-1,B),(-1,-B)\).
These charts follow by the halving identities and cancellation identities
such as
\((BU+2d)(BU-2d)=\alpha V^2\) and
\((BV+2rd)(BV-2rd)=\gamma U^2\). They cover every point of the proper
curve, including zeros of individual radicals.

In the order \(Z,U,V,C,D\), the primitive free coefficients of
\(\Phi([D-3B_0])\) are
\[
 f=((u-3)/2,k_U-3,k_V-3,k_C+3,k_D+3).
\]
The exact Jacobian image gives precisely eight torsion patterns.
Choose bits \(u_0,u_1,d_0,d_1\) with sum congruent to \(f_Z\) modulo
two. In the ordered basis \(T_0,T_1\), the five pairs are
\[
 (d_0+d_1,u_1+d_0),\ (u_0,u_1),\ (d_0+d_1,d_0),\
 (u_0+u_1,u_0),\ (d_0,d_1).                     \tag{12.56.4}
\]
All sums in (12.56.4) are in \(\mathbb F_2\).

#### 12.56.3. A complete finite-field restriction to boundary traces

At each good specialization \((m,q)\), enumerate the proper full-root
curve over \(\mathbb F_q,\mathbb F_{q^2},\mathbb F_{q^3}\), using all
five homogeneous square equations. Form the Frobenius traces of closed
points of degrees one, two and three, and then all effective degree-three
cycles of types \(1+1+1,1+2,3\). Applying the five proper maps above gives
a complete necessary set of primitive trace tuples. Properness of the
relative symmetric cube ensures that an arbitrary generic divisor has
such a specialization; no assumption about good coefficients of a
particular parametrization is made.

The first displayed-map pass uses the exact reciprocal transformation
\(t\mapsto(u,-k_V,-k_U,k_D,k_C)\), retaining both original and transformed
conditions. Starting from the strict box, the complete cached counts give

| Good specialization | Tuples before | Tuples after |

| \(m=2,q=59\) | 69,632 | 3,008 |
| \(m=2,q=67\) | 3,008 | 1,056 |
| \(m=2,q=71\) | 1,056 | 544 |

For each of these 544 tuples, retain all eight patterns (12.56.4).
The primitive proper-map pass then gives

|---|---:|---:|
| \(m=2,q=17\) | 4,352 | 688 |

The final 432 states are exactly the primitive images of the 816

These are exhaustive finite computations on explicitly bounded sets.
The files `certified_sieve.py/.json`, `primitive_maps.py/.json`,

including nonsplit rational-center fibers which contribute degree-two

#### 12.56.4. All 32 Jacobian preimages are tested

Let \(\Phi:J(C_5)\to\prod E_i\) be the primitive product norm map.
The proved identities \(\Phi\Psi=\Psi\Phi=[2]\) give
\(\ker\Phi\cong C_2^5\), with all 32 points rational. They are supported
on boundary differences: each \(q_i^*(T_i-O)\) is
\[
 B_h+B_{h+\tau_i}-B_0-B_{\tau_i}
\]
for a suitable double sign flip \(h\).

For every one of the 432 states, choose a boundary triple \(D_0\).
All rational preimages are exactly \([D_0-3B_0]+\ker\Phi\).
Thus there are 13,824 candidate degree-three classes, all represented by
boundary-supported divisors. The coordinate sign group of order sixteen
reduces them to 864 orbits. Exactly 51 orbits contain one of the 816
known boundary triples. The remaining 813 orbits require an effectivity
test; neither the isogeny nor the finite-field trace sieve removes them.

For exact class bookkeeping, the twenty coordinate hyperplanes yield
principal differences of their eight-point boundary divisors. Their
rank-ten integer relation matrix has quotient \(\mathbb Z^5\oplus C_2^5\).
The actual boundary subgroup has rank five and contains all 32 kernel
points as its torsion, so the exhibited relations are complete. Column
Hermite reduction supplies exact characteristic-zero class comparisons.
Alternatively, genuine principal witnesses for every Hermite column,
together with the independent degree-zero tests for all 32 kernel
classes, give the same exhaustive enumeration without assuming a
principal-relation search is complete.

#### 12.56.5. Complete Riemann--Roch calculation

Write \(h=1-m^2,A=1+m^2\). The center field has the biquadratic model
\[
 K(n,u,v),\quad
 u^2=A^2(1+n^2)^2-16h^2n^2,\quad
 v^2=A^2(1+n^2)^2-16m^2(1-n^2)^2.               \tag{12.56.5}
\]
The two quartics are squarefree and disjoint, so the affine curve is
smooth and its coordinate ring has basis \(1,u,v,uv\) over \(K[n]\).
The boundary consists of all four points above each of
\(n=\pm m,\pm1/m\), all unramified.

For a boundary-supported divisor \(E\) of degree three, put
\[
 d_a=\max(0,\max_{P\mid n=a}E(P)),\quad
 D(n)=\prod_a(n-a)^{d_a},\quad d=\deg D.
\]
Every function in \(L(E)\) has a unique form
\[
 \frac{P_{00}(n)+P_{10}(n)u+P_{01}(n)v+P_{11}(n)uv}{D(n)},
\]
with respective degree bounds \(d,d-2,d-2,d-4\). Indeed multiplying
by \(D\) removes all finite poles. At the four geometric infinity
points the independent radical signs force these four degree bounds
separately, so no cancellation at infinity is missed. At each boundary
point above \(a\), impose vanishing of the numerator through order
\(d_a-E(P)-1\). The square-root Taylor series divide only by the units
\(2u(P),2v(P)\). These conditions at ALL points over each denominator
root are a complete linear system for \(L(E)\).

Specialize to \(m=2\) modulo 137. The equations become
\[
 u^2=25n^4+43n^2+25,\qquad
 v^2=98n^4+41n^2+98.
\]
The quartics are squarefree and coprime. The four boundary abscissae
are \(2,135,68,69\). Their radical values are independently \(\pm7\)
above the first two and \(\pm101\) above the last two. All sixteen
sections remain distinct, and every matrix denominator is a unit.

For all 813 nonboundary representatives the matrix has full column rank.
Its nonzero maximal minor modulo 137 is therefore a nonzero rational
function of \(m\); hence \(L(E)=0\) generically. Each of the 51 known
boundary representatives has nullity one and is matched to an actual
boundary triple by an explicit integer principal relation. Thus the
only effective generic candidate classes are exactly the 816 boundary
triples.

This computation has independent implementations. The first uses the
four monomials in (12.56.5), with matrices of at most 48 columns. A second
uses a uniform denominator and an independent prime, 149. A third uses
the eight radical monomials in the original \(r,R,U,V\) model. In that
model \(D(r)=(r-p)^{e_+}(r+p)^{e_-}\), where each exponent is the largest
nonnegative divisor coefficient in its eight-point boundary fiber.
Writing \(d=e_++e_-\), the numerator multiplying
\(R^aU^bV^c\) has degree at most \(d-a-b-c\); all eight infinity sign
characters enforce these bounds. Every implementation gives exactly
813 zero spaces and 51 one-dimensional boundary spaces. Independent
integer witnesses also verify every principal relation used for the
positive matches. The detailed certificates are
`next_pythagorean_cover/center_rr_boundary.py/.json`,
`root_center_rr_boundary.py/.json`,
`simultaneous_units/verify_boundary_rr_uniform_independent.py/.json`,
and the independent RR and principal-witness files in
`rank4_next/trace_center_norm`.

#### 12.56.6. The irreducible cubic contradiction

The genus-five center curve has geometric gonality four. Its
canonical model is the smooth intersection of three quadrics above,
and the earlier sign-involution argument excludes both hyperelliptic
and trigonal pencils. In particular its degree-three Abel map is
injective: two distinct effective degree-three divisors in one class
would give a map to \(\mathbb P^1\) of degree at most three.

The hypothetical divisor \(D\) from (12.56.1) must have one of the 432
boundary primitive trace states. The complete kernel calculation and
Riemann--Roch test show that it is linearly equivalent to a boundary
triple \(D_1\). Abel injectivity gives \(D=D_1\). This contradicts the
fact that \(D\) is an irreducible closed point of degree three, whereas
\(D_1\) is a sum of rational boundary points. This proves the theorem
for the first projection; exchanging the two variables proves the
second projection statement. All actual roots, proper charts, torsion
choices and Jacobian kernel classes have been retained throughout.


### 12.57. Exact full-cover gonality and the next quartic stratum

The complete cubic exclusion leaves projection degree four as the next rational-family stratum. The full square-root curve has a stronger Abel property than its genus-five center quotient: its gonality is exactly sixteen. This restores uniqueness of effective divisor representatives in degrees through fifteen, but does not supply the missing arithmetic control on the full Jacobian.

**Exact gonality of the radical tower.** Over $K=\mathbb Q(m)$ write
\[
\begin{aligned}
F_0&=(1+m^2)(1+n^2),\\
F_{1,\pm}&=F_0\pm4n(1-m^2),\\
F_{2,\pm}&=F_0\pm4m(1-n^2).
\end{aligned}
\]
The full curve $X_5$ is the smooth projective normalization obtained by adjoining the five labeled square roots. Let $X_s$ be the intermediate curve obtained from any fixed $s$ of these radicals. Their pairwise disjoint simple branch roots make the squareclasses independent. Over an algebraic closure of $K$, the map $X_s\to\mathbb P^1_n$ has degree $2^s$, with $2s$ branch places, each having inertia order two. Infinity is unramified because all radicands have degree two. Riemann–Hurwitz gives
\[
g_s=1+2^{s-1}(s-2),\qquad
(g_1,g_2,g_3,g_4,g_5)=(0,1,5,17,49).
\tag{U-FULL-RADICAL-TOWER-GENUS}
\]

We claim $\operatorname{gon}(X_s)=2^{s-1}$. The first curve is a conic, so its geometric gonality is one. Inductively, let $f:X_s\to\mathbb P^1$ have degree $d$. If $f$ factors through the quadratic map $X_s\to X_{s-1}$, then
$d\ge2\operatorname{gon}(X_{s-1})=2^{s-1}$.
Otherwise the two function fields $K(X_{s-1})$ and $K(f)$ generate $K(X_s)$, since the first has prime index two. The Castelnuovo–Severi inequality [53, Proposition 3.2] therefore applies with degrees $2,d$ and target genera $g_{s-1},0$:
\[
g_s\le2g_{s-1}+d-1,
\qquad
d\ge g_s-2g_{s-1}+1=2^{s-1}.
\]
Conversely, projection to $X_1$ has degree $2^{s-1}$ and attains the bound. Hence
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{gon}_{\overline K}(X_5)=16.}
\tag{U-FULL-GONALITY-SIXTEEN}
\]
This is also the gonality over $K$: choose $X_1$ as
$\sigma^2=(1+m^2)(1+n^2)$, whose $K$-point $(n,\sigma)=(m,1+m^2)$ makes it a rational conic. Thus the degree-sixteen upper-bound map is defined over $K$, while the geometric lower bound remains valid over $K$.

The same result holds for every rational specialization $m=m_0\notin\{0,1,-1\}$. Indeed the leading coefficients, discriminants and pairwise resultants have no other rational zero. Up to nonzero constants, all their factors belong to
\[
m,\ m-1,\ m+1,\ m^2+1,\ m^2-3,\ 3m^2-1,
\ m^2\pm4m+1,\ m^2\pm2m-1.
\]
The quadratic factors have no rational zero. The specialized first conic retains its boundary point. This specialized gonality statement is geometric and does not assert a rational-point classification of the specialized fiber.

**Abel injectivity through degree fifteen.** For every $d\le15$, two distinct linearly equivalent effective divisors of degree $d$ would give a pencil of degree at most $d$ after removing their common fixed part. Thus
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Sym}^d(X_5)\longrightarrow
\operatorname{Pic}^d(X_5)\text{ is injective on geometric effective divisors for }d\le15.}
\tag{U-FULL-ABEL-FIFTEEN}
\]
In particular, quartic divisors have at most one effective representative in a full Jacobian class. The analogous statement fails on the center curve $C_5$, whose degree-four pencil already exists.

**Necessary quartic trace bounds.** Let a nonboundary full-root rational curve have $M=4$ and second projection degree $N$. Retain the notation of Section 12.51:
\[
Z=2Q+P,\quad \operatorname{Tr}Q=kP+T,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}Z=uP,\quad u=2k+4,
\]
where $T$ is two-torsion. The two trace-height bounds give
\[
B=48+\frac{r_0}{2}+r_o\le54,\qquad
k^2\le72,\quad(k+4)^2\le72.
\]
Therefore
\[
-8\le k\le4,\qquad
u\in\{-12,-10,-8,-6,-4,-2,0,2,4,6,8,10,12\}.
\tag{U-QUARTIC-TRACE-RANGE}
\]
The central root gives $N\equiv M\pmod2$, and the signed degree bound is
$4N\le228-6|u|$.
The completed lower-degree exclusions, applied symmetrically, give $N\ge4$. The resulting necessary bounds are:

| $|u|$ | Maximum even $N$ | Maximum root degree $M+N$ | Even pair coefficient cap | Even triple coefficient cap |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|0|56|60|12|14|
|2|54|58|12|14|
|4|50|54|10|14|
|6|48|52|10|14|
|8|44|48|10|12|
|10|42|46|10|12|
|12|38|42|10|12|

Here the five displayed center traces are
\[
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_Z=uP,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_U=2k_UQ_U,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_V=2k_VQ_V,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_C=2k_CQ_C,\quad
\operatorname{Tr}\phi_D=2k_DQ_D.
\tag{U-QUARTIC-FIVE-COSETS}
\]
The torsion terms $MT_0,MT_B,MT_\gamma$ vanish since $M=4$. The exact Jacobian-image parity condition gives $k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D$ even: subtracting the fourfold boundary trace and dividing the displayed maps by two changes these coefficients by even integers. The last two table columns follow from the already proved local-loss bounds
\[
k_U^2,k_V^2\le\frac{4(4+2N)}3,
\qquad k_C^2,k_D^2\le4(4+N).
\tag{U-QUARTIC-FIVE-BOUNDS}
\]
They are necessary coefficient bounds, not an effectiveness test. The cubic all-factor saturation argument is not imported: two-division fibers may have degree four.

The original offset saturation theorem does still make its trace-zero residual nonzero. Setting
$\varepsilon=\widehat h_L(Q)-3k^2/4$ gives exactly
\[
\begin{aligned}
\widehat h_L(Q+P)&=\varepsilon+\frac{3(k+4)^2}{4},\\
\widehat h_L(Z)&=4\varepsilon+\frac{3u^2}{4},\\
0<\varepsilon&\le B-\frac{3(|u|+4)^2}{16}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-QUARTIC-TRACE-RESIDUAL}
\]
This strict residual inequality does not make the degree bound strict. In particular, $N=54,48,42$ are retained in their respective rows. The trace-zero case $u=0$ is also retained; its degree-two exclusion does not automatically extend to a quartic cover.

**The imprimitive image cases and remaining arithmetic.** Let $L=\mathbb Q(t)$ and let $L_0$ be the field generated by the center point. The missing full-root coordinates are square roots, so
\[
[L:L_0]\in\{1,2,4\},\qquad
[L_0:\mathbb Q(m)]\in\{4,2,1\}.
\tag{U-QUARTIC-CENTER-IMAGE-DEGREES}
\]
Every $L_0$ is rational by Lüroth. The degree-one center image is boundary by the generic center theorem. A degree-two center image is not excluded by the full-root degree-two theorem: its missing original roots may appear only on the further quadratic cover. Section 12.61 subsequently excludes the degree-two center-image case by analyzing its actual missing central root. A primitive degree-four center image remains.

The full Jacobian has dimension $49$, whereas the five controlled elliptics give only a dimension-five quotient. Its character decomposition has ten elliptic, ten genus-two, five genus-three and one genus-four factors, with dimensions summing to $49$. Thus the kernel beyond the five center factors has dimension $44$. The finite five-trace table does not bound the full Jacobian class. Formula (U-FULL-ABEL-FIFTEEN) gives uniqueness per full class, not finiteness of all classes in the unbounded kernel. Additional character-height and arithmetic controls are required before a complete quartic Abel reduction can be asserted.

The radical-tower proof and arithmetic conic upper bound have an independent review in `simultaneous_units/full_root_gonality_sixteen_review.md/.json`. Exact genus recurrences, quartic integer bounds and the specialization branch factors are recorded in `rank4_next/trace_center_norm/verify_quartic_trace_bounds.py/.json` and `verify_full_radical_branch_locus.py/.json`.


### 12.58. All tetragonal pencils of the center curve

The degree-four center problem differs from the cubic problem because its Abel map has positive-dimensional fibers. Those fibers can nevertheless be classified exactly: they are the pencils pulled back from the five primitive elliptic quotients, with ten explicitly known halfcanonical intersections.

Retain \(K=\mathbf Q(m)\), \(p,\alpha,\beta,\gamma\), and the genus-five canonical curve
\[
 C:\quad W^2=r^2+t^2,\qquad
 U^2=\alpha r^2+\beta t^2,\qquad
 V^2=\beta r^2+\gamma t^2
\]
of Section 12.52. Its coordinates are indexed by \((r,W,U,V,t)\), with sign involutions \(\tau_0,\ldots,\tau_4\). The primitive quotient maps are
\[
 q_i:C\longrightarrow E_i,
 \qquad(E_0,E_1,E_2,E_3,E_4)=(E_C,E_Z,E_V,E_U,E_D),
\]
normalized by \(q_i(B_0)=O\). As before, \(B_h=h(B_0)\), and \(b_i=\phi_i(B_0)\) denotes the full elliptic point, including its torsion component.

**The discriminant of the canonical net.**

Write the three canonical quadrics as
\[
 Q_W=W^2-r^2-t^2,\qquad
 Q_U=U^2-\alpha r^2-\beta t^2,\qquad
 Q_V=V^2-\beta r^2-\gamma t^2.
\]
They span the entire net of quadrics containing \(C\). At the net point \([a:b:c]\), the diagonal coefficients of \(aQ_W+bQ_U+cQ_V\), in coordinate order, are
\[
 -a-\alpha b-\beta c,\quad a,\quad b,\quad c,
 \quad-a-\beta b-\gamma c.
 \tag{12.58.1}
\]
Consequently its discriminant consists of five \(K\)-rational lines \(\ell_i\), one for the vanishing of each coefficient. Every three coefficient forms are independent. Their determinants are nonzero constants or nonzero factors among
\[
 \alpha,\ \beta,\ \gamma,\ \beta-\alpha,\ \gamma-\beta,
 \ \alpha\gamma-\beta^2,
\]
where
\[
 \beta-\alpha=4,\qquad\gamma-\beta=-4p^2,\qquad
 \beta^2-\alpha\gamma=4(p^2-1)^2.
\]
Thus a general quadric on \(\ell_i\) has rank four; the ten pairwise line intersections have rank three; and no quadric in the net has rank at most two. The rank-four vertex is the \(i\)-th coordinate point, while the vertex at \(\ell_i\cap\ell_j\) is the corresponding coordinate line.

Every such vertex is disjoint from \(C\). If a point of \(C\) lay in a net quadric's vertex, one linear combination of the three defining gradients would vanish there, contradicting smoothness of the canonical complete intersection.

**Completeness of the pencil construction.**

Let \(L\) be a geometric degree-four line bundle with \(h^0(L)\ge2\). Since \(C\) has gonality four, \(L\) is basepoint free and \(h^0(L)=2\). Indeed, a basepoint would give a pencil of degree at most three, while three sections would leave a pencil after imposing one point. Riemann--Roch gives
\[
 h^0(K_C\otimes L^{-1})=2,
\]
and this residual degree-four pencil is also basepoint free.

For bases \(s_0,s_1\) of \(H^0(L)\) and \(t_0,t_1\) of \(H^0(K_C\otimes L^{-1})\), the pencil relation identifies the kernel of multiplication with \(H^0(K_C\otimes L^{-2})\). If \(L^2\not\simeq K_C\), that degree-zero bundle has no section. The four products are therefore independent, and
\[
 (s_0t_0)(s_1t_1)-(s_0t_1)(s_1t_0)=0
 \tag{12.58.2}
\]
is a rank-four net quadric. Its two plane rulings cut out \(L\) and \(K_C\otimes L^{-1}\). If \(L^2\simeq K_C\), the products instead span \(\operatorname{Sym}^2H^0(L)\), giving a rank-three quadric and its unique family of ruling planes. The quadric is intrinsic to \(L\), hence unique.

Conversely, each plane ruling of a rank-four net quadric cuts out a degree-four divisor on \(C\): the other two quadrics restrict to two conics in the plane. The vertex is disjoint from \(C\), so these divisors form a basepoint-free pencil. A rank-three quadric gives one such pencil. This establishes a bijection between all degree-four pencils and the rulings of rank-four or rank-three quadrics in the net. In particular, there is no omitted class of non-pullback pencils.

**Five elliptic components, with ten intersections.**

Quadrics on \(\ell_i\) omit the \(i\)-th coordinate. Projection away from that coordinate is the degree-two quotient \(q_i\), with target the corresponding elliptic quartic in \(\mathbf P^3\). A ruling line of a quadric through this elliptic quartic cuts out a degree-two divisor on \(E_i\); its pullback is the degree-four ruling divisor on \(C\). Conversely, every degree-two line bundle on \(E_i\) produces such a ruling by multiplication with its residual bundle in the elliptic hyperplane class.

It follows that the reduced geometric locus of pencils is
\[
 \boxed{W^1_4(C)=\bigcup_{i=0}^4 q_i^*\operatorname{Pic}^2(E_i).}
 \tag{12.58.3}
\]
Each component is an embedded elliptic curve. Pullback on \(\operatorname{Pic}^0\) is injective: a nontrivial kernel element would be two-torsion and would define an étale double cover of \(E_i\) contained in the ramified double cover \(C\to E_i\), which is impossible.

On each component, the map to \(\ell_i\) is a double cover. Its involution exchanges a degree-two bundle with its residual bundle in the elliptic hyperplane class. Its four branch points are the four rank-three quadrics on that line. Two components meet exactly at their common rank-three quadric, and no three components meet. Therefore there are exactly ten self-residual pencils, satisfying
\[
 L^2\simeq K_C,\qquad h^0(L)=2.
 \tag{12.58.4}
\]
They are precisely the effective even theta characteristics on this curve. The classification here concerns the reduced locus and its points; no additional assertion about a nonreduced Brill--Noether scheme is needed.

These ten pencils have explicit boundary members:
\[
 D_{ij}=B_0+B_{\tau_i}+B_{\tau_j}+B_{\tau_i\tau_j},
 \qquad 0\le i<j\le4.
 \tag{12.58.5}
\]
Indeed, the ruling plane through \(B_0\) at \(\ell_i\cap\ell_j\) is spanned by \(B_0\) and the vertex coordinate line. Its intersection with \(C\) consists of exactly these four distinct sign points. Thus (12.58.5) specifies every halfcanonical pencil without solving for an unspecified ruling.

**Rational descent and the trace signature.**

All five lines, all ten rank-three intersections and all quotient maps are defined over \(K\). The rational point \(B_0\) removes the Picard descent obstruction. At a rank-three quadric, projection of \(B_0\) from its vertex supplies a \(K\)-point on the conic parameterizing ruling planes, so its unique geometric pencil descends. At a rank-four quadric a ruling descends exactly when its degree-two elliptic bundle is rational. Hence
\[
 W^1_4(C)(K)=\bigcup_iq_i^*\operatorname{Pic}^2(E_i)(K),
 \qquad\operatorname{Pic}^2(E_i)(K)\simeq
 \mathbf ZG_i\oplus(\mathbf Z/2)^2.
 \tag{12.58.6}
\]
All ten intersections in (12.58.5) are rational. This uses the fixed quotient origins and the exact elliptic groups, rather than an unspecified geometric isogeny or twist.

Every divisor in a pencil \(q_i^*M\) is an actual pullback of a degree-two divisor on \(E_i\). The injection
\[
 H^0(E_i,M)\longrightarrow H^0(C,q_i^*M)
\]
is an isomorphism because both dimensions are two. For \(j\ne i\), the displayed character map satisfies \(\phi_j\circ\tau_i=-\phi_j\), so the trace on such a divisor is \(O\), including ramified fibers counted with their multiplicity. If the degree-two quotient divisor has elliptic sum \(S\), then \([2]q_i=\phi_i-b_i\) gives the exact remaining trace:
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_D(\phi_j)=O\quad(j\ne i),
 \qquad\operatorname{Tr}_D(\phi_i)=[4](S+b_i).
 \tag{12.58.7}
\]
Thus a positive-dimensional degree-four Abel fiber has four zero displayed traces, and its axis trace belongs to \(4E_i(K)\). If two displayed traces are nonzero, any effective quartic class has a unique effective representative. An axis target is only a necessary signature, not by itself proof of membership in a pencil.

Since \(E_i(K)\) has torsion \((\mathbf Z/2)^2\), the axis trace vanishes at exactly the four sums \(S=-b_i+T\), \(T\in E_i[2]\). The four rank-three pencils on that component already have all five traces zero: summing a displayed sign character over the four points in (12.58.5) gives zero, because no such character is trivial on both \(\tau_i\) and \(\tau_j\). Therefore the positive-dimensional Abel fibers with all five displayed traces zero are exactly the ten halfcanonical pencils, with no further zero-trace pencils.

The net coefficients, all ten nonzero triple determinants, every rank-three intersection and all cross-character signs admit exact polynomial certificates. The completeness of (12.58.3), the descent argument and the trace formula have also been independently verified. These checks distinguish the actual elliptic pencils from an unsupported assumption that every degree-four point moves in a pencil.

**Scope for full-root quartic covers.**

The degree-four center Abel problem has finite fibers away from five explicitly known elliptic families; on those families its fibers are projective lines. The individual full-root square conditions remain additional conditions on members of each pencil. No member is known to lift merely because its center class lies in (12.58.3), and the existence of these pencils does not produce a rational full-root cover.

A degree-four rational full-root cover can have center image of degree one, two or four over \(K\), since the remaining root extension has power-of-two degree. A degree-two center image contributes a doubled degree-two divisor to \(\operatorname{Sym}^4(C)\). The pencil classification applies to that class but does not discard the case. In particular, neither the absence of other tetragonal pencils nor the trace signature (12.58.7) is a quartic-cover exclusion.


### 12.59. Uniform dyadic kernel reduction and odd-prime normalization strata

The local restrictions here start with the full five-root curve and
do not assume the surviving $P'$ representative. After rational base
symmetries, dyadic arithmetic reduces the sixteen joint cover orbits
to four. Three of those already have a $P'$ factor and hence the
genus-three reduction of Section 12.49. Only the orbit
$(P'+Q',P'+Q')$ is new, and it requires a deeper dyadic base chart.
A point outside the known boundary Kummer spans retains a rank-at-least-three
alternative; no specialized rank upper bound is inferred.

Use
\[
h=1-m^2,\quad A=1+m^2,\quad\alpha=m^2-3,\quad\gamma=1-3m^2,
\quad B=4h,\quad d=B^2/A,
\]
and the actual five roots
\[
\sigma^2=D=A(1+n^2),\quad u^2=D+Bn,\quad v^2=D-Bn,
\quad a^2=D+4m(1-n^2),\quad b^2=D-4m(1-n^2).
\tag{U-DYADIC-FULL-ROOTS}
\]
On $E':Y^2=X(X+d-2B)(X+d+2B)$, index the uniformly independent
boundary basis by $(a_0,b_0,p_0,q_0)=(T_0,T_1,P',Q')$. Its first two
full-Kummer coordinates are
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
 &\delta_1&\delta_2\\\hline
a_0&-\alpha\gamma&2h\gamma A\\
b_0&-2h\gamma A&-2\gamma A\\
p_0&\alpha A&-hA\\
q_0&\gamma A&h\gamma
\end{array}
\tag{U-DYADIC-GLOBAL-BASIS}
\]
These are actual global squareclasses. The kernel of the full Kummer
map is $2E'(\mathbb Q)$. Its boundary span has dimension four on
every permitted rational fiber; a candidate outside it forces the
corresponding symmetric elliptic rank to be at least three.

**Normalization of every rational base.** The map $m\mapsto1/m$
scales all roots by $1/m$ and interchanges $u,v$. The simultaneous
reflection
\[
m'=(m-1)/(m+1),\quad n'=(n-1)/(n+1),\quad
\lambda=2/((m+1)(n+1))
\]
carries the roots to $\lambda(\sigma,b,a,v,u)$. Both transformations
are exact rational full-root isomorphisms. When $v_2(m)=0$, exactly
one of $m-1,m+1$ has valuation one and the other has valuation at
least two. Reflection therefore makes $v_2(m)$ nonzero; inversion
makes it positive. Every rational full-root point consequently has
a representative with
\[
e=v_2(m)\ge1.
\tag{U-DYADIC-BASE-NORMALIZATION}
\]
Now $A$ is a unit. A unit $n$ would give $v_2(\sigma^2)=1$, which is
impossible. The exact $n\mapsto1/n$ automorphism, scaling roots by
$1/n$ and interchanging $a,b$, lets us take $v_2(n)\ge1$. Reducing
the central equation modulo eight gives
\[
v_2(n)=1\Longleftrightarrow e=1;
\qquad\text{otherwise both valuations are at least two.}
\]
All five roots are units. Choose their independent signs so that
$u,v,a,b\equiv1\pmod4$, and put $L=(u+v)/2$, $M=(a+b)/2$, both odd.
The rational exceptional $n$-charts are already excluded by the
complete degenerate-locus theorem; the local zero/infinity charts
are retained below.

**Actual dyadic classes.** For the f image the two coordinates are
\[
\eta=(u+v)^2-d=4(L^2-4h^2/A),\qquad
\eta+d-2B=4(L^2-2h).
\]
The parenthesized units are respectively $5,7\pmod8$, so
\[
\delta_f=(5,-1)\quad\text{in }(\mathbb Q_2^\times/\mathbb Q_2^{\times2})^2.
\]
For the reflected g image,
\[
Z_g=\frac{16M^2}{(m+1)^2(n+1)^2},\quad
d_g=\frac{128m^2}{A(m+1)^2},
\]
and exactly
\[
\frac{d_g}{Z_g}=\frac{8m^2(n+1)^2}{AM^2}\in32\mathbb Z_2,
\qquad \frac{2B_g}{Z_g}=\frac{2m(n+1)^2}{M^2}.
\]
Thus its first coordinate is square and its second has unit class
$1-2m$, equal to the class of $A$. Hence $\delta_g=(1,A)$.

Substitution in (U-DYADIC-GLOBAL-BASIS) gives the complete local table:

| Factor | $a_0$ | $b_0$ | $p_0$ | $q_0$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| f at $m$ | $(3,2h)$ | $(-2h,-2)$ | $(5,-1)$ | $(1,1)$ |
| g at $m'$ | $(-1,-2m)$ | $(2m,2)$ | $(-1,-2mA)$ | $(-1,-2mA)$ |

For the second row use
\[
h'=\frac{4m}{(m+1)^2},\quad A'=\frac{2A}{(m+1)^2},\quad
\alpha'=\frac{-2(A+4m)}{(m+1)^2},\quad
\gamma'=\frac{-2(A-4m)}{(m+1)^2}.
\]
Both $A(A\pm4m)$ and $A^2-16m^2$ are $1\pmod8$. These formulas
retain the valuation of $2m$ and cover arbitrarily large $e$.

Write a mask $a_0^i b_0^j p_0^k q_0^l$, and put $t=k+l$ in
$\mathbb F_2$. In f, the first valuation forces $j=0$, the second
forces $i=0$, and the unit class forces $k=1$. For g put $w=i+t$.
Its equations are
\[
(-1)^w(2m)^j=1,\qquad (-2m)^w2^jA^t=A.
\]
If $e$ is even, valuation parity gives $j=0$ then $w=0$. If $e$ is
odd, the second valuation first gives $j=0$, after which the first
unit equation gives $w=0$, since $-1$ is nonsquare. Therefore $A^t=A$.
The root flips add $a_0$ independently; proper n-inversion adds
$p_0+q_0$ only in f, and n-negation adds it only in g. These exact
cover isomorphisms preserve $j,t$. Consequently the necessary
conditions without the temporary sign and n choices are
\[
\boxed{j_f=j_g=0;\qquad e=1\Longrightarrow t_g=1.}
\tag{U-DYADIC-ORBIT-RESTRICTION}
\]
The local chart $n=0$ obeys the same unit calculation whenever
soluble; $n=\infty$ is transported to it by proper inversion. The
full Kummer map is continuous with its standard values at $O$ and
two-torsion, so those charts cannot hide points. No zero root is
possible after the even-n unit normalization; $n=\pm1$ is already
locally forbidden by the central valuation.

Each joint orbit has sixteen masks and is indexed by
$(j_f,t_f,j_g,t_g)$. Thus at least192 of the256 indexed covers are
dyadically empty at every normalized base, and at least224 are empty
when $e=1$. The four remaining orbit representatives can be chosen
\[
(p_0,p_0),\quad(p_0,p_0q_0),\quad(p_0q_0,p_0),\quad(p_0q_0,p_0q_0).
\]
Any orbit with a $p_0$ factor gives the known $P'$ genus-three
reduction, using reflection for a g factor. The sole new joint orbit
is $(P'+Q',P'+Q')$, and it requires $e\ge2$.

This proves the all-base alternative: after exact rational base
symmetries, a full-root point either gives a new full-Kummer direction
and a symmetric rank at least three, or reaches a $P'$ genus-three
cover, or belongs to the single new joint orbit with $v_2(m)\ge2$.
If both symmetric ranks are two, the first alternative is absent.
No assertion of global emptiness is made for either surviving type.

**An independently complete odd-prime stratum.** The good-reduction
condition for the five binary quadratics at an odd prime is
\[
\Delta_0(m)=m(1-m^2)(1+m^2)(m^2-3)(1-3m^2)
 (m^4-14m^2+1)(m^4-6m^2+1)\ne0.
\tag{U-KUMMER-GOOD-BASE}
\]
It follows from their discriminants and pairwise resultants. The
selected bases below satisfy it, as do the elliptic models and every
boundary representative.

The finite calculation tests all five radicands, including zero, for
every $n\in\mathbb F_l$ and in the projective infinity chart. It
enumerates the actual products $uv,ab$ and evaluates
\[
x_f=2A(1+n^2)-d+2uv,\qquad
x_g=\frac{8(A(1+n^2)+ab)}{(m+1)^2(n+1)^2}-d'.
\]
At $n=-1$ the g map gives $O$ or $T_0$; at $n=\infty$ the f map
does likewise and g is evaluated on leading root products. At an
elliptic root, its vanishing Kummer coordinate is replaced by the
product of the other root differences; at $O$ the vector is trivial.
Good odd reduction has a uniquely two-divisible formal kernel, so
this finite Kummer evaluation agrees with the local class. The
boundary representatives are units. Proper reduction therefore
covers rational points with arbitrary n-valuations, including
nonintegral n; no assumption that elliptic coordinates remain units
is made.

The complete tables are:

| Prime | Base residues | Necessary mask conditions |
|---|---|---|
| 19 | $4,5,14,15$ | $j_g=0$, $j_f+t_f=1$ |
| 19 | $7,8,11,12$ | $j_f=0$, $j_g+t_g=1$ |
| 29 | $4,7,22,25$ | $j_f=0$, $t_g=1$ |
| 29 | $8,11,18,21$ | $t_f=1$, $j_g=0$ |

Every selected finite curve has exactly128 points, above
$n=\pm m,\pm1/m$, with all32 root sign choices at each. Each row

The constraints also follow from the separate f and g projections:
using an f row does not first require the g vector to belong to its

Let $m=p/q$ with $\gcd(q,551)=1$. Either of the following CRT

For rational m the condition is $p\equiv cq\pmod{551}$; its numerator

### 12.60. Uniform deck restriction and all quadratic fixed loci

The completed cubic calculation leaves projection degrees at least four.
There is also a uniform restriction on the degree over the image, independent
of those projection degrees.

**Theorem 12.60.1.** Let \(Y\) be a curve over \(\mathbb Q\) on the
full-root surface, with normalization \(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\), meeting
the admissible locus. Then:

1. Its degree over its \((m,n)\)-image is one or two; degree four is
   impossible, without any bound on \(\deg m\) or \(\deg n\).
2. A nontrivial image-cover involution can change only the central root,
   only one edge root, or one \(F\)-edge together with one \(G\)-edge.
   These are exactly nine directions left by the fixed-locus obstruction.
3. Its degree over its image in the genus-five center model is one or two.
   In the latter case the involution changes only the central root. All
   four individual edge roots already belong to the center-image field.

The nine directions are necessary possibilities, not nine constructed
families. In particular, a degree-two image does not inherit a full-root
point if its missing root lies only in the double cover.

**12.60.1. Complete fixed loci over fields of degree at most two.**

Use the homogeneous radicands
\[
 F_0=(1+m^2)(1+n^2),\qquad
 F_\pm=F_0\pm4n(1-m^2),\qquad
 G_\pm=F_0\pm4m(1-n^2).
\]
The projective versions are obtained by replacing \(m,n\) with their two
homogeneous coordinate pairs. The sign deck group is \(V=C_2^5\), in
slot order \(F_0,F_+,F_-,G_+,G_-\).

The quadratic zero-edge theorem of Section12.43 determines every full-root
point of residue degree at most two at which an edge root vanishes. The
center cannot vanish there: that would require both \(i\) and \(\sqrt2\)
in the residue field. With nonzero center, the ratio of the opposite edge
root to the center forces the field \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\). The rank-zero
calculation on \(Y^2=X^3-X\) over this field gives only the degenerate
normalized offsets. The inverse Segre formulas, over all signs and proper
charts, give
\[
 m\in S=\{1+\sqrt2,1-\sqrt2,-1+\sqrt2,-1-\sqrt2\}.
\]
Interchanging the two variables in that already complete theorem gives
\(n\in S\) as well.

The exact zero masks are particularly simple. Write
\(m=\varepsilon+\delta\sqrt2\), with \(\varepsilon,\delta=\pm1\).
Then \(m^2-2\varepsilon m-1=0\). The four possible \(n\)-values and
zero roots are

| \(n\) | Vanishing edges |
|---|---|
| \(m\) | \(F_\varepsilon,G_\varepsilon\) |
| \(-m\) | \(F_{-\varepsilon},G_\varepsilon\) |
| \(1/m\) | \(F_\varepsilon,G_{-\varepsilon}\) |
| \(-1/m\) | \(F_{-\varepsilon},G_{-\varepsilon}\) |

Thus exactly one \(F\)-edge and one \(G\)-edge vanish. The center is
nonzero, and each of the two remaining radicands is \(2F_0\). Actual
square witnesses are \(\sqrt{F_0}=1+m^2\) when \(n=\pm m\), or
\((1+m^2)/m\) when \(n=\pm1/m\), and \(\sqrt2\) times this root for
the remaining edges. This proves both necessity and existence of all
sixteen base pairs in the table; no opposite-edge or center-edge zero
mask occurs over a quadratic field.

The remaining fixed locus is the center-zero one. The homogeneous
identity \(F_0=0\) forces \(m=\pm i\) or \(n=\pm i\), hence the field
is \(\mathbb Q(i)\). By symmetry and conjugation take \(m=i\). Then
\[
 F_+=8n,\qquad G_+=4i(1-n^2).
\]
For actual roots \(f^2=F_+,g^2=G_+\), set
\[
 X=2in,\qquad Y=fg/2.
\]
They give a point on
\[
 E_+:Y^2=X^3+4X.                                  \tag{12.60.1}
\]
The map \((x,y)\mapsto(x-1/x,y(1+1/x^2))\) is a two-isogeny from
\(y^2=x^3-x\) to (12.60.1), so the previous rational rank-zero theorem
also gives \(\operatorname{rank}E_+(\mathbb Q)=0\). Its quadratic twist
by \(-1\) is the same model. Consequently
\(\operatorname{rank}E_+(\mathbb Q(i))=0\). Good reduction at the split
primes 5 and 13 gives eight points in each residue field. The complete
group therefore consists of
\[
 O,(0,0),(2,\pm4),(-2,\pm4i),(2i,0),(-2i,0).
\]
The possible finite \(n\)-coordinates are \(0,\pm1,\pm i\).
At \(n=0\), a root of \(4i\) would be required; at \(n=\pm1\), a
root of \(\pm8\) would be required. These are impossible since neither
\(i\) nor 2 is a square in \(\mathbb Q(i)\). The projective \(n=\infty\)
chart again requires a root of \(\pm4i\), so adds nothing. Thus
\(n=\pm i\). Conversely all four pairs
\[
                    (m,n)=(\pm i,\pm i)            \tag{12.60.2}
\]
have actual edge roots in \(\mathbb Q(i)\): for \(m=ei,n=fi\), roots
of \(F_+,F_-,G_+,G_-\) are respectively
\(2+2fi,2-2fi,2+2ei,2-2ei\). All four edges are nonzero.

This classifies all quadratic fixed-locus base points, including infinity
and zero-center charts. The finite exact certificate is
`next_pythagorean_cover/verify_quadratic_fixed_loci.py/.json`; the
center-zero computation was also obtained independently in
`simultaneous_units/central_zero_quadratic_points.md` and its verifier.

**12.60.2. Only nine involution directions remain.**

A nonidentity involution of \(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\) has two distinct
geometric fixed points, each defined over a field of degree at most two.
Their images are fixed points on the full-root surface. The four corner
coordinates cannot vanish simultaneously: the defining equations would
then force all projective coordinates to vanish. Since a sign deck
transformation fixes the corner coordinates, its fixed projective scalar
is \(+1\). Every changed root therefore really vanishes.

If an edge sign is changed, the table above forces its support to be a
nonempty subset of a single cross pair \(\{F_\varepsilon,G_\delta\}\).
If no edge is changed, only the central sign can be changed. The surviving
supports are precisely
\[
 \{F_0\};\quad\{F_+\},\{F_-\},\{G_+\},\{G_-\};\quad
             \{F_\varepsilon,G_\delta\}\ (\varepsilon,\delta=\pm1).
                                                               \tag{12.60.3}
\]
In the five-bit convention their masks are
\(1,2,4,8,16,10,18,12,20\). All center-plus-edge directions, both
opposite-edge pairs, and every direction changing three or four edges
are thereby excluded at every projection degree. The fixed fields are
\(\mathbb Q(i)\) in the central case and \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\) in the
other eight cases. These conclusions hold even when the image curve
itself is singular, since its normalization maps properly to the surface.

**12.60.3. A rational Klein-four image cover is impossible.**

The previous deck reduction gives image degree \(1,2\), or 4. In the
last case the stabilizer is a constant, \(\mathbb Q\)-defined Klein-four
group \(H\) acting faithfully on the rational normalization. Its quotient
is \(\mathbb P^1_{\mathbb Q}\).

For a nonidentity \(h\in H\), its two fixed points form one \(H\)-orbit.
Indeed the other involutions commute with \(h\), and cannot fix either
point separately: finite point stabilizers in \(\operatorname{PGL}_2\) in
characteristic zero are cyclic. Their common quotient image is rational,
since the fixed pair is Galois-stable. Thus all three inertia-labelled
branch values of this Klein-four cover are rational. In particular the
functions \(m,n\) on the quotient take rational values at every fixed
point, with infinity included.

A rank-two subgroup of \(V\) contains an element changing an edge sign,
since the central-only subspace has rank one. Its fixed image point has
residue degree at most two, so the quadratic zero-edge theorem makes its
\(m\)-coordinate one of \(\pm1\pm\sqrt2\), which is irrational. This
contradicts the rationality just proved. Hence the image degree is never
four. This argument imposes no bound on either projection degree.

**12.60.4. The residual cover of the center image.**

The degree-eight map from the full-root curve to the center curve retains
\(n\), \(f_+f_-\), and \(g_+g_-\). Its deck subgroup is generated by
changing the central sign, changing both \(F\)-signs, and changing both
\(G\)-signs. Every noncentral element of this subgroup changes an
opposite-edge pair. None appears in (12.60.3), so none can preserve a
rational curve nontrivially.

Consequently the degree over the center image is at most two. If it is
two, the only possible involution is central-only. It fixes every
individual edge root, proving that all four edge roots already lie in
the rational center-image field. Only the central root may be missing.

For projection degree four this separates two genuinely different
problems: a degree-four center point with all roots in its residue field,
or a degree-two center point with all four edge roots and a further
rational quadratic central extension. The latter is not a full-root
quadratic family and is not discarded by the earlier degree-two theorem;
Section 12.61 supplies its separate exclusion.

Finally, in the ten halfcanonical center pencils the pair \((U,V)\)
would have \(n\in K\) and an irreducible quartic full-root residue field,
hence image-cover degree four; it is now excluded. The central-involution
argument already excludes the four pairs containing \(Z\) and the pair
\((C,D)\). Section 12.61 subsequently excludes the four remaining intersection pencils \((C,U),(C,V),(D,U),(D,V)\) as well. They have quadratic \((m,n)\)-image
and still require their actual residual root conditions. No assertion is
made here that a general effective quartic center divisor belongs to a
pencil.


### 12.61. Quartic center reductions and the ten halfcanonical pencils

The uniform deck restriction closes a further whole stratum in projection
degree four. The argument retains the central root in the field where it
actually lives; it does not invoke the earlier full-root quadratic theorem
on a field missing that root.

**Theorem 12.61.1.** A nondegenerate rational full-root family with
\(m\)-degree four is birational to its center image. Its center divisor
cannot belong to any of the ten halfcanonical tetragonal pencils. Thus a
remaining quartic family gives an irreducible degree-four center point,
with every full root in the same residue field, whose moving class, if
any, lies away from the intersections of the five elliptic pencil
components.

Birationality to the center image does not assert birationality to the
\((m,n)\)-image. A residual degree-two image cover can still occur inside
the quartic center field.

**12.61.1. The only possible smaller center field.**

By Section12.60 the only nontrivial cover of a rational center image is
central-only. Suppose this occurs. Write
\[
 K=\mathbb Q(m),\qquad F=\mathbb Q(s),\qquad L=\mathbb Q(t),
 \qquad [F:K]=[L:F]=2.
\]
All four individual edge roots belong to \(F\), while
\(f_0^2=(1+m^2)(1+n^2)\) generates \(L/F\). The four-edge construction
supplies the actual offset point \(Q\in E_Z(F)\) with \(Z=2Q+P\).
Its center expression is already a square through
\(R=(1+n^2)/(1-n^2)\); this does not require \(f_0\in F\).

The central involution has two fixed points, and the complete quadratic
fixed-locus theorem makes their \((m,n)\)-values \((\pm i,\pm i)\).
If the quadratic map \(m:\mathbb P^1_s\to\mathbb P^1_m\) ramifies at
one of them, it ramifies at both by conjugation. These exhaust its
ramification, so
\[
                    F=K\bigl(\sqrt{c(1+m^2)}\bigr)
                                                               \tag{12.61.1}
\]
for a rational constant squareclass \(c\). The all-constant central-circle
theorem gives the exact old elliptic group over every such rational
cover. Hence \(Q\) is old, and the completed old-section center theorem
excludes a nonboundary rational lift.

We may assume that this quadratic \(m\)-map is unramified at both
central branch points. Also \(n\) is primitive in \(F/K\): otherwise
the full degree-four field \(L\) would be a degree-four root cover of its
graph \((m,n)\)-image, which Section12.60 excludes. Thus \(F=K(n)\).

**12.61.2. A ramification loss gives the same finite trace range.**

The full degree-four \(m\)-map has ramification budget six. Its two
central ramification points lie over the beta-bad fibers \(m=\pm i\)
and consume two units outside \(r_0,r_o,r_\alpha,r_\gamma\). Therefore
\[
 r_0+r_o+r_\alpha+r_\gamma\le4,
 \qquad
 \widehat h_L(Q),\widehat h_L(Q+P)
       \le48+r_0/2+r_o\le52.
\]
The corresponding heights over \(F\) are at most 26. Put
\[
 \operatorname{Tr}_{F/K}Q=kP+T_2,\qquad
 \operatorname{Tr}_{F/K}Z=2jP,\qquad j=k+1.
\]
The trace-height inequality gives
\(3k^2\le52\) and \(3(k+2)^2\le52\). Thus \(k=-4,\ldots,2\), or
\(j=-3,\ldots,3\).

The full trace over \(L\) is \(4jP\). Applying the established
coordinate/intersection inequality with \(M=4,u=4j\) gives
\[
 4N_L\le204-24|j|+2r_0+4r_o+2r_\alpha+r_\gamma
         \le220-24|j|.
\]
Since \(n\in F\), \(N_L=2N_F\). The resulting bounds are
\[
 \begin{array}{c|rrrr}
 |j|&0&1&2&3\\ \hline
 N_F\text{ at most}&27&24&21&18.
 \end{array}                                                   \tag{12.61.2}
\]
No parity assertion for \(N_F\), and no local central-root refinement
over \(F\), is used. In particular the middle bound is 21, not the
full-root quadratic bound 20.

**12.61.3. Nonzero traces reuse the exact fixed elliptic reduction.**

The fixed \(E_D\) reduction of Section12.48 uses only the actual signed
trace of \(Z\), the conic formula \(r=2n/(1-n^2)\), and the actual
rational duplication roots of \(x(2jP)\). Thus it remains valid over
\(F\) with only the four edge roots. Write
\(S=n+\sigma n,T=n\sigma n\). Its explicit genus-one map again gives
an actual point of the fixed curve \(E_D(K)\), with no unrecorded twist.

For that point the height bound is
\[
 \widehat h(A_D)\le16+2\bigl(N_F+h(d_{j,\varepsilon})\bigr).
\]
The previously certified degree pairs are \((8,2),(12,14),(32,26)\).
Combining them with (12.61.2) yields

| \(|j|\) | \(N_F\) bound | Maximum auxiliary height | Multiplier bound |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 24 | 80 | 8 |
| 2 | 21 | 86 | 9 |
| 3 | 18 | 116 | 10 |

The height 86 in the second row still gives radius nine. Thus the list
is exactly the same 432 non-torsion points already tested in Section12.48,
with both signs and all four torsion translates. The 428 exact regular
nonsquare witnesses for the reconstructed \(S^2\) do not use the central
root. The four exact survivors have split or zero discriminant and make
\(n\in K\), contradicting primitivity. Reusing these certificates
requires no new point search.

The four auxiliary torsion points give \(T=\pm1\). The \(T=-1\)
case is treated below rather than discarded by falsely placing \(f_0\)
in \(F\). If \(T=1\), the two offset abscissae coincide. Nonzero trace
makes \(Z\) old; since \(2Q=Z-P\), the uniform no-new-halves theorem on
rational quadratic \(m\)-covers makes \(Q\) old. The old-center genus
theorem then excludes the nonboundary curve. Its center-square
hypothesis is already supplied by \(R\in F\). The fixed elliptic
isomorphism retains all remaining pole and infinity charts.

**12.61.4. Trace zero and the newly retained inverse-negative branch.**

For zero trace the exact factorization gives
\(S=0,T=1,T=-1\). The old \(S=0\) and \(T=1\) arguments require only
the four edge roots. For \(S=0\), conjugation interchanges the two
\(F\)-roots with matching signs, making \(U\) invariant; the actual
signed zero trace forces \(V\) invariant, and \(R\) is invariant
directly. For \(T=1\), the divided \(G\)-roots make \(V\)
anti-invariant, zero trace makes \(U\) anti-invariant, and \(R\) is
anti-invariant. The simultaneous Mobius transformation gives the
invariant coordinates \(V/(pr),U/(pr),R/r\), reducing to the same exact
\(E_C\) coset.

That argument needs only \(N_F\le30\); (12.61.2) gives 27. Its
multiplier bound is therefore still \(|k|\le4\). The exact quadratic
cover genera for \(k=0,1,2,3,4\) are \(1,\mathrm{split},9,17,33\).
The split case makes \(n\) old; all other cases have positive genus and
cannot have rational normalization. Hence \(S=0\) and \(T=1\) are
excluded without a central root in \(F\).

It remains to treat \(T=-1\), which now has genuine mathematical
content. Here \(\sigma n=-1/n\), and \(\sigma\) extends to \(L\) by
\[
                       \widetilde\sigma(f_0)=f_0/n.
\]
This is an actual extension because \(\sigma(F_0)=F_0/n^2\). Its square
fixes \(F\) and negates \(f_0\), so it has order four. Thus \(L/K\)
is cyclic quartic. An order-four Mobius transformation has the same two
fixed points as its square; its rational quotient has precisely two
branch values, both of index four. The square is central-only, so the
quadratic fixed-locus theorem identifies these values as \(m=i,-i\).
The intermediate field is exactly (12.61.1).

The all-constant central-circle theorem now gives
\(E_Z(F)=E_Z(K)\). Hence \(Q\) is old and \(Z=2Q+P\) is an old odd
multiple of the nontorsion point \(P\), whose trace cannot be zero. In
the nonzero-trace \(T=-1\) chart the old-center theorem supplies the
same exclusion. This closes the only branch where the earlier direct
central-root argument could not be reused.

We have excluded the entire missing-central quadratic center image.
The detailed hypothesis audit is
`next_pythagorean_cover/quartic_central_residual_exclusion.md` and the
independent review is
`simultaneous_units/central_residual_quartic_review.md`. The 432-case
arithmetic remains the existing exact Section12.48 certificate, with the
changed height bound recorded explicitly above.

**12.61.5. All ten halfcanonical quartic pencils are excluded.**

Index the coordinate involutions of \(C_5\) by \(C,Z,V,U,D\), in
coordinate order \(r,R,U,V,t\). The diagonal canonical net has five
rank-four components and ten rank-three intersections. The rank-three
quadric omitting coordinates \(i,j\) gives a degree-four conic quotient
with deck group \(\langle\tau_i,\tau_j\rangle\cong C_2^2\). Its fiber
at the projected boundary point is
\[
 D_{ij}=B_0+B_{\tau_i}+B_{\tau_j}+B_{\tau_i\tau_j},
                   \qquad 2D_{ij}\sim K_{C_5}.     \tag{12.61.3}
\]
The exact tangent hyperplanes prove (12.61.3), and the ten fibers have
\(h^0=2\). Every divisor in one of these pencils is an actual fiber of
that conic quotient.

An irreducible quartic fiber has a residue field \(L/K\) with that
constant Klein-four Galois group. The first part of the theorem has
already made the full-root field equal to the center field, so these
involutions act on the rational full-root normalization as well. Their
actions on \(n\) are
\[
 \tau_C:n\mapsto-n,\quad \tau_Z:n\mapsto-1/n,\quad
 \tau_U,\tau_V:n\mapsto n,\quad \tau_D:n\mapsto1/n.
                                                               \tag{12.61.4}
\]
No order-two field automorphism can send \(n\) to \(-1/n\) when the
central root belongs to the field: its action on \(f_0\) would be
\(\pm f_0/n\), whose square negates \(f_0\). Hence all four pairs
containing \(Z\), and the pair \((C,D)\), are excluded. The pair
\((U,V)\) would have \(n\in K\) and image-cover degree four, which
Section12.60 excludes.

Consider the four remaining pairs individually:

| Pair | Involution fixing \(n\) | Required edge action |
|---|---|---|
| \((C,U)\) | \(\tau_U\) | one \(G\)-edge sign |
| \((D,U)\) | \(\tau_U\) | one \(G\)-edge sign |
| \((C,V)\) | \(\tau_V\) | one \(F\)-edge sign |
| \((D,V)\) | \(\tau_V\) | one \(F\)-edge sign |

Indeed \(\tau_U\) fixes \(m,n,U\) and negates \(V\). As an
involution of the actual full-root field fixing \(m,n\), it is a sign
deck transformation with even \(F\)-parity and odd \(G\)-parity. The
nine-direction theorem leaves only a single \(G\)-edge sign. The
\(\tau_V\) cases are the exchanged statement.

The rational degree-four \(m\)-cover here is Klein-four, so every
inertia-labelled branch value on the \(m\)-line is rational by the
branch lemma of Section12.60. But a fixed point of the indicated edge
involution has quadratic residue field and \(m=\pm1\pm\sqrt2\), which
is irrational. This contradiction excludes each of the four rows. The
argument uses the Klein-four cover over \(m\), not an incorrectly
asserted degree-four cover over \((m,n)\).

All ten halfcanonical pencils are therefore closed. The certificates
`next_pythagorean_cover/verify_center_tetragonal_net.py/.json` give the
exact net, boundary fibers and sign actions. General quartic classes
with \(h^0=1\), and the nonintersection parts of the surviving elliptic
pencil components, remain for further common-lift analysis.


### 12.62. Zero constant trace of the full genus-forty-nine Jacobian

The full Jacobian has no constant part over $\mathbb C(m)$. Consequently its function-field canonical height is positive definite modulo torsion. This supplies a height-theoretic input beyond the five center factors; it does not compute the full Mordell--Weil lattice or complete the quartic reduction.

Put $A=1+m^2$, $h=1-m^2$, and retain
\[
F_0=A(1+n^2),\qquad
F_{1,\epsilon}=A(1+n^2)+4\epsilon hn,\qquad
F_{2,\epsilon}=A(1+n^2)+4\epsilon m(1-n^2).
\]
Let $X$ be the full genus-forty-nine curve over $K=\mathbb C(m)$ and $J=\operatorname{Jac}(X)$. For every nonempty subset $S$ of the five radical labels, let
\[
C_S:\quad y^2=\prod_{j\in S}F_j
\]
denote its smooth projective model. Its genus is $|S|-1$. The five commuting deck involutions split rational cohomology into their character spaces, and quotient pullback identifies $H^1(C_S)$ with the corresponding character space. Thus
\[
J\sim_K\prod_{S\ne\varnothing}\operatorname{Jac}(C_S).
\tag{U-FULL-CHARACTER-ISOGENY}
\]
The factors containing the central label have total dimension $32$, and those omitting it have total dimension $17$.

**The seventeen noncentral elliptic factors.** Define
\[
\begin{aligned}
P(t)&=A^2(1+t)^2-16h^2t,\\
L_\epsilon(t)&=A(1+t)+4\epsilon m(1-t),\\
Q_\epsilon(t)&=P(t)L_\epsilon(t),\\
R_\epsilon(t)&=8\bigl[(A+2\epsilon h)+(A-2\epsilon h)t\bigr]
                    \bigl[A^2(1+t)^2-64m^2t\bigr],\\
Q_4(t)&=P(t)L_+(t)L_-(t),\\
K_4(t)&=16(1-t)(A^2-16m^2t)(A^2-4h^2+4h^2t).
\end{aligned}
\tag{U-FULL-NONCENTRAL-MODELS}
\]
The noncentral product in (U-FULL-CHARACTER-ISOGENY) is isogenous to the following seventeen elliptic Jacobians:

| Character source | Exact genus-one equations | Number |
|---|---|---:|
| Two of the four noncentral labels | $y^2=F_i(n)F_j(n)$, $i<j$ | 6 |
| $F_{1,+}F_{1,-}F_{2,\epsilon}$ | $y^2=Q_\epsilon(t)$ and $y^2=tQ_\epsilon(t)$ | 4 |
| $F_{1,\epsilon}F_{2,+}F_{2,-}$ | $y^2=R_\epsilon(t)$ and $y^2=tR_\epsilon(t)$ | 4 |
| All four noncentral labels | $y^2=Q_4(t)$, $y^2=K_4(t)$, $y^2=tK_4(t)$ | 3 |

The quotient maps of an even sextic $y^2=Q(n^2)$ are $(n,y)\mapsto(n^2,y)$ and $(n,y)\mapsto(n^2,ny)$; their differential eigenspaces are complementary. The reciprocal triple-character sextics become even under
\[
n_{\rm old}=\frac{1+n_{\rm new}}{1-n_{\rm new}},\qquad
y_{\rm new}=(1-n_{\rm new})^3y_{\rm old}.
\]
For the all-four character, the first quotient is $y^2=Q_4(t)$ and the other is $Y^2=tQ_4(t)$; the same Cayley change makes the latter an even sextic with polynomial $K_4$. All scalar factors in these formulas are retained.

Each of the seventeen elliptic factors has nonconstant $j$. This is certified by the binary-quartic invariants $I=12ae-3bd+c^2$, $J=72ace+9bcd-27ad^2-27b^2e-2c^3$ and $j=6912I^3/(4I^3-J^2)$. Their exact rational values at $m=2$ and $m=4$ are finite and already differ modulo $101$:
\[
\begin{array}{c|c}
\text{models in the order just described}&(j(2),j(4))\bmod101\\\hline
F_{1,+}F_{1,-}&(41,28)\\
F_{1,\epsilon}F_{2,\eta}\ \text{(four models)}&(60,24)\\
F_{2,+}F_{2,-}&(69,65)\\
Q_+,tQ_+,Q_-,tQ_-&(77,27),(43,88),(43,88),(77,27)\\
R_+,tR_+,R_-,tR_-&(22,24),(38,30),(38,30),(22,24)\\
Q_4,K_4,tK_4&(39,28),(6,65),(65,28).
\end{array}
\]
A nonzero constant elliptic factor would make its $j$ algebraic over $\mathbb C$, hence constant. The noncentral dimension-seventeen part therefore has zero $K/\mathbb C$-trace.

**The central characters have negative unipotent local monodromy.** Fix a positive-genus $C_S$ containing $F_0$, and put $\tau=m-i$. It is the quadratic twist by $A$ of
\[
C'_S:\quad y'^2=(1+n^2)\prod_{j\in S\setminus\{0\}}F_j.
\]
In homogeneous coordinates $[N:Z]$, the four possible remaining factors at $m=i$ become
\[
8NZ,\quad-8NZ,\quad-4i(N-Z)(N+Z),\quad4i(N-Z)(N+Z).
\]
The fixed roots $n=\pm i$ stay simple. All other collisions are pairs: at $0,\infty$ when both $F_1$ signs occur, or at $\pm1$ when both $F_2$ signs occur. The root derivatives with respect to $m$ are respectively
\[
(-i/4,i/4),\quad(-i/4,i/4),\quad(1/2,-1/2),\quad(-1/2,1/2),
\]
using $1/n$ at infinity. Thus every pair separates to first order. Each local double-cover singularity is analytically
\[
y^2=(x-a(\tau))(x-b(\tau)),\quad
\operatorname{ord}_\tau(a-b)=1,
\qquad\text{hence}\qquad uv=\tau^2\cdot\text{unit}.
\]
Resolving these ordinary double points gives a reduced nodal model without a ramified base change. Its local $H^1$ monodromy $U$ is unipotent; equivalently the disjoint colliding pairs give commuting squared Picard--Lefschetz transvections. The semistable-unipotent implication is also recorded in Illusie, *Grothendieck and vanishing cycles*, Remark 3.5(a) [55].

Since $A$ has a simple zero, going around $\tau=0$ reverses $\sqrt A$. The twist therefore multiplies $U$ by the hyperelliptic involution, which acts as $-I$ on $H^1$. The original character has monodromy $-U$, with every eigenvalue equal to $-1$. A nonzero constant abelian subvariety would yield a nonzero trivial-monodromy subspace in homology, which is impossible. This proves zero trace for the entire central dimension-thirty-two part.

Combining the character factors yields
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb C(m)/\mathbb C}J=0,
\qquad \operatorname{Tr}_{\mathbb Q(m)/\mathbb Q}J=0.}
\tag{U-FULL-JACOBIAN-TRACE-ZERO}
\]
The second assertion follows by extending any proposed nonzero constant map from $\mathbb Q$ to $\mathbb C$. By the Lang--Neron theorem and positivity modulo trace [54, Theorems 7.1 and 9.15], $J(\mathbb C(m))$ is finitely generated and every ample symmetric canonical height is positive definite on its real vector space modulo torsion.

The trace here is over the stated constant-field extension. No absence of potentially constant factors after arbitrary finite base change is asserted: an even ramified cover can remove the negative monodromy sign. Nor does (U-FULL-JACOBIAN-TRACE-ZERO) compute the integral lattice, torsion, or height constants. The five known center traces still leave forty-four Jacobian dimensions without the arithmetic controls needed for a complete quartic enumeration.

Exact models and all specialization and local-derivative identities are recorded in `rank4_next/trace_center_norm/verify_full_jacobian_trace_zero.py/.json`. The complete proof is in the companion `full_jacobian_trace_zero.md`; the independent review and separate mod-$101$ calculations are in `simultaneous_units/full_jacobian_trace_zero_review.md/.json`.


### 12.63. The remaining joint orbit forces a coupled rank gain

Retain h=1−m², A=1+m², α=m²−3, γ=1−3m², B=4h and d=B²/A. Let p,q be the full Kummer vectors of P′,Q′ on E′. The dyadic reduction leaves one orbit beyond the covers having a boundary factor: (pq,pq). Here pq is the class of P′+Q′, whose first two coordinates are (αγ,−γA).

For its f-factor write η=(u+v)²−d=4αγR²/A² and η+d−2B=−4γS²/A. The exact quotient is
\[
 \alpha R^2+AS^2=-2hA,\qquad
 Y^2=A(\alpha\gamma R^2+4h^2A)(R^2-A),\qquad
 n=\frac{Y}{A^2R}.                                      \tag{63.1}
\]
It has genus three: over x=R² the independent quadratic characters have five distinct branch points
\[
 0,\quad-2hA/\alpha,\quad-4h^2A/(\alpha\gamma),\quad A,\quad\infty.
\]
The original five roots remain necessary. In particular this quotient alone is not a point parametrization. Its R=0 chart has no rational point because Y²=−4h²A³<0. A rational infinity point would force −γ=3m²−1 to be a square, impossible by the sum-of-two-squares obstruction at 3. Thus every rational quotient point has finite nonzero R; on the full-root locus Y and the two factors in (63.1) are also nonzero.

There is a rational elliptic map
\[
 (x,y)=\left(\frac{\alpha\gamma R^2}{A},
                  \frac{\alpha\gamma RY}{A^2}\right)
 \in E_A(m):y^2=x(x+4h^2)(x-\alpha\gamma).               \tag{63.2}
\]
This is the same rank-one generic pencil as in the boundary P′ quotient. Its known boundary section is P_A=(αh²,αh²Am). In the root order (0,−4h²,αγ), its torsion and boundary Kummer vectors are
\[
 a_A=(-\alpha\gamma,1,-\alpha\gamma),\quad
 b_A=(-1,1,-1),\quad p_A=(\alpha,A,\alpha A).
\]
Since (u+v)²=4(αγR²+4h²A)/A², an actual full-root image in (63.2) has
\[
                 \delta_A=(\alpha\gamma A,A,\alpha\gamma).       \tag{63.3}
\]
If A is nonsquare, the three known vectors are independent and (63.3) lies outside their span. Indeed the second coordinate would force its p_A coefficient to be one; dividing by p_A would require γA to be one of 1,−1,αγ,−αγ. This contradicts the previously proved uniform nonsquareness of ±γA and ±αA. Hence rank E_A(m)(Q)≥2. When A is square, (63.3) is a_A b_A, so this argument correctly retains that exception on an individual factor.

The reflected factor has m′=(m−1)/(m+1) and A′=2A/(m+1)². The two quantities A,A′ cannot both be squares. Applying the same argument to both pq factors therefore proves
\[
 \boxed{\quad\operatorname{rank}E_A(m)(\mathbb Q)\ge2
       \quad\text{or}\quad
       \operatorname{rank}E_A(m')(\mathbb Q)\ge2.\quad}            \tag{63.4}
\]
Both ranks are at least two unless A or2A is square. This is a necessary specialized rank gain, not an exclusion of the orbit; no generic rank bound has been substituted for a specialized rank bound.

The quotient (63.1) itself has no Q(m)-section. Its finite nonzero image has first Kummer coordinate αγA, whereas the certified complete generic group of E_A has first-coordinate image generated by −1,α,γ. The factor m²+1 has odd valuation only in the former. The R=0 and infinity charts are excluded by the same polynomial-square obstructions; Y=0 would require R²=A or R²=−4h²A/(αγ), both again having odd A-valuation. This generic statement does not rule out specialized points.

There is an additional independent restriction retaining the individual roots. The exact cover automorphisms carry (pq,pq) to the identity pair. Then Z−2B,Z,Z+2B, with Z=(u+v)², are nonzero rational squares. If their roots are a,b,c, the sides c+a,c−a,2b give a rational right triangle of area |2B|. Scaling by1/2 gives area |2h|. The reflected progression has difference 2B′=32m/(m+1)² and gives area |2m| after scaling by |m+1|/4. Thus
\[
          |2m|\quad\text{and}\quad|2(1-m^2)|
          \quad\text{must both be rational congruent numbers}.  \tag{63.5}
\]
This can remove a specialized remaining orbit when either area is in a certified noncongruent squareclass. It is not asserted to remove every base.

Exact identities, all branch differences and the Kummer constants are certified in `coupled_lifts/pq_orbit_rank_gain.py/.json`; the complete argument and chart coverage are in its companion note. The dyadic reduction and this result together give a uniform alternative: a boundary-factor genus-three reduction, a symmetric elliptic rank at least three, or the coupled rank gain (63.4) together with the two triangle conditions (63.5).

The independent quotient, chart, specialized-rank and triangle-scaling audit is recorded in varying_primes/pq_orbit_independent_review.md; its exact reconstruction is in pq_three_factor_arithmetic.py/.json.


### 12.64. A complete necessary trace filter for primitive quartic center points

The quartic problem admits the following finite center-trace reduction. Sections 12.68–12.69 exclude its isolated classes and reduce the pencils to forty representatives; Sections 12.72–12.75 subsequently complete the exclusion of all rational full-root members. The non-strict bounds of Section 12.57 give 345,669 displayed tuples and eight possible primitive torsion masks for each, hence 2,765,352 states. Every irreducible quartic full-root point must have one of these states.

For a degree-four divisor \(D\), the normalized primitive free coordinates, in factor order \(Z,U,V,C,D\), are
\[
 \left((u-4)/2,\ k_U-4,\ k_V-4,\ k_C+4,\ k_D+4\right).
 \tag{U-QUARTIC-PRIMITIVE-COEFFICIENTS}
\]
Write the four free torsion bits as \(a,b,c,d\). Their parity is
\(a+b+c+d=(u-4)/2\) modulo two. The five factor torsion pairs are
\[
 (c+d,b+c),\quad(a,b),\quad(c+d,c),\quad(a+b,a),\quad(c,d).
 \tag{U-QUARTIC-PRIMITIVE-TORSION}
\]
These are the exact generic Jacobian-image equations applied to
\([D-4B_0]\); no arbitrary pointwise choice of halves is made.

**Proper specialization and all cycle types.** At each good rational base
and odd prime, the calculation enumerates the proper full genus-forty-nine
curve over the extensions of degrees one through four. It then forms the
five possible effective degree-four Frobenius cycle types:
\[
 1+1+1+1,\qquad1+1+2,\qquad2+2,\qquad1+3,\qquad4.
\]
Repeated points and repeated degree-two closed points are allowed.
Frobenius orbits are taken on the original five-root curve before projecting
to the center. Thus a full-root point with smaller center residue field
is not accidentally discarded.

If \(N_e\) counts points over \(\mathbb F_{q^e}\), the exact closed-point
counts are
\[
 c_1=N_1,\quad c_2=(N_2-N_1)/2,\quad
 c_3=(N_3-N_1)/3,\quad c_4=(N_4-N_2)/4.
\]
In particular the quartic count removes the entire quadratic subfield.
The raw cycle counts are
\(\binom{c_1+3}{4},\binom{c_1+1}{2}c_2,
\binom{c_2+1}{2},c_1c_3,c_4\).
Deduplicating their elliptic trace images loses no effective cycle.
All infinity, zero-coordinate and torsion charts use the already audited
proper normalized quotient maps.

The quartic finite-field modulus is verified by
\(X^{q^4}=X\bmod f\) and \(\gcd(f,X^{q^2}-X)=1\).
The complete multiplicative cycle, inverses and Frobenius fixed-subfield
counts are checked. At every extension degree the closed-point counts
recover the full point count, and the latter satisfies the genus-forty-nine
Hasse--Weil bound.

Properness of the relative symmetric power makes these necessary tests
valid even if coefficients of a putative rational family have poles at the
chosen specialization. The reduced divisor may become reducible or
nonreduced, which is why all five cycle types are retained.

**Exact reciprocity.** Summing the normalized map identities over a divisor
of degree \(M\) multiplies their constant torsion corrections by \(M\).
The displayed tuple transforms as
\[
 (u,k_U,k_V,k_C,k_D)\longmapsto
 (u,-k_V,-k_U,k_D,k_C),
\]
and the torsion mask transforms as
\((a,b,c,d)\mapsto(d,c+M,b+M,a)\).
For \(M=4\) this is \((d,c,b,a)\).
The extra torsion term of the reciprocal \(Z\)-generator is retained;
the parity equation in (U-QUARTIC-PRIMITIVE-TORSION) gives exactly its
required correction. Hence a genuine quartic state must survive each
filter together with its reciprocal.

The initial independently replayed stages are:

| Necessary test | Remaining primitive states |
|---|---:|
| Complete height and torsion box | 2,765,352 |
| \(q=17,m=2\) | 831,217 |
| \(q=19,m=2\) | 235,258 |
| \(q=23,m=2\) | 68,415 |
| \(q=29,m=2\) | 34,753 |
| Exact reciprocal closure | 13,219 |
| \(q=19,m=4\), with reciprocity | 12,115 |
| \(q=31,m=2\), with reciprocity | 4,799 |
| \(q=37,m=2\), with reciprocity | 2,947 |
| \(q=29,m=4\), with reciprocity | 2,263 |
| \(q=29,m=5\), with reciprocity | 2,263 |

All 1,307 primitive trace states of boundary quadruples survive. Boundary
membership here describes a trace state, not every divisor class above
it. Every surviving primitive state still has 32 rational Jacobian
preimages. Their effectiveness, possible moving pencils and individual
root conditions remain separate tests. In particular the zero displayed
trace does not by itself put a divisor in one of the ten excluded
halfcanonical pencils. Section 12.65 supplies a separate complete
classification sufficient to exclude all zero-trace quartic lifts.

The full implementation and exact data are in
root_quartic_sieve/full_quartic_cycles.py and quartic_trace_sieve.py,
with one complete trace certificate per prime and base. The independent
