### 14.6. Mathematical dependence and numerical dependence

The defining equivalences in Sections 1–4 do not depend on any finite computation, conjectural rank formula, geometric non-density statement, or reported exclusion range. The minimum-dependent inequalities are proved symbolically. Section 13 imports the established minimum-entry exclusion with its variable correspondence. The finite local tables, genus computations by displayed discriminants, binary ranks, and polynomial coefficient identities elsewhere have their explicit domains and witness rules in the text. Their numerical conclusions are computer-assisted wherever exhaustive finite arithmetic is required.

Applications of Faltings' theorem concern fixed curves after the stated parameter restrictions. Applications of finite-rank unit equations retain their fixed group or support. The uniform point-counting results do not supply a global height maximum. Selmer conditions impose local compatibility and rank upper bounds; they do not identify a rational lift. A derivative, resultant, or auxiliary cover yields a proper locus only after its nonvanishing or nondominance is proved on the actual integral surface.

Material adapted from the public Magic Squares of Squares research archive retains the attribution and CC BY 4.0 notice in reference [5]. Imported theorems are used only in the forms and under the hypotheses identified in their applications. Their citations do not import unrelated assertions from the same source.

### 14.7. Denominator, cubic-descent and quotient certificates

The exact denominator proof in Section 12.5 uses the twenty-four coefficient
rows of Section 12.2. Its finite domain comprises eight projective sign
columns, four retained-product choices and twenty-four forms. Every
partial substitution is tested as a polynomial identity; complementary
exponents and the phase correspondence are compared as linear functions
of the symbolic integers $e,a$. No finite exponent cutoff replaces that
comparison. Independent reconstruction verifies the same 768 identities.

The rational cubic descent in Section 9.51 enumerates all primitive
projective residues for each of the sixteen supported norm-square
classes at the exclusion moduli in its table. A first unit coordinate is
normalized to one; preceding coordinates range over all multiples of the
residue characteristic, including nonzero lifts. The full descent over
$L$ instead uses eighteen global bits, with no rational norm restriction.
Its local images are generated by the displayed actual local-point
witnesses and have the full theoretical dimensions. Independent field
arithmetic and dyadic labels give the same accumulated constraint ranks.
The quartic isomorphism and its inverse are polynomially checked before
specialization. These certificates establish the rank bounds, not a
finite-index Mordell–Weil basis or analytic point completeness.

For Section 12.6, the singular-locus exhaustion and degree argument are
geometric proofs. The finite algebra checks the ten Hessians, the two
generic ruling substitutions, removal of the fixed component, the cubic
transformations, and the invariant valuations at every singular
parameter, including infinity. An independent affine-chart calculation
gives the same models and discriminants. The explicit B section, its
nontorsion specialization, and the coupled symmetry identities are
checked exactly. The resulting exact generic ranks retain their
function-field domain.

For Section 12.7, two independent reconstructions verify all twelve
complementary-product identities against the twenty-four coefficient rows.
The exact finite checks include the odd square-root implication modulo 64,
the three possible integer residues, both binary quadratic forms at all
eight nonzero pairs over $\mathbb F_3$, and the polynomial identities in
the real and valuation arguments. The exclusion of all integer levels is
proved for arbitrary heights; it is not inferred from a bounded search.

For Section 12.8, the two quotient polynomial identities, the rational
progression normalization, the conjugate differential determinant, the

from the sample progression. The four-step obstruction uses every one of
the 4095 nontrivial even subsets of the thirteen branch lines and exact
rational ranks of their homogeneous evaluation matrices. Both independent

For Section 12.9, the twelve boundary substitutions, all sixteen product

of a product by the product of the reduced denominators.

For Section 12.10, independent checks verify the squareclass identities,
the permitted odd-prime parity vectors, and the labeled rule at 2.
The theorem follows uniformly from the allocation lemma and the four

For Section 12.11, independent polynomial reconstructions check the orbit
products, both A-orbit identities, the two B-orbit real envelopes, and
the exact residues. The full total norm has 91 monomials. All ninety
nonconstant terms satisfy the weighted 2-adic and 3-adic coefficient
bounds used in (Q-TOTAL-CONGRUENCE), agreeing with the shorter

specified triangle, not a sampled subset.

For Section 12.12, the 36 pairwise entry differences factor as displayed,
verifying the exact deleted divisor and split-torus correspondence.
Completeness of the reciprocity criterion uses [32] and the stated
torus pairing; no numerical computation of the full intersection is

For Section 12.13, independent exact verification checks the four offset
relations, the signed Gaussian factorizations and equal-norm conjugacy

or finite-height search supplies its uniformity, and the resulting

For Section 9.53, exact field arithmetic verifies the point and all three
factor squares. Independent quadratic characters at two good primes above
29 give binary rank four. Section 9.54 additionally has independent exact
doubling and differential certificates. Its all-orders coefficient estimate,

For Sections 12.14–12.15, independent symbolic certificates verify all six
boundary resultants, their norm-one nonvanishing, local monomial bounds,
and the repeated-row circuits. An exhaustive exact rational-rank check of

For Section 9.56, two independently reconstructed local-descent certificates give exact rank one for each elliptic factor. The finite-height calculation uses whole polynomial balls and complete projective duplication orbits to prove zero tails. Separate rational-doubling and Fermat-quotient arithmetic verifies all 11-adic leading constants. The displayed coefficient bounds prove convergence and uniqueness on entire disks, and the two reflected equations exhaust every possible residue class. The theorem concerns simultaneous six-radical lifts, including both real intervals outside $(0,24)$, not every point on one genus-two quotient. Section 9.57 has a separate complete rank-zero, torsion and omitted-chart certificate.

For Sections 12.18–12.19, exact integral matrices verify the torsion overlattice, its discriminant form and the complete Galois action. The cohomology calculation uses integral cocycles, not only rational characters. Independent projective enumeration covers every point at 7 and 13; the gradient and unit Hessian calculation proves good reduction. The Brauer bound uses its actual quotient Tate lattice at 2 and 3 and separately treats the primes equal to a counting characteristic. The normalized quaternion presentation and every necessary valuation class are exhaustive; the two rational middle-component residues eliminate all rational two-primary classes. A separate exact dual-lattice calculation, equivariant discriminant gluing, and the complete mod-three Frobenius/conjugation calculation eliminate the remaining primary part. The resulting vanishing concerns the proper product K3 only. Section 12.20 retains both projective local charts and gives complete closed rules at every prime by unbounded valuation comparisons, independently checked against a terminating local decision procedure; its conic obstructions are generic-section statements.

For Sections 12.21–12.24, separate certificates verify the fixed division-curve ranks, Kummer independence, signed-energy valuation identities, finite two-twist gcd argument and every quotient map. The eight elliptic rank upper bounds include a complete global squareclass list over the two class-number-one cubic fields, all denominator primes, and all primitive dyadic projective charts. A second implementation enumerates complete residue arrays independently of the first lifting procedure. Matching nonidentity points and square-character matrices give exact ranks; no analytic rank or full saturation assumption is used. The offset K3 singular-locus ideals, four residue charts, inverse-map boundary coefficients and norm identity are also exact. The theorem about unramified quaternion pullbacks is restricted to its displayed constant-corrected family.

For Sections 12.25–12.27, local minimal charts establish the actual component incidences before the lattice matrices are formed. The torsor-lattice input is [42] with geometric multisection index two; the bisection discriminant-exponent argument selects the offset lattice without assuming a full gluing basis. The intrinsic Brauer argument uses the quotient Tate lattice and global Kummer lifts of actual arithmetic classes. The center-curve proof has independent complete local Selmer images, rational torsion bounds, exact birational maps, a whole-disk formal-domain check and an all-orders logarithmic coefficient bound. Every projective rational point is included; neither a bounded point search nor a finite series truncation supplies completeness.

For Section 12.28, exact degree-ten projective coordinates and the forward elliptic chart identify the section before its center is factored. The homogeneous denominator factor is retained. The three resultants restrict one primitive cubic factor to two signed squareclasses; the conic parameter gcd gives exactly four genus-two twists. The two new cubic descents cover every supported squareclass, and all 512 dyadic root residues are tested with independent field arithmetic. The valuation bound proves that this finite residue test covers whole rational disks. Section symmetries supply only the explicitly stated orbit; arbitrary multiples and specialized higher-rank points remain outside that theorem.

For Sections 12.29–12.30, the split-quadric chart has an explicit rational inverse, and every omitted chart is proved degenerate for a full-root point. The degree-four map has the full two-torsion translation kernel. Minimal charts supply the section heights before the discriminant formula proves saturation. The five-square root identities are exact, including the global inverse Pythagorean parameters. The new center-curve proof exhausts the supported cubic Kummer classes in the discriminant-$-44$ field; two independent dyadic arguments exclude the nontrivial unit. Exact good-reduction counts and the five-term group-law cycle determine the elliptic quotient, and every projective pullback chart is included. The uniform old-cubic limitation uses a smooth degree-four quadric intersection and a degree-eight divisor; it is not inferred from finitely many multiples.

For Sections 12.31–12.34, the five-radical chart has a birational inverse on the normalized root surface and covers every admissible point after choosing positive roots. Every branch discriminant, resultant and exceptional rational parameter is certified exactly. The 128 degenerate points are exhausted by the full-root identities and the four-square-progression theorem, including all infinity charts. The character maps retain constants and their differential eigenspaces prove the isogenies. Five good specializations certify the nontorsion boundary sections without assuming saturation. The universal-basechange proof supplies simultaneous smooth resolutions at 5 and 7, full Frobenius component characters, two independent implementations of every finite-field count, and the exact divisor-field and Artin–Tate hypotheses. Arithmetic group equality is proved separately from rank equality. The specialized Kummer proof uses a complete fixed rank-zero curve, explicit quartic maps with their missing charts, and the actual local torsion group at 3; it claims only finite odd index at rank-one specializations.

For Section 12.35, the center factorization is verified as a function-field identity with its scalar and removable origins fixed exactly. The section-height formula and the eight separate bad-fiber charts determine intersection degrees for every integer, not only computed multiples. The weighted Betti theorem is applied to its actual local intersection indices. At the four multiplicative fibers of type $I_4$ the indices are one; at the four of type $I_2$ they are zero. Their total saturates the theorem and proves transversality at every good torsion intersection. The two independent parity arguments include the complex beta roots, all real bad fibers, and infinity before the exact genera are stated. The generic full-root point count uses the saturated arithmetic group and every inverse chart. It is explicitly a function-field statement.

For Sections 12.36–12.37, the specialized rank proof uses actual rational isogeny images with the factor of four retained. Six fixed genus-two covers and two signed quartics are exhausted by exact rank-zero elliptic descents, with all finite and infinity charts checked. The natural second quotient is explicitly identified with the dual isogenous model, preserving constants. The geometric center theorem applies the weighted tangency formula to the full rank-two Mordell–Weil lattice and every torsion translate. Exact squarefree tests and an independent modular branch-count calculation exhaust both the square-center and genus-zero candidate lists. Four unramified Kummer valuation rows and the anti-invariant torsion calculation prove exact geometric saturation on the beta cover. The final geometric point count includes the product sign determining the fixed base, every exceptional chart, and every labeled radical sign. None of these function-field statements is substituted for a point classification on specialized rational fibers.

For Sections 12.38–12.41, the full two-Kummer calculation retains all three coordinates, including torsion limiting values. Uniform independence includes the two scalar-degenerate conics; the reciprocal-point relation is an exact identity. Geometric connectedness of the four-root covers is proved by a rational-evaluation descent lemma and independent root-sign changes, not by treating rational constants as geometric obstructions. At the test fiber both ranks are certified by complete actual images and exhaustive primitive local congruences. The four-prime sieve enumerates the entire smooth reductions and includes the infinity chart; independent implementations give the same sixteen surviving patterns. The arbitrary-cover degree bound tracks all ramification, minimal coordinates at infinity, even gamma-fiber components and odd-alpha pole restrictions. Its coefficient is an infinite-degree theorem, not a sample of maps. The next quadratic-cover group statement enumerates all possible old Kummer kernels and proves that none has a rational base curve. It uses rank equality only where explicitly stated.

For Sections 12.42–12.44, all constant twist classes are retained. The arithmetic rank arguments use a Galois-equivariant divisor injection and good reduction; the geometric rank argument uses Artin–Tate only under a hypothetical maximal Picard rank that itself supplies the Tate hypothesis. Independent finite-field presentations reproduce every required count. The graph exclusion accounts for every sign direction, all projective fixed loci and quadratic residue fields, but does not classify a curve mapping birationally to its image. The specialized cover isomorphisms include actual rational square multipliers. Genus-two lower bounds keep the even-degree diagonal quotient and need no fake-descent injectivity. Genus-three exact ranks use exhaustive local primitive charts and actual lower-image witnesses. Their numerical quadratic-Chabauty inequality does not evaluate the remaining analytic set.

For Sections 12.45–12.46, the quadratic descent retains actual root traces in one field, with signed elliptic addition and complete exceptional charts. The auxiliary center group includes a primitive half-generator, exact torsion and a proved Kummer coset. The auxiliary-prime argument separately proves saturation at thirteen and includes all projective and nonintegral charts. The fixed-fiber theorem supplies no uniform conclusion at other rational bases.

Sections 12.47–12.49 retain three distinctions essential to their scope. The quadratic trace quartics are identified with a fixed elliptic curve by direct inverse maps, with an actual rational scaling and no omitted twist. Their 432-case domain follows from the exact primitive group and a function-field height inequality; every nonsquare witness is regular, and the four exceptions have exact split discriminants. Torsion and equal-abscissa charts use the actual no-new-halves condition before applying the old-center theorem. The uniform genus-three rank proofs use injective specialization only on a completely bounded squareclass support, including constants. Their primitive generators have independently checked local components. Sections 12.50–12.51 prove saturation and trace bounds in arbitrary rational-cover degree. The odd-prime proof imports only the two explicit Legendre vanishing-cycle matrices from [51]. The normal degree-eight base cover, finite monodromy image, affine orbit alternatives, local divisibility at all fourteen bad fibers and exact Riemann–Hurwitz genera are supplied in full. The prime-two argument uses the previously certified entire geometric group, including torsion, and an individual nontrivial positive-genus Kummer subfield. Arithmetic descent preserves the constant field. The cubic degree bounds use trace orthogonality over every embedding, the actual central root for parity, and the completed saturation theorem for strict positivity. The genus-two center-only quotient retains a projective line of effective cubic divisors per divisor class, so its two trace coordinates do not themselves give a finite effective-divisor enumeration.

Sections 12.52–12.54 distinguish character maps of degree eight from primitive elliptic quotients of degree two. The norm-only limitation uses complete Jacobian generation, including the three additional torsion classes, and invariant square roots in every quotient field. Section 12.55 distinguishes specialized arithmetic from generic section heights. Sections 12.57–12.58 distinguish geometric uniqueness from arithmetic enumeration. Sections 12.59–12.60 retain two different scopes. Doyle and Bjorn Poonen.** “Gonality of dynatomic curves and strong uniform boundedness of preperiodic points.” [Primary author manuscript](https://math.mit.edu/~poonen/papers/dyn_gonality.pdf), dated December 30, 2018. **Use:** Proposition 3.2, printed page 5, states the Castelnuovo–Severi inequality for two curve subfields whose compositum is the full function field. Section 12.57 checks this compositum hypothesis using each prime quadratic extension, and proves the radical-tower gonality formula directly. No dynamical uniform-boundedness conclusion is imported.

Section 12.62 verifies zero trace separately for the full Jacobian over the finitely generated regular extension $\mathbb C(m)/\mathbb C$.

Section 12.62 constructs its proper paired-branch local models explicitly before using this implication; the negative sign comes from the separately tracked quadratic twist.

Section 12.71 checks every relevant squarefree root-difference divisor at m=5 using an independent complete squareclass-support test. The auxiliary rank and lattice calculations are separately proved here. The theorem was checked directly in the primary PDF.

The separate elliptic bound on printed page150 is not substituted for the general-genus statement. The displayed theorem locations were checked in the primary PDF.

### Additional references and theorem locators

The external inputs below retain the hypotheses stated in their applications. The numbered entries above record the principal sources.

- [Bruin–Thomas–Várilly-Alvarado, arXiv:1912.08908](https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.08908): surface geometry and symmetric differentials.
- [Caro–Garcia-Fritz, *Linear x-coordinate relations of triples on elliptic curves*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.17592): exceptional translates and uniform counting for fixed elliptic curves.
- [Voutier–Yabuta, primitive divisors on $y^2=x^3+ax$](https://arxiv.org/abs/1009.0872): the even-multiple input to the doubled-point rank obstruction.
- [Dujella–Janfada–Salami, Section 3](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/journals/JIS/VOL12/Janfada/janfada3.pdf): Monsky's matrices and parity; [Fisher](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s40993-022-00376-z): the Cassels–Tate pairing; [Bruin–Hemenway](https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/83557): the prime-class class-number condition.
- [Smith, *$2^\infty$-Selmer groups, $2$-class groups, and Goldfeld's conjecture*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.02325): density input; [Evertse–Schlickewei–Schmidt](https://arxiv.org/abs/math/0409604): the finite-rank unit-equation bound, including the explicitly nondegenerate six-coordinate application (U-MIN-SUPPORT) and all-height radical count (U-MIN-RADICAL).
- [Zarhin, *Division by 2 on odd degree hyperelliptic curves and their jacobians*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1809.03061): the halving and torsion restrictions; [Balakrishnan–Dogra](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.00388): the quadratic-Chabauty criterion.
- [Mumford, *Prym varieties I*](https://www.dam.brown.edu/people/mumford/alg_geom/papers/1974a--PrymVar-I-NC.pdf): the Prym framework used for the step double covers.
- [Auel–Singer, arXiv:2609.09351](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.09351): surface topology and invariants.

- [Hast, explicit genus-two two-cover descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/2009.10313); [Bruin–Doerksen, Richelot and split Jacobians](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.3480); [Yan, explicit Cassels–Tate pairings for Richelot isogenies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.08257).
- [Garcia-Fritz–Pasten, effective Mordell with automorphisms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.10443): the explicit gap inequality underlying the character averages.
- [Das–Saikia, prime and twice-prime congruent-number restrictions](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jpaa.2023.107335): the two additional published one-prime conditions.
- [van Bommel–Maistret–Shi–Sutherland, Pryms and local reduction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09512); [Borówka–Shatsila, genus-three involutions and Pryms](https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.07038): the commuting-involution model enters the degree-four exclusion, alongside the octahedral case.

- [Call–Silverman, *Canonical heights on varieties with morphisms*](https://www.numdam.org/item/CM_1993__89_2_163_0.pdf), Theorem 3.1, and [Milne, *Jacobian Varieties*](https://www.jmilne.org/math/xnotes/JVs.pdf): uniform all-point height comparison and canonical polarization identities.
- [Shisong Xu, explicit Cassels matrices, v2](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.03238v2): the matrix input (22m); only its descent matrices are imported.
- [Bruin–Flynn, towers of two-covers](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/flynn/arts/art20.pdf); [Bruin–Stoll, two-cover descent](https://arxiv.org/abs/0803.2052); [Fisher–Yan, genus-two Cassels–Tate pairing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2306.06011); [Harpaz, second descent on Kummer varieties](https://www.math.univ-paris13.fr/~harpaz/Kummer_second_descent.pdf): the last theorem's nondegeneracy hypothesis fails for the specified class under the hypothesis specified in that source.
- [de la Bretèche--Tenenbaum, *Remarks on the Selberg--Delange method*](https://arxiv.org/abs/2010.12929), Theorem 2.1: the analytic summation input in (U-GH); the applicable multiplicative function, Euler product and constant are displayed above.
- [Salberger, *Counting rational points on projective varieties*, Proc. London Math. Soc. 126 (2023), 1092--1133](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms.12508), Theorems 0.9(b) and 1.17: the surface-cover and uniform curve-count inputs in (U-COUNT). The bounded-degree rigidity and admissible-locus deductions are proved here, rather than attributed to that paper.
- [Güntürkün--Hochster, *The Eisenbud--Green--Harris conjecture for defect two quadratic ideals*](https://arxiv.org/abs/1812.07539), Theorem 4.1: the full five-quadric case used in (U-RIG).
